author: nayer-kotry
body:
## Summary

- Adds `reasoning_effort` parameter to `CompletionArguments`, typed directly from the OpenAI SDK's `ReasoningEffort` type (`none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`)
- Adds `supports_reasoning_effort: bool = False` field to `OpenAIChatModel` so each model declares this capability in its YAML config, defaulting to `false`
- Adds `supports_temperature: bool = True` field to `OpenAIChatModel`. The previous string-match heuristic that skipped `temperature` for GPT-5 / o-series models has been removed; each model now declares explicitly whether it accepts `temperature`
- In `chat()`, `reasoning_effort` is only forwarded when the model declares `supports_reasoning_effort: true` and the pipeline passes a value; `temperature` is dropped when the model declares `supports_temperature: false`. A debug log fires when `reasoning_effort` is passed to a non-supporting model, including the model id and a concrete fix hint
- Adds GPT-5.4 as an example entry in `llm_config.example.yml` with `supports_temperature: false` and `supports_reasoning_effort: true`
- Adds unit tests for the gating logic in `tests/test_openai_chat_reasoning_effort.py`

## ⚠️ Migration required (breaking change for deployments)

The name-based heuristic that used to detect reasoning models and skip `temperature` (matching `gpt-5*`, `o1*`, `o3*`, `o4*`, `gpt-o*`) has been **removed**. Each model now declares its API surface explicitly via two booleans:

- `supports_temperature: bool = True` — set `false` on reasoning models that reject the `temperature` parameter
- `supports_reasoning_effort: bool = False` — set `true` on models that accept the `reasoning_effort` parameter

**Every reasoning model in every deployed `llm_config.yml` must declare `supports_temperature: false`.** If a deployment is missed, `temperature` is forwarded to the model and the API rejects the request.

### Deployment status

- [x] `/opt/pyris/llm_config.yml` on **pyris-prod.artemis.cit.tum.de** — flags applied, backup at `/opt/pyris/llm_config.yml.bak.<timestamp>`, not yet restarted (will be picked up by the post-merge image deploy)
- [x] `/opt/pyris/llm_config.yml` on **pyris-test.artemis.cit.tum.de** — flags applied, backup retained, `pyris-app` restarted; LangFuse, Uvicorn, Weaviate all came up cleanly
- [ ] **Local developer `llm_config.yml` files** — each developer must add `supports_temperature: false` to their reasoning-model entries

Applied to both servers on the three GPT-5 chat entries (`gpt-5-mini`, `gpt-5-nano`, `gpt-5.4`):

```yaml
supports_temperature: false
supports_reasoning_effort: true
```

Non-reasoning chat models (`gpt-4.1-mini`, `gpt-oss-120b`, `gemma-3-4b-it`) keep the defaults — no flags needed.

See the in-tree migration note at the top of [`iris/llm_config.example.yml`](iris/llm_config.example.yml) for the canonical reference.

## How to use

In any pipeline, pass `reasoning_effort` via `CompletionArguments`:

```python
# Disable reasoning entirely (GPT-5.4+)
CompletionArguments(reasoning_effort="none")

# Use medium reasoning
CompletionArguments(reasoning_effort="medium")

# Don't touch it (default, all existing pipelines unchanged)
CompletionArguments(temperature=0.3)
```

In the model's YAML config, opt in:

```yaml
- id: gpt-5.4
  type: azure_chat
  model: gpt-5.4
  supports_temperature: false
  supports_reasoning_effort: true
  ...
```

## Test plan

- [x] Unit tests cover: `reasoning_effort` dropped when model doesn't support it; not forwarded when unset even if model supports it; forwarded when both true; `temperature` dropped when `supports_temperature: false`; `temperature` forwarded by default; debug log fires with the helpful hint
- [x] pyris-test config-only restart confirms the existing (pre-merge) code silently ignores the new fields — no startup regression
- [ ] Post-merge: verify an Iris chat against `gpt-5-mini` or `gpt-5.4` on pyris-test still returns 200 (no 400 from temperature)
- [ ] Post-merge: verify all valid effort levels (`none`, `minimal`, `low`, `medium`, `high`, `xhigh`) are accepted by `CompletionArguments` against a live Azure GPT-5.4 deployment

author: learhy
body:
## Summary

Re-implementation of the Approval Matrix (Bundle 2.5) on current `main`. Replaces the stub always-approve evaluator with the real deterministic evaluator from the spec pseudocode. PR #14 was closed as stale (7 bundles behind, 8 merge conflicts).

## Changes

### Core: `studio/orchestrator/approval.py` (new)
- **`matrix_lookup(complexity, risk)`** — 3×3 matrix: bands low/med/high × low/med/high → `AUTO`, `AUTO_NOTIFY`, `SUMMARY`, `FULL_REVIEW`, `FULL_REVIEW_COOLDOWN`
- **`evaluate_approval_matrix(proposal, findings, triggers, ...)`** — full deterministic evaluator per spec pseudocode:
  1. Mandatory-review triggers override the matrix entirely
  2. Critical security findings → `FULL_REVIEW_COOLDOWN`
  3. Unresolved medium+ security → `FULL_REVIEW`
  4. Sensitive tags (auth, billing, secrets, pii) → `FULL_REVIEW`
  5. Score-driven tier from the 3×3 matrix
  6. Bundler self-escalation (escalate only, never de-escalate)
  7. Auto-ship eligibility resolution
- **`MandatoryReviewTrigger`** — configurable trigger with `matches(proposal, tags)` supporting: `target_new_repo`, `tag_matches`, `path_patterns`, `min_files_deleted`
- **`CooldownError`** — typed exception with `bundle_id` + `cooldown_until`
- **`cooldown_seconds()`** — reversible (1h default) vs irreversible (24h default)

### `studio/orchestrator/models.py`
- **`ApprovalSettings`** model with band thresholds, cooldown durations, summary timeout, mandatory review triggers list
- Added `approval: ApprovalSettings` field to `Settings`
- Added `irreversible: bool`, `tags: list[str]`, `self_escalation_tier: str | None` to `BundleProposal`

### `studio/orchestrator/db.py`
- Migration v4: adds `irreversible INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0`, `cooldown_until INTEGER`, `tags TEXT` columns to `bundles`
- Updated `SCHEMA_SQL` for new databases

### `studio/orchestrator/state_machine.py`
- Cooldown enforcement in `transition_4_approve_from_review`: checks `cooldown_until` column, raises `CooldownError` if still in cooldown

### `studio/orchestrator/main.py`
- Replaced stub `_evaluate_approval_matrix` with the real evaluator
- Tier-based surface behavior:
  - `AUTO` / `AUTO_NOTIFY`: auto-approves (fires transition 4)
  - `SUMMARY` / `FULL_REVIEW`: notifies PM, waits for explicit decision
  - `FULL_REVIEW_COOLDOWN`: sets `cooldown_until`, waits for decision

### `settings.json`
- Added `approval` section with band thresholds, cooldown config, and 5 built-in mandatory-review triggers

### Tests
- **27 new tests** (`test_approval.py`): all 9 matrix cells, 4 boundary tests, security gate overrides, mandatory triggers, sensitive tags, self-escalation, cooldown durations, CooldownError, trigger matching, settings defaults
- Updated existing review test to match real evaluator behavior

author: majabri
body:
## UAT P2 — resume consent double-fire

**Reporter:** Amir, manual UAT 2026-05-10

> on career os i clicked build profile → took me to career profile. i clicked update resume to upload, i got the consent popup → I clicked understand → got popup to select resume → I select the resume that i want to upload → the consent popup showup again → i klicked understand it gave me to select my resume again. something is looping in this function.

### Root cause

The hidden `<input type="file">` was rendered as a **child** of the drop-zone `<div>`, whose `onClick={() => requestUpload()}` triggers the consent modal. The interaction loop:

1. User clicks drop-zone → `onClick` → `requestUpload()` → consent opens.
2. User clicks `I Understand` → `onResumeConsentAccept` → `fileInputRef.current?.click()`.
3. The programmatic `.click()` on the input fires a synthetic click event that **bubbles up through the DOM** and hits the parent drop-zone's `onClick` → `requestUpload()` runs **again** → consent re-opens.
4. User clicks Understand a second time → another `.click()` → file picker opens. They never see step 3 visually because the file picker has already been queued, but the modal flashed back up after picking the file.

The synthetic-event bubble from a programmatic `.click()` on a nested element through to a parent's React `onClick` is a textbook DOM pitfall; React doesn't suppress it.

### Fix

Move the `<input type="file">` so it is a **sibling** of the drop-zone div, not a child. The input is `className="hidden"`, so visual layout is unchanged. The programmatic `.click()` no longer has a parent `onClick` to bubble into.

### Files touched

| File | Drop-zone for |
|---|---|
| `src/app/(app)/mycareer/profile/page.tsx` | Career Profile → Import from Resume |
| `src/app/(app)/resumeadvisor/page.tsx` | Resume Advisor → Upload tab |

Both pages had the same bug and got the same restructure.

### Manual verification (post-deploy)

1. `/mycareer/profile` → click the drop-zone (or anywhere in it).
2. **Expect:** consent popup appears **once**.
3. Click `I Understand`.
4. **Expect:** file picker opens. Select a file.
5. **Expect:** file uploads + parses. **No second consent popup.**
6. Repeat on `/resumeadvisor` → Upload tab.

### Tests

No test changes — neither the consent component nor the upload handlers have rendered-DOM coverage. `src/app/actions/__tests__/consentActions.test.ts` covers the server action that records the audit row; that path is unaffected (one `consent_records` row will still be written per successful upload now — same behaviour, just no longer double-prompted on the way there).

### Out of scope

- The "consent on every upload" policy itself is intentional (one audit row per upload — see comment in `ResumeUploadConsent.tsx`). Not changing that.
- Drag-and-drop flow (`handleDrop` → `requestUpload(file)`) was always single-fire because the consent's accept callback uses the `pendingDroppedFile` branch and never calls `.click()`. Untouched.

Squash-merge OK once CI is green.

## Thinking Path

> - Paperclip is moving from demo-ready local development toward a deployable product instance.
> - The repository already has a production-oriented Dockerfile used by the existing quickstart flow.
> - The BBA Memory path needs persistent process data and a persistent Playwright browser profile across container restarts.
> - Operators also need Docker-level health feedback rather than only app logs.
> - This pull request adds production compose wiring around the existing image and adds health checks to the container contract.
> - The benefit is a clearer single-service production deployment path without changing application behavior.

- Added `HEALTHCHECK` to the root `Dockerfile` using the existing `/api/health` endpoint.

## Summary

- Closes user UX feedback during v0.23.0 dogfood: *"we just shown ◼ 3b DAG wave dispatch (multi-repo) in conductor progress, it is too little, i want at least show each trooper's task. maybe it can further list out, captain rex on dag part xxx, commander cody on dag part xxx"*
- Drops the single rolled-up `3b DAG wave dispatch (multi-repo)` row from `commands/deploy.md` upfront task table
- At Step 3b entry, after `dag-waves.txt` is parsed and `WAVE_GROUPS` is computed, fires one `TaskCreate` per `(wave, repo)` tuple with subject `3b.<step> <Rank> <Cmdr> on <repo> [wave <w>]` and activeForm `<Rank> <Cmdr> implementing <repo>`
- Each sub-row flips `in_progress` on dispatch rc=0, `completed` on `TS=ok` wave-wait notification — so the conductor display surfaces a spinner per in-flight trooper
- New `cw_cmdr_rank` helper (canonical Star Wars ranks: rex → Captain, cody/bly/wolffe → Commander, hunter → Sergeant, etc.) appended to existing `lib/commanders.sh`
- UX-only change: dispatch / wave-wait / fix-loop mechanics byte-equal v0.23.0; single-repo deploy + `/clone-wars:consult` byte-equal v0.23.0

## Visual effect (mock from this session)

For a 3-sub-repo multi-repo deploy with Wave 1 (auth-svc + data-plane parallel), Wave 2 (api-gw):

```
✓ 0    Audit + routing detect [yoda]
✓ 3a   Preflight pane allocation (multi-repo) [yoda]
◼ 3b.1 Captain Rex on auth-svc [wave 1]      ← spinner: Captain Rex implementing auth-svc
◼ 3b.2 Commander Bly on data-plane [wave 1]  ← spinner: Commander Bly implementing data-plane
○ 3b.3 Commander Cody on api-gw [wave 2]
○ 3c   Final verification (multi-repo) [yoda]
○ 3d   Fix-loop (multi-repo) [yoda+troopers]
○ 4    Teardown + archive [yoda]
```

Two spinners run concurrently (one per in-flight trooper), each naming its rank/commander/sub-repo. When wave 1 finishes both 3b.1 + 3b.2 flip to ✓ and 3b.3 starts.

## Stage 1/2 failure handling

- **Stage 1 retry-once:** in-flight repos remain `in_progress` across the retry — work IS in progress, just on attempt #2.
- **Stage 2 partial-success "Proceed degraded":** dropped repos flip to `completed` with description note `skipped per user choice` so no orphan spinner remains.

## Tests

- New: `tests/test_v0_23_1_static_wiring.sh` — 6 invariants (cw_cmdr_rank lookup behavior, upfront table omits 3b, Step 3b sources commanders.sh + has TaskCreate directive with canonical patterns, REPO_TO_TASK_ID + ≥2 TaskUpdate references, plugin.json semver-shape)
- All 6 v0.23.1 invariants pass; v0.23.0 + v0.22.0 + v0.21.0 + v0.20.x static-wiring tests still green
- Suite baseline matches v0.23.0 PR notes: 3 pre-existing failures (test_consult_load_prompt_migration, test_consult_spawn_rollback, test_deploy_provider_flag) + 1 known intermittent flake (test_consult_targets_forces_escalation; same flake exists on main — not introduced by this branch)

- [ ] Once Step 3b begins, sub-rows appear with rank prefixes — `Captain Rex on <repo>`, `Commander Cody on <repo>`, etc.
- [ ] Wave numbers in the `[wave <w>]` suffix match `dag-waves.txt`
- [ ] Wave 1 sub-rows flip to ✓ before wave 2 sub-rows start
- [ ] Stage 2 partial-success "skipped per user choice" path doesn't leave an orphan spinner

author: randroid88
body:
Damage was being computed as baseDamage * relativeSpeed * impactComponent,
which is essentially quadratic in closing speed. Any clean hit at near-top
speed clamped to MAX_HIT_DAMAGE (80) and erased a 100 HP sedan in 1-2 hits.

Switch to a linear-in-impact-speed model with a lower per-hit clamp, raise
each vehicle's health, and widen the stat spread so the four vehicles play
to clear roles:

  Sedan      200 HP, 14 dmg, mid mass    (balanced all-rounder)
  School Bus 400 HP, 16 dmg, heaviest    (rolling tank)
  Big Truck  320 HP, 24 dmg, heavy       (heaviest hitter)
  Racecar    130 HP, 12 dmg, lightest    (glass cannon)

Also normalize the AI's wounded-target preference by maxHealth so it works
across vehicles with very different HP pools, and bump the leaderboard
anti-cheat floor to track the new worst-case time-to-win.

body:
## Resumo

Refatora a operação de **Alimentação** para que tudo fique visível em **1 tela sem scroll**, eliminando duplicações entre Home e Scan e deixando a janela ativa sempre clara para o operador.

## O que mudou

- **`AlimentacaoScanPage`** (`src/pages/pwa/alimentacao/AlimentacaoScanPage.tsx`) — reescrita do layout, mantendo toda a lógica existente:
  - Bloco da janela ativa com dot pulsante e status colorido (`ATIVA` / `ENCERRADA` / `AGUARDANDO`), clicável → abre `JanelaSheet`.
  - 4 KPIs em grid: `JANELA` · `HOJE` · `OK` · `ERRO`.
  - Botão de scan dinâmico que **desabilita visualmente** quando a janela não está ativa (rótulo `🔒 Janela não disponível`).
  - **Câmera embutida** (200px) na própria página — não sai mais para fullscreen na tela operacional principal.
  - Busca sempre visível (nome / CPF / código de voucher) com resultados imediatos.
  - Ações rápidas: link para `Lista consumos` e toggle compacto de `Modo contínuo`.
  - Linha de status de sync (online/offline) com tag de versão.

- **`QrCodeScanner`** (`src/components/pwa/QrCodeScanner.tsx`) — novo prop `variant="inline"` que renderiza só o viewfinder (sem header tactical, sem footer com fallback manual). O modo `fullscreen` padrão segue intacto para os demais módulos (transporte, alojamento, credenciamento).

- **`JanelaSheet`** (`src/components/pwa/alimentacao/JanelaSheet.tsx`, novo) — bottom sheet com a lista de janelas do dia, status pill por janela, `Check` na selecionada. Substitui o dropdown de 2 cliques por 1 toque.

- **`AlimentacaoHomePage`** (`src/pages/pwa/alimentacao/AlimentacaoHomePage.tsx`) — agora apenas redireciona para `/pwa/alimentacao/scan`. Mantém compatibilidade com o `homeTo` do `PwaLayout` e com links externos.

## O que foi preservado

- Lógica completa: `registerMealConsumption`, `handleScan`, `handleManualPick`, `evaluateMealEligibility`, `recordIncident`.
- Pipelines offline: `addToOfflineQueue`, `addToVoucherQueue`, `enqueueIncident`, `tryRedeemVoucher`.
- Bottom nav do `PwaLayout` — não foi tocado.
- Modo fullscreen do `QrCodeScanner` — segue padrão para os outros módulos.
- Cache de janelas do dia (`mealWindowsCache`) e realtime de `meal_consumptions`.

## Test plan

- [ ] Acessar `/pwa/alimentacao` → deve redirecionar para `/pwa/alimentacao/scan`.
- [ ] Verificar que o bloco "Janela ativa" mostra `ATIVA` em verde com dot pulsante quando a janela atual está aberta.
- [ ] Tocar no bloco da janela ativa → BottomSheet abre listando todas as janelas do dia com status correto.
- [ ] Selecionar outra janela no sheet → o bloco principal e os KPIs atualizam.
- [ ] Quando a janela não está ativa (encerrada/futura), o botão de scan deve aparecer travado e desabilitado.
- [ ] Tocar em "Escanear QR Code" com janela ativa → câmera abre embutida (h-48), botão `✕ Fechar` no canto superior direito.
- [ ] Escanear um QR válido → registra consumo, KPIs `JANELA` / `HOJE` / `OK` incrementam; em `Modo contínuo` ligado, câmera reabre após o delay.
- [ ] Escanear um QR inválido → KPI `ERRO` incrementa, exibe feedback no card de resultado.
- [ ] Buscar por nome/CPF e selecionar um participante → registra consumo manualmente.
- [ ] Modo offline (DevTools → Offline): scan/busca continuam funcionando e enfileiram; banner de sync vira "Offline · dados em fila".
- [ ] Verificar que tudo cabe na viewport mobile sem scroll (testar em 375×667 e 390×844).

## Summary

- **「完整季原則」**：當季必須三個月都齊備（最新月份為 3 / 6 / 9 / 12）才算數，否則回退到上一個完整季
- **月 / 季切換**：卡片、表格、矩陣、管制圖全面套用；季模式下顯示「最近完整季」的值與標籤
- **count 單位（事件數）改用季加總**：HA10-01 異常事件通報件數從 46.33（=139/3 月平均）改為 87（三月加總）
- **PPTX 匯出微調**：HA10-04 急性一般病床開放率隱藏分子分母（床日數對讀者無意義）
- **同步到 qip-portable**（隔壁專案）：所有新功能完整移植 + DataTable 補上分子分母顯示

## What changed

### 共用 util（\`lib/aggregation.ts\`）
- \`lastCompleteQuarter(year, month)\` — 找出最近一個資料齊備的季
- \`previousQuarter(year, quarter)\` — 跨年安全的上一季
- \`latestQuarterlyValue()\` — 卡片 / 表格在季模式下用的代表值 + 標籤
- \`aggregateToQuarterly()\` — 加上完整季過濾；\`count\` 單位改用月加總

### 套用範圍
| 位置 | 變更 |
|---|---|
| \`app/cross-campus/page.tsx\` | 標題與比較對象皆改用「最近完整季」 |
| \`components/cross-campus/CrossCampusTable.tsx\` | \`quarterRange\` 改用 \`lastCompleteQuarter\`；\`quarterRatio\` 對 \`count\` 改加總 |
| \`lib/export/buildQuarterlyScorecard.ts\` | PPTX 匯出同步使用完整季；\`count\` 改加總 |
| \`components/dashboard/IndicatorCard.tsx\` | 季模式下顯示 \`latestQuarterlyValue\` 的值與 \`yyyy.QN\` 標籤 |
| \`components/dashboard/TableView.tsx\` | 表頭依模式切換「最新值」/「最近完整季」；含 N/D 副標 |
| \`app/page.tsx\` | \`PeriodToggle\` 在三種檢視模式都顯示（原本僅 heatmap） |
| \`components/export/QuarterlyScorecardSlide.tsx\` | \`HIDE_NUM_DEN_CODES\` 抑制特定指標的 (N/D) 顯示 |

### qip-portable 同步（另一個 repo / 專案資料夾）
- \`lib/aggregation.ts\` 整檔覆蓋
- \`components/dashboard/IndicatorCard.tsx\` \`TableView.tsx\` 手動編輯（保留 portable 的 \`?code=\` query string 路由）
- \`components/cross-campus/CrossCampusTable.tsx\` 同上
- \`app/cross-campus/page.tsx\` 加入 ExportScorecardButton + 完整季資訊
- \`lib/export/\` 與 \`components/export/\` 三檔複製貼上
- \`components/detail/DataTable.tsx\` 補上分子分母副標（dashboard 早有，portable 漏了）

## Verification

- **TypeScript**：dashboard 與 portable 均 0 個型別錯誤（pre-existing 的 \`IndicatorRow.tsx\` 無關）
- **單元驗證**：\`lastCompleteQuarter\` 邊界條件全通過
  - 1/2 月 → 去年 Q4；3-5 月 → 當年 Q1；6-8 月 → Q2；9-11 月 → Q3；12 月 → Q4
- **瀏覽器驗證**（dashboard）：
  - 季模式下卡片 \`2.79% (115.03)\` → \`2.56% (115.Q1)\`（值與 cross-campus 一致）
  - 事件數類指標確認改為加總（87、1、1、25）
- **靜態打包**（portable）：\`STATIC_EXPORT=true npm run build\` 通過，13/13 頁全部 prerendered

## Why

1. 使用者反映季度分析有時把單月資料當成下一季的代表值（例如最新月份是 4 月，卻被當成 Q2）
2. 卡片 / 表格只能看月值，缺少季視角
3. 事件數類指標（暴力事件、職災等）的「季度發生次數」應該是加總，而不是月平均
4. 床日數的分子分母對 PPT 讀者無意義，反而干擾閱讀

## Test plan

- [ ] 季度分析頁顯示「最近完整季」（在 4 月匯入後檢查標題仍為 Q1）
- [ ] 卡片切到「季」模式，數值與 cross-campus 一致
- [ ] 表格切到「季」模式，表頭變「最近完整季」，每列顯示 \`X.XX% YYY.QN\`
- [ ] PPTX 匯出三院區皆使用最近完整季
- [ ] HA10-01/02/03 事件數類指標季模式顯示整數加總
- [ ] HA10-04 急性一般病床開放率 PPTX 不顯示 (床日 / 床日)
- [ ] Portable 版本同步以上所有行為，且完整數據表顯示分子分母

author: aburan28
body:
## Summary

Expose Envoy's mirror-request mutation surface on `HTTPMirrorPolicy` by adding two fields:

- **`authority`** — rewrites the Host (`:authority`) header on the mirrored request. Maps to Envoy's [`host_rewrite_literal`](https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/api-v3/config/route/v3/route_components.proto#envoy-v3-api-field-config-route-v3-routeaction-requestmirrorpolicy-host-rewrite-literal). When set, Envoy implicitly disables the default `-shadow` suffix append.
- **`headers`** — request header manipulation rules applied to the mirrored request. Maps to Envoy's [`request_headers_mutations`](https://www.envoyproxy.io/docs/envoy/latest/api-v3/config/route/v3/route_components.proto#envoy-v3-api-field-config-route-v3-routeaction-requestmirrorpolicy-request-headers-mutations). This uses `Headers.HeaderOperations` directly so mirror config exposes only request mutations (`set`, `add`, `remove`) and does not expose a meaningless response-mutation branch.

```proto
message HTTPMirrorPolicy {
  Destination destination = 1 [(google.api.field_behavior) = REQUIRED];
  Percent percentage = 2;
  string authority = 3;                     // NEW
  Headers.HeaderOperations headers = 4;     // NEW
}
```

## Motivation

Today, mirrored traffic always carries either the primary destination's Host header or that host with `-shadow` appended (toggled by the `DISABLE_SHADOW_HOST_SUFFIX` pilot env). That's restrictive in several real-world cases:

- **vhost-routed mirror targets.** Sending shadow traffic to a SaaS analytics endpoint or a different namespace where the target performs Host-based routing requires a specific authority, not the primary one.
- **Differentiating shadow traffic.** Adding markers like `x-shadow: true` so downstream systems can ignore mirror requests in metrics/billing.
- **Stripping internal headers.** Removing auth tokens or PII from mirror requests before they leave the trusted boundary.

Today users reach for `EnvoyFilter` patches for these — direct API support is cleaner and easier to validate.

`authority` mirrors the naming of the existing `HTTPRewrite.authority` field (which does the equivalent thing on the primary request), so the API stays internally consistent.

## Changes

- `networking/v1alpha3/virtual_service.proto`: added `authority` (string, fieldnum 3) and request-only `headers` (`Headers.HeaderOperations`, fieldnum 4) to `HTTPMirrorPolicy`.
- Regenerated `networking/v1alpha3/virtual_service.pb.go` with `protoc-gen-go v1.36.11`.
- Regenerated `networking/v1alpha3/virtual_service.pb.html` so API docs include the new fields.
- Regenerated `kubernetes/customresourcedefinitions.gen.yaml`; `mirrors[].headers` now exposes only `set`, `add`, and `remove` in all three VirtualService CRD versions.

## Notes for reviewers

The `v1`/`v1beta1` alias files re-export the `v1alpha3` type via `=` and need no change. Deepcopy delegates to `proto.Clone` and the JSON shim uses proto reflection, so both pick up the new fields automatically.

A companion change in `istio/istio` wires these through `TranslateRequestMirrorPolicy` (including a small `HeaderOperations` → Envoy `HeaderMutation` translator for the mirror case) and will be sent as a follow-up PR once this lands and a tagged `istio.io/api` is available.

## Test plan

- [x] `BUILD_WITH_CONTAINER=0 make gen-proto`
- [x] `buf lint`
- [x] `go test ./...`
- [x] `python3 scripts/validate_crds.py check_equal_schema --kinds VirtualService --versions v1,v1beta1,v1alpha3 --file kubernetes/customresourcedefinitions.gen.yaml`
- [x] `scripts/breaking.sh master`
- [x] `git diff --check`
- [ ] CI builds proto and regenerated artifacts cleanly after `/ok-to-test`

Note: `BUILD_WITH_CONTAINER=0 UPDATE_BRANCH=master make gen-check` cannot complete on this macOS host because `clean.sh` uses `shopt -s globstar`, which is unsupported by the system Bash 3.2. The generation, lint, CRD schema, breaking, and Go test steps above were run directly.

author: reaganbourne
body:
## Problem
Every page refresh wipes JS memory, so `bootstrapAuth` had to call `POST /auth/refresh` using the httpOnly cookie. The app is cross-origin (Vercel + Railway), and SameSite/CORS issues sometimes block that cookie → user sees themselves logged out.

## Fix
When we receive an access token (login, signup, or after a successful refresh), store it in `sessionStorage` with a **14-minute expiry** (1 min buffer before the 15-min JWT TTL).

On next page load, `hydrateAccessToken()` reads it back and sets the in-memory variable. `bootstrapAuth` then calls `/me` directly (no cookie needed) — skipping the cross-origin cookie round-trip entirely.

If sessionStorage is empty, blocked (private browsing), or the cached token is stale, it falls back to the original `/auth/refresh` cookie flow.

## Why sessionStorage (not localStorage)?
- Cleared when the tab closes — no long-lived sensitive data
- Survives page refreshes within the same tab (the exact scenario causing the bug)
- Opening a new tab falls back to the cookie flow (expected behaviour)

## Test plan
- [ ] Log in → refresh the page → still logged in ✓
- [ ] Log in → close and reopen tab → prompted to log in again (cookie flow) ✓
- [ ] Log out → clear sessionStorage → refresh → still logged out ✓
- [ ] Private browsing (sessionStorage blocked) → falls back to cookie refresh ✓

author: copilot
body:
Static audit of every SQL site in `modules/ranking.php`, `modules/account.php`, `modules/buy.php`, and `modules/widgets/*` against the schema embedded in `MuOnline_Bak` (Stock Season 3 Ep.1), checking: table/column existence gating, `COLLATE DATABASE_DEFAULT` on varchar JOINs, parameterized `db_*` usage, and `$config[char_*/guild_*/stat_*/cr_*/usd_*/wcoin_*/gr_*]` consistency.

## Schema ground truth (extracted from the bak)

- **Present:** `Character.{Name,AccountID,cLevel,Class,Resets,PkCount,PkLevel,Strength,Dexterity,Vitality,Energy,Leadership,Money,MapNumber,MapPosX,MapPosY,Quest,Inventory,MagicList,LeftTime,PkTime}`, `MEMB_INFO.{memb___id,memb__pwd,memb_name,memb_guid,ctl1_code}`, `MEMB_STAT.{memb___id,ConnectStat,ConnectTM,IP,ServerName}`, `Guild.{G_Name,G_Master,G_Score}`, `GuildMember.{Name,G_Name,G_Level}`, `AccountCharacter.{Id,GameID1..5}`, `warehouse`.
- **Absent (must be gated):** `Character.{MasterLevel,Reblock}`, `MEMB_INFO.{cash,usd,credits,IsVaultPin,VaultPin,AccountLevel,mail_addr,mail_chek,bloc_code,sno__numb,appl_days}`, `Guild.{G_Mark,G_Notice}`, tables `GameShopPoint`, `MEMB_CREDITS`, `VI_CURR_INFO`, `IGC_BanUser`, `WebDonateItems`, `WebDonateLog`, `WebVotePoints`, `PersonalShopItem`/`PsItem`/`MuPshopItem`.

## Findings

### 🔴 Bugs

- **`modules/buy.php` lines 54, 67 — `@@ROWCOUNT` read on a separate prepared statement.** `db_one("SELECT @@ROWCOUNT AS r")` runs in a fresh ODBC batch and does not see the prior `UPDATE`'s row count, so the `WHERE balance >= ?` overdraft guard is effectively bypassed: `$debited` is truthy whenever the UPDATE executes, even if zero rows matched. A logged-in user can trigger `WebDonateLog` inserts and a "purchase succeeded" flash without funds. Fix by combining into one batch (`UPDATE …; SELECT @@ROWCOUNT AS r` via `db_one()`) or using `OUTPUT`.
- **`modules/widgets/lastinf.php` line 9 — `MEMB_INFO.appl_days` does not exist in the stock bak.** Query will fail with `Invalid column name 'appl_days'`. Detect via `db_column_exists()` and fall back to `memb_guid DESC`, mirroring the `questtop.php` auto-detect pattern.

### 🟡 Hardcoded identifiers (violate the "all names from `$config`" rule)

- `modules/ranking.php:131` — `FROM MEMB_INFO` literal in the stats COUNT.
- `modules/widgets/qinfo.php:6` — `FROM MEMB_STAT WHERE ConnectStat = 1`; should use `$config[stat_table]` / `$config[stat_connect_col]`.
- `modules/widgets/questtop.php:19,21` — `Name`, `cLevel`, `Class` literals; should use `$config[char_name_col]` / `char_level_col` / `char_class_col`.
- `modules/widgets/lastinf.php:9` — `MEMB_INFO` literal (in addition to the `appl_days` bug above).

### 🟢 Clean

- `modules/account.php` — both `read_balance()` and the character query gate every optional column/table and parameterize `WHERE $char_account = ?`.
- `modules/widgets/strongest.php`, `modules/widgets/top5guild.php` — all identifiers from `$config`, MasterLevel gated, both varchar JOINs in `top5guild.php` use `COLLATE DATABASE_DEFAULT` on both sides.
- `modules/widgets/{lastinforum,top5items,baners}.php` — no SQL.

## Cross-cutting

| Rule | Result |
|---|---|
| Only `db_query/one/all/exec` (parameterized) | ✔ across all audited files; no raw `odbc_exec`, no user input concatenated into SQL |
| `COLLATE DATABASE_DEFAULT` on both sides of varchar JOINs | ✔ all 5 JOINs found (`ranking.php` ×3, `top5guild.php` ×2) |
| `db_column_exists()` / `db_table_exists()` for absent items | ✔ for `MasterLevel`, `cash/usd/credits/WCoin`, `WebDonateLog`, `WebVotePoints`, `Quest*`, `G_Mark/G_Notice` ❌ missing for `MEMB_INFO.appl_days` |
| `$config[…]`-driven identifiers | ✔ in `account.php`, `buy.php`, `ranking.php`, `strongest.php`, `top5guild.php`; ❌ partial in `qinfo.php`, `questtop.php`, `lastinf.php`, plus one literal in `ranking.php:131` |

## Suggested fix order

1. `buy.php` `@@ROWCOUNT` — silent money bug, ship first.
2. `lastinf.php` `appl_days` — guaranteed runtime error on stock bak.
3. Replace remaining hardcoded `MEMB_STAT` / `MEMB_INFO` / `Name` / `cLevel` / `Class` / `ConnectStat` literals with `db_ident($config[…])` lookups.

No SQL-injection vectors and no missing collation guards were found.

body:
## Summary
This PR enhances the dashboard analytics to aggregate data by talhão (field/plot) in addition to year and crop type. Previously, data was only grouped by year and culture, but now it's broken down further to show metrics per talhão, providing more granular insights into field-level productivity.

## Key Changes

- **Data Aggregation**: Modified `resumoAnoCultura` memo to group by `(ano, talhao, cultura)` instead of just `(ano, cultura)`, enabling field-level analytics

- **Chart Improvements**: Enhanced the line chart tooltip with custom formatting to clearly display talhão name, year, and productivity metrics
- **Chart Layout**: Fixed the line chart height to a consistent 280px and added a descriptive footer note about displaying the top 8 talhões
- **Database Queries**: Updated Supabase queries to fetch canonical talhão references, allowing the system to use parent talhão names when applicable
- **Type Definitions**: Updated `PlantioComDetalhes` type to include the canonical talhão relationship

## Implementation Details

- The aggregation key now includes talhão: `${p.ano}__${p.talhao}__${p.cultura}`
- Table row sorting now considers talhão name as a secondary sort criterion after year
- The custom tooltip in the line chart provides better readability with formatted output showing all relevant metrics
- Canonical talhão references allow the system to group related talhões under a parent identifier when needed

author: tummyslyunopened
body:
Replaces closed #13 with a cleaner approach: track the IDs of comments the bot itself creates (extracted from the URLs `gh` prints) and filter those IDs on the inbound side. No more pollution of comment bodies with a sentinel marker, no dependency on claude remembering to append it every time.

## How it works

**`claude-runner.ps1`** intercepts every `tool_result` event in the live stream and regex-scans the result text for GitHub comment URLs in either shape:

```
https://github.com/<o>/<r>/(issues|pull)/<n>#issuecomment-<id>      ← issue + PR conversation comments
https://github.com/<o>/<r>/pull/<n>#discussion_r<id>                ← PR review comments
```

Matched IDs are appended to `.data/outgoing-comments.jsonl` (gitignored) with their kind. Real-time recording: as soon as `gh issue comment` prints its URL, the ID is on disk — so the next monitor pass sees it, regardless of how long the worker takes to finish.

**`monitor.ps1`** at startup loads every recorded ID into two typed `HashSet[long]`s (issue-comments and pulls-comments use separate ID spaces in GitHub's API). The issue-comment loop and the PR-review-comment loop each consult their HashSet and skip matched comments, logging the skip for audit:

```
[config] comment 4416687006 skipped -- bot posted it (outgoing-id self-filter)
```

## Why this is better than the marker approach

| | Marker (closed #13) | ID tracking (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Reliability | depends on claude remembering | mechanical — captures every URL gh prints |
| Comment content | injects `<!-- cag-bot -->` everywhere | clean, unchanged |
| Failure mode if claude forgets | full loop returns | n/a — claude can't forget |
| Failure mode if gh changes output format | n/a | regex needs updating (very rare event) |

## Cold start

First run with no `.jsonl` file: empty sets, no crash. New bot comments from that point forward get tracked and filtered. Pre-existing bot comments in queue.json (all `status=done`) are unaffected by ID-based dedup.

## Files touched

- `claude-runner.ps1` — adds `Record-OutgoingCommentIds` helper, calls it from the `tool_result` block
- `monitor.ps1` — loads IDs at startup, filters both comment loops

author: phall1
body:
## Summary

Release prep for cyrs 0.1.0. No Rust source changes. No actual
`cargo publish` performed — the operator pushes that button.

- Bump `[workspace.package].version` 0.0.1 -> 0.1.0 plus the matching
  workspace internal-dep `version = "0.1.0"` pins.
- Validate the publishable set (19 crates) via `cargo package
  --workspace`. All pack + verify clean except `cyrs-py`, which
  cannot link without libpython at verify time (PyO3
  `extension-module`); manifest packs clean under `--no-verify`,
  and the production wheel is built by maturin in CI.
- Update `docs/release-playbook.md`: enumerate the 19 publishable
  crates explicitly, add a Local dry-run validation section
  documenting the workspace package recipe and the cyrs-py caveat,
  fix the binary-build callouts to reference the `cypher` /
  `cypher-lsp` / `cypher-agent` binary names from their `cyrs-*`
  source crates, and append `--no-verify` to the cyrs-py line in
  the manual fallback publish list.
- Pivot `CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased]` -> `[0.1.0] — 2026-05-10` with
  the honest framing the README already uses (openCypher 93.2 %
  TCK, GQL ISO 11.1 % bootstrap, three downstream surfaces are
  scaffolds, three binaries kept `cypher-*` names, rowan UB cy-208
  unresolved upstream).

## Dry-run results

`cargo package --workspace --allow-dirty --exclude cyrs-canary
--exclude xtask --exclude cyrs-testkit` packages all 19 publishable
crates: cyrs-syntax, cyrs-ast, cyrs-diag, cyrs-fmt, cyrs-hir,
cyrs-plan, cyrs-schema, cyrs-sema, cyrs-db, cyrs-project,
cyrs-lang-services, cyrs-agent, cyrs-cli, cyrs-ffi, cyrs-lang,
cyrs-lsp, cyrs-py, cyrs-tck, cyrs-wasm.

With verify (drop `--exclude cyrs-py`): 18 of 19 verify clean;
cyrs-py fails verify with `Undefined symbols for architecture
arm64: _PyUnicode_*` etc. — expected, libpython is unresolved at
verify time. Manifest is publishable; use `cargo publish -p
cyrs-py --no-verify` (or maturin in CI).

Note on `cargo publish --dry-run -p <crate>`: the per-crate
dry-run resolves dependencies against the *live* crates.io index,
so it fails with `no matching package named cyrs-syntax found` for
every non-leaf crate until cyrs-syntax is actually published. This
is a cargo limitation, not a publish blocker. The first real
`cargo publish` of each crate populates the index for the next.

## Rowan patch.crates-io

This branch is based on `main`, which does NOT carry a
`[patch.crates-io]` for rowan. cy-yrz (the rowan 0.15->0.16 bump)
is in flight on a separate branch and is NOT a 0.1.0 prerequisite.
The workspace pins `rowan = "0.15"` from crates.io directly. No
publish blocker from that direction.

If cy-yrz lands before 0.1.0 publishes and introduces a
`[patch.crates-io]`, note that `cargo publish` strips the patch
table cleanly (it's a workspace-level concern), so consumers of
the published cyrs crates resolve `rowan = "0.15"` (or whatever
the version pin is) from crates.io with no fork dependency
leaking through.

## Next step for the user

1. Review this PR and merge.
2. Tag `v0.1.0` on the merge commit.
3. Optional: re-run the local dry-run on the merged main.
4. Publish in dependency order (set `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN` first):
   ```sh
   cargo publish -p cyrs-syntax
   cargo publish -p cyrs-diag
   cargo publish -p cyrs-ast
   cargo publish -p cyrs-schema
   cargo publish -p cyrs-project
   cargo publish -p cyrs-hir
   cargo publish -p cyrs-sema
   cargo publish -p cyrs-plan
   cargo publish -p cyrs-fmt
   cargo publish -p cyrs-db
   cargo publish -p cyrs-lang-services
   cargo publish -p cyrs-wasm
   cargo publish -p cyrs-ffi
   cargo publish -p cyrs-py --no-verify   # PyO3 extension; see playbook
   cargo publish -p cyrs-tck
   cargo publish -p cyrs-lsp
   cargo publish -p cyrs-agent
   cargo publish -p cyrs-cli
   cargo publish -p cyrs-lang             # meta-crate last
   ```
   Each `cargo publish` blocks until crates.io indexes the new
   version; if you hit a transient "not found", wait 30 s and
   retry the same crate.
5. Build + attach binaries to the GitHub Release per
   `docs/release-playbook.md` §1.4.
6. Trigger `sign-release.yml` via `release:published` (automatic).

## Test plan

- [ ] `cargo check --workspace` passes (verified locally).
- [ ] `cargo package --workspace --allow-dirty --exclude
      cyrs-canary --exclude xtask --exclude cyrs-testkit` packs
      all 19 publishable crates (verified locally).
- [ ] `cargo package --workspace --allow-dirty --exclude
      cyrs-canary --exclude xtask --exclude cyrs-testkit
      --exclude cyrs-py` verifies 18 of 19 (verified locally).
- [ ] CI green on this PR.

author: troclaux
body:
## Summary

The `get_span_names` MCP tool passes the `span_kind` input directly to the storage layer without case normalization. Storage backends (Cassandra, Elasticsearch, etc.) store span kinds in lowercase (e.g. `server`, `client`). When an MCP client sends an uppercase value like `SERVER` or `CLIENT` — as the tool's own schema documentation suggests — the filter doesn't match anything and the tool returns an empty list.

**Fix:** call `strings.ToLower` on `input.SpanKind` before building the `OperationQueryParams`.

## Changes

- `get_span_names.go`: normalize `SpanKind` to lowercase before the storage query
- `get_span_names_test.go`: add `TestGetSpanNamesHandler_SpanKindCaseNormalization` that captures the query sent to storage and asserts the span kind is lowercased

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./cmd/jaeger/internal/extension/jaegermcp/internal/handlers/...` passes
- [x] New test `TestGetSpanNamesHandler_SpanKindCaseNormalization` verifies "SERVER" becomes "server" in the storage query

  matching regular Python behavior. Fixes `issue 2157`_.

- Fix: ``Collector.flush_data`` could fail with "RuntimeError: Set changed
  size during iteration" when a tracer in another thread added a line to the
  per-file set that ``add_lines`` (or ``add_arcs``) was iterating. The values
  passed to ``CoverageData`` are now snapshotted via ``dict.copy()`` and
  ``set.copy()``, which are atomic under the GIL. Thanks, `Alex Vandiver <pull
  2165_>`_.

- Fix: the soft keyword ``lazy`` is now bolded in HTML reports.

- We are no longer testing eventlet support. Eventlet started issuing stern
  deprecation warnings that break our tests. Our support code is still there.

.. _issue 1781: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1781
.. _issue 2157: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2157
.. _pull 2162: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2162
.. _pull 2165: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2165


.. _changes_7-13-5:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.13.5
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: `issue 2138`_ describes a memory leak that happened when repeatedly
  using the Coverage API with in-memory data. This is now fixed.

- Fix: the markdown-formatted coverage report didn't fully escape special
  characters in file paths (`issue 2141`_). This would be very unlikely to
  cause a problem, but now it's done properly, thanks to `Ellie Ayla
  <pull 2142_>`_.

- Fix: the C extension wouldn't build on VS2019, but now it does (`issue
  2145`_).

.. _issue 2138: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2138
.. _issue 2141: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2141
.. _pull 2142: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2142
.. _issue 2145: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2145


.. _changes_7-13-4:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.13.4
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: the third-party code fix in 7.13.3 required examining the parent
  directories where coverage was run. In the unusual situation that one of the
  parent directories is unreadable, a PermissionError would occur, as
  described in `issue 2129`_. This is now fixed.

- Fix: in test suites that change sys.path, coverage.py could fail with
  "RuntimeError: Set changed size during iteration" as described and fixed in
  `pull 2130`_. Thanks, Noah Fatsi.

- We now publish ppc64le wheels, thanks to `Pankhudi Jain <pull 2121_>`_.

.. _pull 2121: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2121
.. _issue 2129: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2129
.. _pull 2130: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2130


.. _changes_7-13-3:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.13.3
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: in some situations, third-party code was measured when it shouldn't have
  been, slowing down test execution. This happened with layered virtual
  environments such as uv sometimes makes. The problem is fixed, closing `issue
  2082`_. Now any directory on sys.path that is inside a virtualenv is
  considered third-party code.

.. _issue 2082: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2082


.. _changes_7-13-2:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.13.2
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Fix: when Python is installed via symlinks, for example with Homebrew, the
  standard library files could be incorrectly included in coverage reports.
  This is now fixed, closing `issue 2115`_.

- Fix: if a data file is created with no read permissions, the combine step
  would fail completely. Now a warning is issued and the file is skipped.
  Closes `issue 2117`_.

.. _issue 2115: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2115
.. _issue 2117: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2117


.. _changes_7-13-1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.13.1
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Added: the JSON report now includes a ``"start_line"`` key for function and
  class regions, indicating the first line of the region in the source. Closes
  `issue 2110`_.

- Added: The ``debug data`` command now takes file names as arguments on the
  command line, so you can inspect specific data files without needing to set
  the ``COVERAGE_FILE`` environment variable.

- Fix: the JSON report used to report module docstrings as executed lines,
  which no other report did, as described in `issue 2105`_. This is now fixed,
  thanks to Jianrong Zhao.

- Fix: coverage.py uses a more disciplined approach to detecting where
  third-party code is installed, and avoids measuring it. This shouldn't change
  any behavior. If you find that it does, please get in touch.

- Performance: data files that will be combined now record their hash as part
  of the file name. This lets us skip duplicate data more quickly, speeding the
  combining step.

- Docs: added a section explaining more about what is considered a missing
  branch and how it is reported: :ref:`branch_explain`, as requested in `issue
  1597`_. Thanks to `Ayisha Mohammed <pull 2092_>`_.

- Tests: the test suite misunderstood what core was being tested if
  ``COVERAGE_CORE`` wasn't set on 3.14+. This is now fixed, closing `issue
  2109`_.

.. _issue 1597: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1597
.. _pull 2092: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2092
.. _issue 2105: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2105
.. _issue 2109: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2109
.. _issue 2110: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/2110


.. _changes_7-13-0:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.13.0
   ```
   ---------------------------

- Feature: coverage.py now supports :file:`.coveragerc.toml` configuration
  files. These files use TOML syntax and take priority over
  :file:`pyproject.toml` but lower priority than :file:`.coveragerc` files.
  Closes `issue 1643`_ thanks to `Olena Yefymenko <pull 1952_>`_.

- Fix: we now include a permanent .pth file which is installed with the code,
  fixing `issue 2084`_.  In 7.12.1b1 this was done incorrectly: it didn't work
  when using the source wheel (``py3-none-any``).  This is now fixed. Thanks,
  `Henry Schreiner <pull 2100_>`_.

- Deprecated: when coverage.py is installed, it creates three command entry
  points: ``coverage``, ``coverage3``, and ``coverage-3.10`` (if installed for
  Python 3.10). The second and third of these are not needed and will
  eventually be removed. They still work for now, but print a message about
  their deprecation.

.. _issue 1643: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/issues/1643
.. _pull 1952: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/1952
.. _pull 2100: https://github.com/coveragepy/coveragepy/pull/2100


.. _changes_7-12-1b1:
   ```
   
  
  
   ### 7.12.1b1
   ```
   -----------------------------

- Fix: coverage.py now includes a permanent .pth file in the distribution which
  is installed with the code. This fixes `issue 2084`_: failure to patch for
  subprocess measurement when site-packages is not writable.

.. _issue 2084: https://github.com/coveragepy/co

body:
## Summary

Weekly Monday-09:00-KST intel cycle for 2026-05-05 → 2026-05-11. Combines machine-pipeline run (Phases A–D) with a curator pass per RFC-0003 §4. The curator pass overrides A5's auto-suppress (machine sources were 403-blocked by sandbox egress in this session) with 31 cited sources.

Three vendor-native realizations of AIDE patterns moved preview → public beta this week:

- **Anthropic Outcomes** — separate grader agent in its own independent context window, +10pp success on hardest tasks (+8.4% .docx, +10.1% .pptx). Vendor primitive form of A2 + A4 + P5.
- **Anthropic Multiagent Orchestration** — ≤20 specialists in parallel, shared filesystem, persistent events. Convergent with Gemini CLI Subagents and Codex MultiAgentV2.
- **Claude Code Routines + Auto Mode** — agents become repo-event-driven citizens (PR / push / issue / check_run / workflow_run / discussion / release / merge_queue / schedule / api triggers) under two-stage tool-output trust classification.

## What ships

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `evolution/intel/weekly-2026-05-11.md` | Curator-merged digest with 31 cited sources; explicit machine-source health note; dispatch overridden auto-suppress → YES with reasons |
| `research/en/2026-05-11-weekly-synthesis.md` | English synthesis layer per RFC-0003 §4 — three architectural claims; metadata-trigger discipline |
| `research/ko/2026-05-11-weekly-synthesis.md` | Korean mirror |
| `rfcs/0005-verifier-isolation-and-subagent-topology.md` | Draft RFC: names **Verifier Isolation** pattern, adds **Subagent Topology Mapping** sub-clause to P2 (1 feature dir → 1 specialist), adds **Event/Trigger Surface** to P10 with `events:` / `on:` / `trust_boundary:` / `gate:` schema |
| `rfcs/README.md` | RFC-0005 row added to index |
| `tasks/todo.md` | This week's plan + review summary + follow-ups for next cycle |

## What is intentionally NOT changed

- `docs/en/AIDE-METHODOLOGY.md` and Korean mirror — body changes require different-vendor reviewer co-sign per RFC-0003 §4.3.
- `principle-metadata.yaml` — RFC-0005 is **structural** (named patterns + schemas), not numeric. If the reviewer accepts the structural change, a follow-up RFC adds the metadata slots (e.g., `P5.verifier_isolation`, `P10.event_trigger_surface`).
- `axioms.yaml` — axioms are immutable per A1 / A4.

## Empirical exhibits this week

- **DeepClaude (HN #1, 606 pts, 17× cheaper)** — Claude Code agent loop swapped to DeepSeek V4 Pro via 4-line shell. Strongest exhibit yet for RFC-0004's cost-pressure + vendor-portability story.
- **Terminal-Bench 2.0 +13.3pp swing (GPT-5.5 82.7% vs Opus 4.7 69.4%)** — RFC-0004's P4-VC1 monitor caught it and correctly did **not** trip (Verified / SWE-bench Pro top-3 spreads remain inside 15pp threshold). Confirmation, not change.
- **OpenAI dropping SWE-bench Verified reporting** — methodology-level signal about benchmark source-tiering. N=1 today; logged as next-cycle deliberation candidate.

## Test plan

- [x] Machine pipeline runs (`fetch_vendor_releases.py`, `fetch_social_signals.py`, `fetch_benchmarks.py`, `compile_weekly_digest.py`) executed; A5 auto-suppress fired correctly on `source_health.all_failed=true`.
- [x] Curator override is documented in `dispatch.json` (gitignored — regenerated each CI run) and in the digest's "Source health" + "Dispatch decision" sections.
- [x] All 31 curator citations are anchored as markdown hyperlinks in the digest, en synthesis, ko synthesis, and RFC-0005 evidence section.
- [x] Bilingual contract: English and Korean synthesis notes are paired and cover the same three architectural claims.
- [x] RFC-0005 reviewer checklist is explicit and falsifiable (4 named decision points).
- [ ] Different-vendor reviewer (e.g., Codex / Gemini agent) acknowledges or rejects RFC-0005's reviewer checklist before any body / metadata change.

## Resumo

Fase 2 do P0-F. Companion do PR identity #38 (já mergeado) que fechou o gap AAL2 no DB layer das 7 RPCs caller-JWT.

Esta PR fecha o gap correspondente no Server Action layer · migra 16 actions do pattern `getCallerClaims + getCallerJwt` para o helper `requireSuperAdminAAL2()` (já existente do P0-D).

## Mudanças

**Actions migradas (16):**

- Owner-mgmt: `promote-to-admin`, `promote-to-owner`, `promote-user`, `demote-admin`, `demote-owner`, `demote-user`
- Membership: `grant-membership`, `revoke-membership` (belt-and-suspenders · DB também gateia via P0-A)
- Affiliate: `create-affiliate-invitation`, `revoke-affiliate-invitation`
- Org: `create-org-invitation`
- User mgmt: `invite-user`, `find-user-for-attribution`, `force-logout`, `reset-user-mfa`, `delete-user` (últimas 3 também são belt-and-suspenders · admin_delete_user e admin_reset_user_mfa checam `amr`)

**Tests:** 9 test files atualizados pra mockar `requireSuperAdminAAL2`. 406/406 testes verde.

## Arquitetura resultante

| Camada | Gate |
|---|---|

body:
## Summary

The built-in \`settings\` role bundled 4 tools (manageSource / manageSkills / manageAutomations / presentForm) behind a "Settings assistant" persona. The three \`manage*\` tools effectively just edit markdown / JSON files plus a refresh side-effect — so the role is replaced by a preset skill that drives the same files via plain Read/Write/Edit, with a PostToolUse hook handling the refresh automatically.

Closes #1283.

## Items to Confirm / Review

1. **Hook scope** — fires on Write/Edit of \`.claude/skills/<slug>/SKILL.md\` and \`config/scheduler/tasks.json\`. Sources are intentionally NOT in the pattern set because the news poller re-reads each cycle (eventual consistency, no refresh needed). Confirm this matches the actual reload behaviour you expect.
2. **No general-role expansion** — per the user's "general ロールも増やしたくない" constraint, the 3 manage* tools are NOT added to general. The skill drives the underlying files via Write/Edit (which every role has).
3. **`manage*` tools survive** — the MCP tools + REST routes still exist. Only the role-level bundle is deleted. Other roles can still opt into the direct-call path via \`availablePlugins\`.
4. **Hook coexistence** — wiki-history's PostToolUse hook (matcher Write|Edit) and ours (same matcher, different owner marker \`mulmoclaudeConfigRefresh\`) both land in \`<workspace>/.claude/settings.json\`'s PostToolUse array as independent entries. Test \`coexists with wiki-history hook\` locks this in.
5. **Settings UI implications** — there is no Settings → Roles tab today; role management lives at \`/roles\` (RolesView). Deleting the \`settings\` role doesn't touch that surface. Worth noting in release notes that the dedicated role is gone.

## User Prompt

> Settings という role があるよね。これを role じゃなくて skill にしたいの。
>
> general ロールも増やしたくない。skill だけで、うまくできない？manageSource、manageSkills、manageAutomations って結局 md ファイルを更新するだけだよね？
>
> [refresh approach A/B/C → C: PostToolUse hook auto-refresh]

## Implementation

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| \`server/workspace/skills-preset/mc-settings/SKILL.md\` | NEW — preset skill body. 3 workflows (sources / skills / automations), Write/Edit-driven. |
| \`server/workspace/config-refresh/hook.mjs\` | NEW — hook script. Filters file_path against 2 regex patterns, POSTs to refresh endpoint with bearer token. |
| \`server/workspace/config-refresh/provision.ts\` | NEW — boot-time auto-provision, mirrors \`wiki-history/provision.ts\`. Idempotent. |
| \`server/api/routes/config-refresh.ts\` | NEW — \`POST /api/config/refresh\` calls \`refreshScheduledSkills()\` + \`refreshUserTasks()\`. |
| \`server/index.ts\` | Wire up route mount + provision call. |
| \`src/config/apiRoutes.ts\` | Add \`config.refresh\` entry. |
| \`src/config/roles.ts\` | Delete \`settings\` from \`ROLES\` + \`BUILTIN_ROLE_IDS\`. |
| \`test/workspace/config-refresh/test_provision.ts\` | NEW — 5 cases: first install, idempotent, coexists with wiki-history, preserves user keys, recovers from corrupt settings.json. |

## Validation

- \`yarn typecheck\` ✅
- \`yarn lint\` ✅

body:
## Summary
Redesigned the India household segmentation overview page to present segments grouped by vulnerability level rather than raw segment codes, with a new interactive view toggle and improved visual hierarchy. The page now emphasizes the four vulnerability tiers (most/more/less/least vulnerable) while maintaining access to rural/urban and size-based views.

## Key Changes

- **Vulnerability-based grouping**: Replaced color-coded segment cards with a level-based metadata system (`LEVEL_META`) that maps segments to four vulnerability tiers with consistent visual styling (tag colors, chip colors)

- **Interactive view toggle**: Added `ViewByToggle` component allowing users to switch between three grouping modes:
  - Vulnerability level (default, groups R1/U1 as "least vulnerable", R4/U3 as "most vulnerable")
  - Urban/Rural band (original sector-based grouping)
  - Segment size (sorted by population share)

- **Redesigned segment display**: Replaced `SegmentCard` component with new `SegmentChip` component featuring:
  - Circular vulnerability indicator badges
  - Compact horizontal layout with percentage share
  - Improved accessibility with title attributes and aria-hidden decorative elements

- **Enhanced page structure**: Reorganized content into three clear sections:
  - Hero section with expanded description, metadata strip, and data source attribution
  - Population segments section with dynamic grouping based on view mode
  - "Dive deeper" section with three call-to-action cards linking to comparison, data browser, and map tools

- **Navigation integration**: Updated `OverviewView` to accept `onNavigate` callback and pass it to dive-deeper cards; modified `NavContext` type to support navigation between views

- **Improved metadata presentation**: Replaced KPI cards with a cleaner metadata grid showing data source, sample population, sample size, and geographic coverage

- **Removed components**: Deleted unused `Card` and `Kpi` imports; removed MPCE and per-state analysis sections

- **Minor formatting**: Changed percentage formatting from 1 decimal place to whole numbers (`toFixed(0)`)

## Implementation Details

The vulnerability level system uses a numeric tier (1–4) instead of direct color assignment, enabling consistent styling across rural and urban segments. The `sumShare` utility calculates total population share for arbitrary segment subsets, supporting dynamic group totals regardless of view mode. The page maintains responsive grid layouts and uses the existing `ui` theme system for consistency.

author: prashanthkrishnan91
body:
## Stage 2.0: Deploy Foundation v1

### Severity classification

**Level 2 — New durable architecture seam.** Backend-only, no visible behavior change, no SQL, no UI, no routes. Reclassified from Level 1 because this establishes the Stage 2 subsystem boundary (Deploy domain) — a new durable architecture seam that all future Deploy phases build on.

### Root architectural gap closed

Deploy had no domain boundary. Intel v3 decisions existed but there was no typed contract separating "Intel decides the action" from "Deploy scaffolds action plans." This PR creates that seam: a typed Deploy domain (`app/services/deploy/`) that reads Intel output read-only and emits scaffold-only planning artefacts with null dollar fields. Intel v3 remains the only Buy/Hold/Trim/Sell authority.

---

### Files changed

**New — Deploy domain (`v2/backend/app/services/deploy/`):**
- `__init__.py` — domain marker
- `deploy_contracts.py` — `DeployPlanInput`, `DeployPlanItem`, `DeployGuardrailSummary`, `DeployPlan`; enums `DeployPlanStatus`, `DeployActionabilityStatus`, `DeployActionSource`
- `deploy_intel_adapter.py` — reads Intel v3 snapshot `current_holdings` read-only; extracts evidence health flags; passes PriceBand as supporting context only (not decision authority)
- `deploy_translation_v1.py` — translates Intel decisions to scaffold candidates; HOLD → `NOT_ACTIONABLE_HOLD` always; THIN/stale/blocked evidence suppresses; all dollar fields null; PriceBand never drives actionability

**New — Tests:**
- `v2/backend/tests/test_deploy_foundation_v1.py` — 74 focused tests (all pass)

**Updated — Docs:**
- `docs/ai/HANDOFF.md` — Stage 2.0 entry; severity corrected; next step is Stage 2.1 Deploy sizing input contract
- `v2/progress_log.md` — current phase and next step updated

---

### Tests run and results

| Suite | Tests | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `test_deploy_foundation_v1.py` (new) | 74 | 74 passed / 0 failed |
| Intel v3 pure-python suite (`test_v3_decision_policy`, `test_intel_v3_snapshot`, `test_v3_data_truth`, `test_v3_evidence_quality_*`, `test_v3_intel_card_narrative_contract`, `test_v3_signal_hydration`) | 335 | 335 passed / 0 failed |
| Combined (Deploy + Intel v3 pure-python) | 409 | **409 passed / 0 failed** |

Intel v3 service/router tests (`test_intel_v3_read_only_adapter.py`, `test_intel_v3_router_service.py`) require the `supabase` package which is not installed in the local environment — pre-existing env limitation, not caused by this PR. Full 3,926-test suite passes in CI (established in prior PR).

---

### Supabase SQL required: NO
### UI changes: NO
### New routes: NO
### New providers / LLM / broker calls: NO
### Exact-dollar math added: NO
All dollar/quantity fields are null placeholders (`recommended_dollar_amount = None`, `estimated_share_quantity = None`, `rounding_policy = "not_applied_yet"`, `cash_constraint_status = "not_evaluated_yet"`, etc.).
### Intel visible decision behavior changed: NO

---

### Safety packs applied

- **Deterministic Decision Authority Pack** — Intel v3 is the only Buy/Hold/Trim/Sell authority. Deploy reads Intel output read-only and never derives new actions.
- **Backend-only Scaffold Pack** — No UI surface, no visible behavior change, no route, no flag flip needed.
- **Data Truth / Evidence Suppression Pack** — THIN/stale/blocked/weak evidence suppresses Deploy actionability; Deploy never fabricates evidence.
- **Test Tier Pack** — Tier 1 targeted contract bundle (74 new tests); pure-python Intel v3 regression bundle green.

### Build archetype: `capability-slice`

---

### Guardrail enforcement (in code and tests)

| Guardrail | Enforced in | Test |
|---|---|---|
| BUY candidate only when Intel action is BUY | `_classify_actionability` | `test_only_buy_intel_produces_buy_candidates` |
| TRIM candidate only when Intel action is TRIM | `_classify_actionability` | `test_only_trim_intel_produces_trim_candidates` |
| SELL candidate only when Intel action is SELL | `_classify_actionability` | `test_only_sell_intel_produces_sell_candidates` |
| HOLD → NOT_ACTIONABLE_HOLD always | `_classify_actionability` Rule 1 | `test_hold_cannot_become_actionable_candidate` |
| HOLD has no trade amounts | `_translate_item` | `test_hold_has_null_dollar_amount` |
| Dollar fields null in v1 | `_translate_item` | `test_guardrail_dollar_fields_null` |
| PriceBand not authority | `_classify_actionability` never reads `price_context_label` | `test_priceband_expensive_does_not_suppress_buy_candidate`, `test_priceband_cheap_does_not_override_hold` |
| Intel action preserved read-only | `DeployPlanItem.intel_action = inp.intel_action` | `test_guardrail_intel_action_preserved` |
| THIN evidence suppresses | `has_missing_evidence` flag | `test_thin_evidence_suppresses_buy_actionability` |
| Stale snapshot suppresses | `has_stale_evidence` flag | `test_stale_snapshot_suppresses_buy_actionability` |
| Blocked fit suppresses | `is_blocked` flag | `test_blocked_flag_suppresses_buy_actionability` |
| No intel_v2 / RecommendationService import | source-code inspection | `test_deploy_translation_does_not_import_recommendation_service` |
| No Intel v3 internals in contracts | source-code inspection | `test_deploy_contracts_have_no_intel_v3_imports` |

---

### Self-audit: acceptance criteria mapping

| Criterion | Files | Enforcement |
|---|---|---|
| Deploy Foundation v1 exists as clean backend-only domain seam | `app/services/deploy/` (4 files) | New module; no existing file modified |
| Intel remains the only Buy/Hold/Trim/Sell authority | `deploy_translation_v1.py` — only reads `inp.intel_action`, never recomputes it | Guardrail `intel_action_preserved` |
| Deploy consumes Intel read-only and emits scaffold only | `deploy_intel_adapter.py` reads snapshot dict; `DeployPlanItem.schema_version = "deploy_v1_scaffold"` | Source inspection test |
| No exact-dollar amounts calculated | `recommended_dollar_amount = None`, `estimated_share_quantity = None` in `_translate_item` | `test_guardrail_dollar_fields_null` |
| HOLD cannot become actionable | Rule 1 in `_classify_actionability` | `test_hold_cannot_become_actionable_candidate`, `test_guardrail_hold_never_actionable_true` |
| Weak/missing/stale/blocked suppresses actionability | Rules 2–5 in `_classify_actionability` | 8 suppression tests |
| PriceBand not decision authority | `_classify_actionability` never reads `price_context_label` | 5 PriceBand isolation tests |
| No route/UI/persistence/provider/LLM/broker | No imports of DB, routers, providers | Code review |
| 74 new tests pass | `test_deploy_foundation_v1.py` | CI / local run |
| Intel v3 pure-python tests pass | 335 Intel v3 tests | 409 combined pass |
| Docs updated compactly | `HANDOFF.md`, `progress_log.md` | Updated in this commit |

### Known limitations / intentionally deferred

- All exact-dollar fields are null — Stage 2.1 will first define the Deploy sizing input contract (authoritative cash, position value, portfolio value, target-allocation placeholders, minimum-trade/rounding policy placeholders, suppression behavior) before implementing dollar math.
- Cash/position/target-allocation inputs are not yet certified as authoritative inputs to the Deploy domain; that is the Stage 2.1 gate.
- No route exposing Deploy output — intentionally deferred per task scope.
- No persistence of Deploy plans — intentionally deferred.
- Tax lots, wash-sale, target allocation optimizer — all deferred to later stages.
- PriceBand available as `price_context_label` in `DeployPlanInput` for future supporting context; currently unused by the translation layer.

### Roadmap stage: Stage 2.0 (Deploy Foundation)
### Build queue item: Deploy action-plan foundation seam — complete

prepared action that waits for explicit human review before any authority
chain can proceed.

Chain:
  MSOExecutionProposal
  → AuthorityPreparationRequest       (authority review preparation)
  → ConfirmablePreparedAction         (waiting_for_human_confirmation)

## Summary
This PR converts the Prompt Registry widget from a static snapshot to a dynamic interface that fetches and displays prompt data from a live API backend. It also adds prompt management capabilities to the Prompt Studio application.

## Key Changes

**Registry Widget (`registry/interface/registry_widget.html`)**
- Replaced hardcoded static data with dynamic API fetching via `loadData()` function
- Updated all stat displays (total prompts, production count, eval coverage, avg cost) to calculate from live data
- Added error banner to display API connection failures
- Implemented proper HTML escaping via `esc()` helper to prevent XSS vulnerabilities
- Updated field mappings to match API schema (e.g., `cost` → `costPerRunUsd`, `tokens` → `tokensPromptBody`, `note` → `notes`)
- Added `showBody()` function to display prompt bodies in a new window
- Removed hardcoded action button alerts; now only shows "View body" button when body content exists
- Changed footer from "standalone snapshot" message to "Connected to Prompt Studio API"
- Made stats display "—" as loading state before data arrives

**API Module (`sandbox/js/api.js`)**
- Added four new prompt management functions:
  - `fetchPrompts()` - GET /prompts
  - `savePrompt()` - POST /prompts
  - `updatePrompt()` - PUT /prompts/{id}
  - `deletePrompt()` - DELETE /prompts/{id}

**Application (`sandbox/js/app.js`)**
- Imported new `exportToRegistryDraft` function from sessions module
- Added "Export draft…" button handler that converts current session to registry draft JSON format
- Downloads draft as a timestamped JSON file for later import into registry

**Server (`server.py`)**
- Added database initialization via `init_db()` function that loads schema from `schema.sql`
- Calls `init_db()` on startup to ensure database is properly set up
- Supports schema-driven database creation

## Implementation Details

- API base URL is configurable via `window.PROMPT_STUDIO_API_BASE` environment variable, defaults to `http://localhost:8000/api`
- Stats are recalculated dynamically whenever data loads via `updateStats()` function
- Filtering and sorting logic updated to handle null/undefined values gracefully
- Cost formatting helper `costStr()` handles both high-precision ($0.0001) and standard ($0.05) display
- Error handling displays user-friendly messages when API is unavailable

author: snichols
body:
Closes #31

## Goal

## Goal

Implement a **deferred command queue** so that mutations issued inside `DeferBegin`/`DeferEnd` blocks (or `Defer(fn)`) are buffered and applied in order when the outermost defer scope closes. This is the foundation for safe mutation during query iteration.

Master is at `97c2cbf` (Phase 5.2 just landed: multi-subscriber observers). The repo has a full ECS — storage, queries, pairs, ChildOf cascade, IsA inheritance, name lookup, hooks, observers — and all ECS mutations are currently **synchronous**: `Set`/`Remove`/`Delete`/`AddID` immediately apply, including hook/observer dispatch.

After this lands, users can:

```go
flecs.Each2[Position, Velocity](w, func(e flecs.ID, p *Position, v *Velocity) {
    if p.X < 0 {
        // Direct call would corrupt iteration. Defer instead.
        flecs.Delete(w, e)
    }
})

// Wrap iteration in Defer:
w.Defer(func() {
    flecs.Each1[Position](w, func(e flecs.ID, p *Position) {
        if p.X < 0 {
            flecs.Delete(w, e)  // queued
        }
    })
})  // queued deletes apply here, after iteration finishes
```

Manual control:

```go
w.DeferBegin()
flecs.Set[Position](w, e1, Position{1, 2})  // queued
flecs.Delete(w, e2)                          // queued
w.DeferEnd()                                  // applies in queue order
```

Nested:

```go
w.DeferBegin()           // depth = 1
w.DeferBegin()           // depth = 2
flecs.Set[Position](w, e, p)
w.DeferEnd()             // depth = 1, NO flush yet
w.DeferEnd()             // depth = 0, queue flushes now
```

### Scope explicitly EXCLUDES

- Per-goroutine staging (flecs C has multi-stage cmd queues for threading; Phase 7 territory).
- Suspend/Resume mid-defer.
- Transactional rollback.
- Deferred `RegisterComponent[T]` / `NewEntity` (these are always synchronous).
- Deferred reads (`Get[T]`/`Has[T]`/`Owns[T]` always see CURRENT state, not post-flush).
- Re-deferring while flushing (DeferBegin during flush is allowed — produces a fresh nested scope but won't re-defer the in-progress flush; document).
- Per-operation cancellation handles.
- Bounded queue sizes (queue grows as needed).
- Panic recovery during flush.

### Deliverables

1. **New file `defer.go`** in root `flecs` package.

2. **World fields (unexported, added to `world.go`):**
   - `deferDepth int` — nesting counter. Zero means "apply immediately."
   - `deferred []func(w *World)` — queue of buffered operations. Each closure re-invokes the immediate-apply path with captured arguments.

3. **Public methods on `*World`:**
   - `func (w *World) DeferBegin()` — increment `deferDepth`. Document: "Within a deferred block, Set/Remove/Delete/AddID/RemoveID/SetPair/SetName/RemoveName operations are queued and applied on DeferEnd. Reads (Get/Has/Owns/IsAlive) see CURRENT state, not the deferred future state."
   - `func (w *World) DeferEnd()` — decrement `deferDepth`. If now zero, FLUSH the queue (replay each closure in order) and clear it. If still non-zero (nested), no flush yet. **Panics** if `deferDepth` would become negative (mismatched calls).
   - `func (w *World) Defer(fn func())` — convenience: `w.DeferBegin(); fn(); w.DeferEnd()`. Even if `fn` panics, ensure DeferEnd runs (use `defer` keyword internally). Document: "Wraps fn in DeferBegin/DeferEnd. Recommended over manual Begin/End for matched-pair guarantee."
   - `func (w *World) IsDeferred() bool` — true iff `deferDepth > 0`.

4. **Refactor mutating operations to be defer-aware:**
   For each of `Set[T]`, `AddID`, `RemoveID`, `Remove[T]`, `Delete`, `SetPair[T]`, `SetName`, `RemoveName`:
   - Split into a **public wrapper** that checks `w.IsDeferred()` and either queues a closure or calls the immediate path, AND a **private immediate function** (e.g., `setImmediate[T]`, `addIDImmediate`, etc.) that does the actual work.
   - The closure captures the necessary arguments by value (entity ID, value of type T, raw IDs, etc.). For value types T, the closure captures T by value (a copy on the heap — accept this allocation cost).
   - When flushing, each closure is invoked with `w` (the world). The closure re-enters the immediate function. Hook/observer dispatch happens during flush, in queue order.

   **Operations to NOT defer (read-only or returns-a-value):**
   - `Get[T]`, `Has[T]`, `Owns[T]`, `HasID`, `OwnsID`, `IsAlive`, `Count` — read-only.
   - `RegisterComponent[T]` — synchronous (no point deferring registration).
   - `NewEntity` — synchronous (caller needs the ID NOW).
   - `Observe[T]` / `ObserveID` / `Unsubscribe` — observer manipulation synchronous.
   - `OnAdd[T]` / `OnSet[T]` / `OnRemove[T]` — hook registration synchronous.
   - `ChildOf` / `IsA` / `Name` accessors — read-only.
   - `LookupChild` / `Lookup` / `PathOf` / `GetName` — read-only.
   - `ParentOf` / `PrefabOf` / `EachChild` / `EachPrefab` — read-only.
   - `EachTableFor` / `TablesFor` — read-only.
   - All query-related: `NewQuery`, `Query.Iter`, `QueryIter.Next/Table/Count/Entities`, `Field[T]` — read-only.
   - `Each1/2/3/4` — iteration is read-only; the user's fn may queue mutations if Deferred.

5. **Flush semantics:**
   - The flush iterates the `deferred` slice in order, calling each closure.
   - **Critical**: during flush, `deferDepth` is 0 so closures don't re-defer themselves into the same queue. Closures call the immediate paths, which fire hooks and observers.
   - If a closure panics, the flush aborts. Remaining queued operations are lost. Document. (Phase 7 may add rollback; defer for now.)
   - **Re-deferring during flush:** if a closure calls `DeferBegin` (manually or via a hook/observer), a fresh nested defer scope starts. Queue allocates fresh entries. The new scope must DeferEnd before the outer flush continues. The simplest implementation: closures see `deferDepth == 0` at entry, so they apply immediately by default; if they explicitly call DeferBegin within their body, they enter a new defer scope which they must close themselves. Document the contract precisely.

6. **Hook/Observer interaction:**
   - When a deferred Set is flushed, OnSet fires (and OnAdd if applicable). Hooks and observers fire DURING flush, in flush order.
   - If a hook/observer calls a mutating operation while flushing (deferDepth == 0 at flush time), that operation applies IMMEDIATELY. This can cause subtle bugs if the user expected those nested mutations to also be deferred. The standard mitigation is "wrap your whole event-driven flow in a Defer block."
   - Document this behavior clearly with examples.

7. **Cascade Delete + Defer:**
   - When deferred Delete is flushed, the cascade still happens (ChildOf children are deleted as part of the single Delete operation). The cascade is internal to `Delete`, so it just runs at flush time.
   - If a CHILD of the deleted parent is also separately queued for Delete, the second Delete might find the entity already dead (cascaded). The current `Delete` returns false for dead entities — that path is already exercised. No special handling needed.

8. **Tests** in `defer_test.go`:
   - **Basic queue + flush:** `DeferBegin`; `Set[Position]`; verify `Has[Position] == false` (deferred, not yet applied); `DeferEnd`; verify `Has[Position] == true`.
   - **Get during defer sees old state:** entity has Position{1,2}; `DeferBegin`; `Set[Position](w, e, Position{99,99})`; `Get[Position](w, e)` returns `(Position{1,2}, true)`; `DeferEnd`; `Get` returns `(Position{99,99}, true)`.
   - **Order preserved:** queue 3 Sets with different values for the same entity; after flush, Get returns the LAST value.
   - **Multi-operation:** queue Set + Delete on different entities; both apply on flush.
   - **Nested DeferBegin:** `Begin; Begin; Set; End; verify still deferred; End; flushes.`
   - **Convenience `Defer(fn)`:** calls fn, flushes on return. Even if fn panics, flush attempts to run (verify via captured state).
   - **Mismatched DeferEnd panics:** `DeferEnd` without prior `DeferBegin` → panic.
   - **IsDeferred reports cor

author: richertunes
body:
## Summary
\`QobuzDownloadItem\` implements \`IDisposable\` (with proper \`Cancel\` + CTS disposal in its \`Dispose(true)\` path), but **three** removal paths cancelled the item via \`.Cancel()\` and then dropped the reference without ever calling \`Dispose()\`. Every download removal leaked one \`CancellationTokenSource\` until GC finalisation walked the unreachable object.

## Leak sites fixed
| File | Path | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| \`QobuzDownloadClient.cs\` | \`RemoveItem\` — \`_queueService.TryGetDownload\` branch | dispose \`downloadItem\` after queue removal |
| \`QobuzDownloadClient.cs\` | \`RemoveItem\` — internal-tracking branch (queue-service miss) | dispose \`activeItem\` after cancel |
| \`DownloadQueueService.cs\` | \`RemoveDownload\` — after file cleanup | dispose \`removedItem\` |
| \`DownloadQueueService.cs\` | \`CleanupCompletedDownloads\` — periodic sweep | dispose the removed entry |

## Why this matters
Under heavy library imports (hundreds of album removals — Lidarr cleans up completed downloads periodically), this manifested as gradual handle accumulation. The CTS's own finalizer eventually returns the handle, but only at GC-pressure-dependent latency.

## Safety
\`QobuzDownloadItem.Dispose\` is idempotent via its \`_disposed\` guard, so the defense-in-depth double-call between \`QobuzDownloadClient.RemoveItem\` and \`DownloadQueueService.RemoveDownload\` (both target the same instance because \`AddDownload\` stores the same reference) is safe.

## Audit trail
2026-05-10 defect-hunt audit; verified by reading the source (no false-positive issues here — the leak is clear from the IDisposable + missing-call pattern).

## Test plan
- [x] \`Qobuzarr.csproj\` builds clean (0 errors).
- [ ] CI: full build + tests.

author: buttbreaker
body:
### 💡 What:
Implemented request-level in-memory caching for the `Configuracion` model and reduced the external API timeout for exchange rate retrieval.

### 🎯 Why:
Global configuration keys, specifically the BCV exchange rate (`tasa_bcv`), are accessed in the global `header.php`, resulting in at least one database query (and potentially an external API call) on every single page load. This creates unnecessary overhead and makes the application vulnerable to slow external API responses.

### 📊 Impact:
- **Reduces DB Round-trips:** Eliminates redundant database queries for configuration keys within the same request. After the first call to `get('key')`, subsequent calls return immediately from memory.
- **Optimized Exchange Rate:** `getTasaBCV()` now only performs its expiration check and potential DB/API hit once per request.
- **Improved Resilience:** Reduced the `curl` timeout for the external BCV API from 10s to 3s, ensuring that if the API is slow, it doesn't hang the entire application boot process.

### 🔬 Measurement:
Verified using `tests/verify_config_optimization.php`.
- Before: Multiple `get()` calls triggered multiple DB queries.
- After: Multiple `get()` calls trigger exactly one DB query.
- Verified that `set()` updates the cache and returns correct success/failure status.
- Verified support for "negative caching" (caching null values) via `array_key_exists`.
