author: rjwalters
body:
## Summary

Phase 2F of Epic #2556 makes the escape router couple differential pairs at launch from dense packages. Today's `EscapeRouter` knows per-net trace widths but not pair partnerships -- adjacent diff-pair pads on BGA / QFN / USB-C get independent escapes that diverge, forcing the coupled pathfinder to recover spacing after escape. This PR threads a bidirectional `diff_pair_map` from the autorouter into `EscapeRouter` and adds a pre-pass that emits two coupled escape segments for any pad whose partner pad lives on the same package.

## Scope (per curator's three-dispatcher priority)

- **BGA** (`_escape_bga_rings`) -- paired pre-pass active
- **QFP/QFN/TQFP** (`_escape_qfp_alternating`) -- paired pre-pass active
- **MULTI_ROW_CONNECTOR / USB-C** (`_escape_multi_row_connector`) -- paired pre-pass active
- SSOP/TSSOP, SOP, radial -- fall through to single-ended for v1
- Cross-package coupling (pair partner on a different package) is intentionally out of scope -- the main pathfinder owns that case.

## Five-gate verification chain

Per the issue's #2587 dormant-signal lesson, every link in the wiring chain is exercised by a concrete assertion-able test (not just an inspection). 22 new tests in `tests/test_escape_diffpair.py`:

| Gate | Verification |
|---|---|
| **1: CLI → Autorouter map** | `Autorouter.get_diff_pair_map()` returns `{"USB_D+": "USB_D-", "USB_D-": "USB_D+"}` for paired nets, `{}` otherwise |
| **2: Autorouter → EscapeRouter ctor** | All three construction sites (`core.py:7271`, `orchestrator.py:563`, `orchestrator.py:1183`) thread the map |
| **3: ctor stores AND `generate_escapes` consults** | `EscapeRouter.diff_pair_map` stores the map; `diff_pair_segment_calls` counter bumps on `generate_escapes` |
| **4: Per-dispatcher reach** | BGA + QFN + USB-C fixtures each invoke `_escape_diff_pair_segment` once; negative cases (no relevant pair / partner off-package) keep the counter at zero |
| **5: Grid reservation** | Paired escape endpoints survive `apply_escape_routes` to the grid-mark call that feeds both Python and C++ A* search |

## Geometry verification

Synthetic USB-C fixture, pad pitch 0.5mm, `intra_pair_clearance=0.075mm`, `trace_width=0.2mm`:

```
Single-ended baseline:  USB_D+/USB_D- escape endpoints at 0.5000mm separation
Paired escape (Phase 2F): USB_D+/USB_D- escape endpoints at 0.2750mm separation
```

Target = `intra_pair_clearance + trace_width = 0.275mm`. Within +/-15% acceptance band specified in the issue.

## Cross-backend parity

`EscapeRouter` is Python-only and feeds grid reservations consumed identically by both backends. No C++ binding changes were required. Gate 5 verifies the paired escape segments are correctly handed to `RoutingGrid.mark_route` (the function both backends consult for cell occupancy).

## Curator-verified line numbers

| Architect cited | Verified actual | File |
|---|---|---|
| escape.py:697 (`__init__`) | line **715** | `escape.py` |
| escape.py:750 (`net_class_map` storage) | line **750** | same |
| escape.py:823 (`generate_escapes`) | line **823** | same |
| core.py:7117 (`_escape` property) | line **7271** | `core.py` |
| orchestrator.py:563 | line **563** | `orchestrator.py` |
| orchestrator.py:1183 | line **1183** | same |
| `cli/commands/route_cmd.py:3272` | line **3317** in `cli/route_cmd.py` | (cli/route_cmd.py path, not cli/commands/) |

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest tests/test_escape_diffpair.py` -- 22 new tests pass (the five-gate chain)
- [x] `pytest tests/test_escape*.py` -- 174 escape tests pass + 10 pre-existing skips
- [x] `pytest tests/test_diffpair*.py` -- 144 diffpair tests pass + 9 skips
- [x] `pytest tests/test_router_autorouter.py tests/test_router_core.py tests/test_routing_output.py` -- 257 routing tests pass
- [x] No new lint errors in modified files (`ruff check src/kicad_tools/router/{escape,core,orchestrator}.py`)

author: 0xgrizz
body:
## Summary

- Remove module-level `_SESSION` cache in `storage.py` so each `get_s3_client()` call creates a fresh `aiobotocore` session + client
- Bump `connect_timeout` 3s → 15s (was below R2's 99p connect latency under load, causing false-positive timeouts)
- Bump `retries.max_attempts` 2 → 3 with `mode=standard` (exponential backoff between attempts)

## Why

Today the validator hit recurring `botocore.exceptions.ConnectTimeoutError` on `_archive_window` uploads to R2 — even when R2 itself was fully healthy (verified via sync `boto3` from the same host returning in <0.3s, plus the bucket serving 422+ existing objects without issue).

The failure pattern was deterministic: after a clean process restart, the validator uploaded ~5-6 windows successfully, then every subsequent upload failed for the rest of the process lifetime. Only `docker restart reliquary-trainer` cleared it.

### Root cause

`storage.py:19` cached a single `aiobotocore` Session at module scope. aiobotocore Sessions own an internal HTTP connection pool. During a transient R2 slow spell, broken sockets accumulated in the pool. Every subsequent `create_client(...)` call returned a client wired to the same poisoned pool, so the validator silently lost the ability to upload for hours.

Today's incident: a load spike on R2 (from the `/api/miners` dashboard route hammering `GetObject` calls) triggered the initial pool poisoning around 23:17Z. The validator then failed to archive W418, W419, W420, W421 — 4 windows of audit data permanently lost. Manual restart at 02:31Z fixed it temporarily, but the pattern recurred within 30 minutes (W423, W424 also failed).

### Fix details

`get_s3_client()` now calls `aiobotocore.session.get_session()` on every invocation. Each upload gets a clean transport stack with no shared state. This mirrors the proven pattern in the miner-side `backfill_length_data.py` script, which uses sync `boto3` against the same endpoint and has had zero failures during the same windows the validator's cached-session client was timing out.

Cost: ~ms of session-allocation overhead per upload. At our upload volume (~15 files/hr) this is negligible.

## Test plan

- [ ] Merge → wait for `docker-image.yml` GH Action to build + push `:latest`
- [ ] Manually `docker pull ghcr.io/reliquadotai/reliquary-validator:latest` on validator host
- [ ] `docker stop reliquary-trainer && docker rm reliquary-trainer && docker run -d --name reliquary-trainer <flags> ghcr.io/reliquadotai/reliquary-validator:latest`
- [ ] Monitor `docker logs reliquary-trainer --since 30m | grep -E "Uploaded GRPO|window archive failed"` for 1+ hour
- [ ] Confirm: 12+ consecutive successful uploads (vs previous ~5 before pool poisoning)
- [ ] Confirm: `Uploaded GRPO dataset for window N` cadence matches seal cadence within ~30s

## Files touched

- `reliquary/infrastructure/storage.py` (+39 / -14)

This is **Layer 1** of a 3-layer R2 reliability fix. Follow-up PRs:
- Layer 2: switch `upload_window_dataset` to sync `boto3` in `asyncio.to_thread()` (avoids aiobotocore entirely on the hot path)
- Layer 3: non-blocking archive with persistent retry queue (never lose a window's audit data again)

author: artemiopadilla
body:
## Summary

PR #550 added the \`refresh-conservation-status\` cron schedule inside a \`DO \$\$ … \$\$\` block. Both the outer DO body AND the inner \`cron.schedule\` command literal use the default \`\$\$\` delimiter — so the SQL parser treats the inner \`\$\$SELECT net.http_post(...)\` opening as the close of the outer DO body, yielding "syntax error at or near SELECT" against the matching outer \`\$\$\` later in the file.

**Fix:** tag the outer block as \`\$do\$ … \$do\$\` and the inner command as \`\$cron\$ … \$cron\$\`. Same effective semantics; unambiguous parse.

author: artemiopadilla
body:
## Summary

PR #997 (v1.5 institutional endorsements + weekly validator lottery) introduced **two** \`CREATE TABLE\` statements that are missing their closing \`);\` before the next statement:

1. **\`public.institutions\`** (~line 12501-12510) — runs into the next \`CREATE TABLE public.institutional_affiliations\` as if the column list never ended. *(This is the bug that was actively breaking validate.)*
2. **\`public.weekly_validator_rewards\`** (~line 12586-12591) — same pattern: ends with \`UNIQUE(...)\` and runs straight into the next \`CREATE INDEX\`.

Postgres parses each as a single runaway statement until it hits an unexpected keyword 100+ lines later, then reports "syntax error at or near CREATE" against the wrong line.

**Fix:** add the missing \`);\\n\\n\` between each table's last column and the following statement. Two-line diff per table.

- [ ] Both tables now applied with the intended columns

author: rogervineeth-cloud
body:
Defence in depth: refuse the dev grant-test-plan endpoint when VERCEL_ENV='production' or NODE_ENV='production', regardless of the NEXT_PUBLIC_TEST_MODE flag.

Context: a manual smoke of /pricing today showed the TEST MODE banner and 'Grant test plan' buttons rendering in production, which would let any visitor self-grant a paid plan. The root cause is that NEXT_PUBLIC_TEST_MODE is currently set to 'true' in the Vercel production env. The immediate UI fix is to unset that env var in Vercel and redeploy.

This PR adds the second layer of safety: even if NEXT_PUBLIC_TEST_MODE=true gets set again by mistake, the server route will refuse to grant credits in production.

Note: I made this edit through the GitHub web editor, so the indentation may be slightly inconsistent. Please re-run prettier locally before merging if your CI doesn't auto-format.

body:
## Summary

This PR implements the `--language` parameter for the `/understand` command, allowing users to generate knowledge graph content in their preferred language.

Closes #141

---

## Changes

### Skill Definition (`SKILL.md`)
- Updated `argument-hint` to include `--language <lang>`
- Added `--language` documentation in Options section
- Added Phase 0 step 3.6 for language configuration:
  - Language code normalization (friendly names → ISO codes)
  - Config persistence in `.understand-anything/config.json`
  - `$LANGUAGE_DIRECTIVE` template for agent dispatch

### Agent Dispatch Modifications
Injected `$LANGUAGE_DIRECTIVE` into dispatch prompts for all content-generating phases:
- Phase 1 (SCAN) - project-scanner
- Phase 2 (ANALYZE) - file-analyzer
- Phase 4 (ARCHITECTURE) - architecture-analyzer
- Phase 5 (TOUR) - tour-builder

### Agent Definition Updates
Added language directive handling instructions in:
- `project-scanner.md` - affects `description` field
- `file-analyzer.md` - affects `summary`, `tags`, `languageNotes`
- `architecture-analyzer.md` - affects layer `name`, `description`
- `tour-builder.md` - affects `title`, `description`, `languageLesson`

### Locale Template Files
Created `locales/` directory with language-specific guidance:

| File | Language |
|------|----------|
| `en.md` | English (default) |
| `zh.md` | Chinese Simplified |
| `zh-TW.md` | Chinese Traditional |
| `ja.md` | Japanese |
| `ko.md` | Korean |

Each locale file provides guidance for:
- Tag naming conventions (localized vs English technical terms)
- Summary writing style
- Technical term handling (when to keep English)
- Layer name translations

---

## Usage Examples

```bash
# Generate in Chinese
/understand --language zh

# Generate in Japanese
/understand --language ja

# Combine with other options
/understand --language ko --full

# Use friendly name (auto-normalized to ISO code)
/understand --language chinese
```

---

## Testing

- All packages build successfully (`pnpm build`)
- No TypeScript compilation errors
- New locale files validated for syntax

---

## Implementation Notes

- **Config persistence**: Language preference is stored in `.understand-anything/config.json` for consistency across incremental updates
- **Fallback behavior**: If no `--language` specified, uses stored config or defaults to `en`
- **Locale injection**: If `$OUTPUT_LANGUAGE` is NOT `en`, locale guidance file is injected into architecture-analyzer prompt (Phase 4 step 4)
- **Technical terms**: Locale files recommend keeping certain terms in English (middleware, hook, barrel, ORM, REST API, etc.)

author: kim-em
body:
This PR removes ~50 lines of dead code in `SOS/Raw.lean` (`Raw.eval`, `naturalValuation`, and `Raw.eval_cast` — the last of which a doc comment called "the crucial reflection theorem" despite nothing depending on it) and fixes three categories of stale comments in `SOS/Search.lean`. No runtime behaviour changes.

The CSDP comment fixes:

- **Cost-matrix direction.** Two contradictory doc blocks in `Search.lean` — one said "CSDP minimises `tr(X)`", the other "Cost matrix: maximise `tr(X)`". The truth, per `LeanCsdp/Basic.lean:6` ("maximise tr(C · X)") and the CSDP user manual, is maximise. The LP-slack code at `buildSdpStrict` already relies on this: `+1` cost on the λ-block diagonal maximises λ, which is what `runStrict` reads back.

- **Off-diagonal halving.** The module-level doc claimed CSDP's `tr(A·X) = b` form "uses upper-triangle `A` with off-diagonal entries halved", but the code emits `value := ratToFloat c` directly. CSDP's `op_a` doubles off-diagonal sparse entries internally against symmetric `X`, so the code is correct as-is; only the doc was stale. Now matches the inline comment at the aTriple emission site.

- **Return-code label.** The filter `ret ∈ [0, 3]` was always correct, but the comment described `3` as "stuck at edge of primal feasibility". Per the CSDP user manual Table 13.1, `3` is "Problem solved to near optimality"; `5` is the stuck-at-primal-edge case. Comment updated to list the full code table.

Plus smaller comment fixes: documenting `runSearch`'s `.strict` arm as defensive (it's a public API, so kept as `return none` rather than `unreachable!`), adding a concrete output example to `monomialsUpTo`'s docstring, and tightening doc blocks on `fourSquaresNat`, `ParsedConcl`, `tryReify`, and `formatPoly`.

Verified by `lake test`.

## Summary

Closes #3774. Tiny follow-up to #3773: makes `MAX_SANE_DURATION_MS` a named export of `packages/protocol/src/schemas/server.ts` instead of a module-private constant, and imports it from the three boundary tests in `packages/protocol/tests/schemas.test.js`.

**Why it matters:** if the ceiling ever changes (e.g. dropped to 12h based on operational data), tests would silently keep passing — `MAX-passes / MAX+1-rejects` succeeds against any value as long as both the schema and the inline test constant move together. Inline drift = test no longer guards the actual boundary.

## Change

```diff
- const MAX_SANE_DURATION_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000
+ export const MAX_SANE_DURATION_MS = 24 * 60 * 60 * 1000
```

Three test sites now use `import { MAX_SANE_DURATION_MS: MAX }` instead of redeclaring it locally.

## Test plan

- [x] 119/119 protocol tests pass
- [x] `npm run build` regenerates `dist/schemas/server.{js,d.ts}` with the new export

author: magmueller
body:
## Summary

The agency operating doctrine had two homes that were drifting:

1. `agent/AGENCY.md` — in this repo, generic, 798 lines, the file the project CLAUDE.md instructs the agent to read on \"start agency\".
2. `~/.claude/skills/agency/SKILL.md` — on each box, off-git, 498 lines, personalized to Magnus (verbatim quotes, references to private-memory files). Only Claude Code saw it. Codex never did. A box rebuild would lose it.

This PR collapses them into one canonical doctrine:

- **`agent/AGENCY.md`** absorbs the skill's unique content: two-zone framing (internal vs visible boundary), anti-patterns to refuse, parallel sub-agent scan process (7 steps), synthesize-report template (🔥 FIRES / 📧 EMAIL / 💬 SLACK), compression bar (specific char limits), voice-for-drafts section, common-block-patterns table, variant-picker example, honor-access-gaps.
- Strips the remaining user-personal references (`@mamagnus00`, \"Magnus's box\", \"the look Magnus has on file\") so the doc reads as generic doctrine — the file was already mostly generic and just had a few leftover lines.
- **New `agent/agency-skill.md`** is a thin Claude Code skill stub that owns the trigger phrases (`start agency`, `scan everything`, `what's pending`, `triage my inbox/slack/github`, …) and points at `AGENCY.md`. ~12 lines, intentionally tiny.
- **`agent/bootstrap.sh`** symlinks the stub into `/home/bux/.claude/skills/agency/SKILL.md` on every install/update, so every box gets it without local drift.

Codex picks up the same doctrine via the existing `AGENTS.md → CLAUDE.md` symlink, which already instructs reading `AGENCY.md` on \"start agency\". Both CLIs now share one source of truth.

## Test plan

- [ ] Merge → `git -C /opt/bux/repo pull --ff-only origin main` → `sudo bash /opt/bux/repo/agent/bootstrap.sh`
- [ ] Confirm `/home/bux/.claude/skills/agency/SKILL.md` is a symlink to `/opt/bux/repo/agent/agency-skill.md`
- [ ] Confirm `readlink ~/.claude/skills/agency/SKILL.md` resolves to the repo file
- [ ] In a fresh Claude Code session, confirm `agency` skill still surfaces (look for it in the available-skills list) with the new trigger phrases
- [ ] Trigger \"start agency\" in a Telegram lane and confirm the agent reads `AGENCY.md` and runs the onboarding/scan flow as documented
- [ ] Codex lane: same \"start agency\" trigger picks up the doctrine via `AGENTS.md → CLAUDE.md → AGENCY.md` reference

author: pyramation
body:
## Summary

Replaces the inline `sha256()` and `putToPresignedUrl()` helpers in `graphql/server-test/__tests__/upload.integration.test.ts` with imports from `@constructive-io/upload-client`, eliminating duplicated code. This is the same dogfooding pattern applied in constructive-db PR #1099.

Changes:
- Removed `import crypto from 'crypto'` and the two inline helper functions (~19 lines)
- Added `import { hashContent, putToPresignedUrl } from '@constructive-io/upload-client'`
- Added `@constructive-io/upload-client` as a `workspace:*` dependency in `graphql/server-test/package.json`
- Replaced 4 `sha256(...)` call sites with `await hashContent(...)`
- Moved 2 describe-level `contentHash` declarations into `beforeAll` blocks (since `hashContent` is async, unlike the old synchronous `sha256`)

## Review & Testing Checklist for Human

- [ ] **`putToPresignedUrl` signature compatibility**: The old inline helper explicitly set `Content-Length` via `Buffer.byteLength(content).toString()`. Verify the upload-client export handles this internally and accepts the same arguments `(url, content, contentType) → Promise<Response>`.
- [ ] **`hashContent` output equivalence**: The old `sha256()` used `crypto.createHash('sha256').update(content).digest('hex')`. Confirm `hashContent` produces an identical hex digest — a mismatch would cause uploads to succeed but deduplication and content verification to break silently.
- [ ] **Run the upload integration tests**: `cd graphql/server-test && pnpm test -- --testPathPattern=upload.integration` to confirm all tests pass end-to-end against MinIO. These tests require a running MinIO instance (CI provides this).

### Notes
- The lockfile diff is large but substantively just adds the workspace dependency; the rest is pnpm formatting changes.
- Related: constructive-db PR #1093 applied the same dogfooding to `entity-storage-security.integration.test.ts`.

author: kikin81
body:
## Summary

Replaces the deprecated `androidx.compose.material:material-icons-extended` library with **Material Symbols Rounded** — Google's variable icon font — exposed via a new `NubecitaIcon(name = NubecitaIconName.X, filled = …, …)` composable in `:designsystem`. Every call site across 6 modules migrates; the legacy library is dropped from every `build.gradle.kts` and from the version catalog.

Design: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-05-10-material-symbols-rounded-migration-design.md`
Plan: `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-10-material-symbols-rounded-migration.md`

## What ships

| Module | New | Modified |
|---|---|---|
| `:designsystem` | `NubecitaIcon` + `NubecitaIconName` (30 entries) + `Modifier.mirror()` + showcase screenshot fixture + `material_symbols_rounded.ttf` (77 KB, subset) + the developer-facing `scripts/update_material_symbols.sh` + Apache 2.0 license file | 3 component files migrated; `material-icons-extended` dropped |
| `:feature:composer:impl` | — | 4 files migrated |
| `:feature:feed:impl` | — | 5 files migrated |
| `:feature:postdetail:impl` | — | 1 file migrated |
| `:feature:mediaviewer:impl` | — | 1 file migrated |
| `:app` | — | `MainShell` bottom-nav migrated; `material-icons-extended` dropped |
| `gradle/libs.versions.toml` | — | version-catalog entry removed |
| `openspec/specs/design-system/spec.md` | — | new requirement codifying the icon contract (4 scenarios) |

## Notable design choices

- **Subset script, not full font in APK.** The upstream variable font is 14.9 MB. A developer-facing `scripts/update_material_symbols.sh` runs `pyftsubset` to slim it to ~50–80 KB containing only the codepoints declared in `NubecitaIconName`. The script is **not** wired into Gradle (would force every CI runner to pip-install fonttools). Run it manually when adding/removing an icon; commit the regenerated font alongside the enum change.
- **`NubecitaIcon` collapses Filled/Outlined pairs.** The legacy `if (selected) Icons.Filled.Home else Icons.Outlined.Home` pattern becomes `NubecitaIcon(name = NubecitaIconName.Home, filled = selected, …)` — single call site, FILL axis carries the active/inactive distinction. Major DX win for bottom-nav code.
- **`Modifier.mirror()` for RTL directional icons.** Material Symbols doesn't auto-mirror like `Icons.AutoMirrored.*` did — added a per-call-site opt-in modifier so RTL behavior survives the migration. Applied to: ArrowBack, Reply, Article, VolumeUp, VolumeOff.
- **Baseline-alignment guards in `NubecitaIcon`.** Rendering a glyph through Compose `Text` (vs `Icon`'s `Painter`) subjects it to font metrics. Three mitigations: `includeFontPadding = false`, locked `lineHeight = fontSize`, and a `Box(size, contentAlignment = Center)` wrapper. Caught + verified by the showcase screenshot fixture.
- **A11y correctness.** Inner `Text` carries `Modifier.clearAndSetSemantics { }` so the PUA codepoint never leaks to TalkBack — only the `contentDescription` on the parent Box is exposed. Non-null `contentDescription` also declares `role = Role.Image` to match `androidx.compose.material3.Icon`'s behavior. Decorative icons (`contentDescription = null`) have no a11y node at all.

## Test plan

- [x] `:designsystem:testDebugUnitTest` — 17 new JVM unit tests (`NubecitaIconNameTest` codepoint validity + collision detection, no production regressions)
- [x] `:designsystem:connectedDebugAndroidTest` — 5 instrumentation tests on emulator-5554:
  - `NubecitaIconInstrumentationTest` (3) — a11y exposure, FILL-axis raster diff, decorative-icon a11y omission
  - `MirrorInstrumentationTest` (2) — LTR no-op + RTL row-reverse-mirror with calibrated GPU tolerance
- [x] `:designsystem:validateDebugScreenshotTest` — new `NubecitaIconShowcase` baselines (6 × all 30 glyphs in outlined+filled), all pre-existing :designsystem baselines refreshed
- [x] All feature modules' `:testDebugUnitTest` — pre-existing tests green (no VM regressions from icon swaps)
- [x] All feature modules' `:validateDebugScreenshotTest` — baselines refreshed wholesale; visual diff is intentional (Rounded vs default Material Icons style)
- [x] `:app:validateDebugScreenshotTest` — bottom-nav baselines show fully-filled glyphs on active tabs (FILL axis verified end-to-end)
- [x] All modules' `:lint` — clean
- [x] `spotlessCheck` — clean
- [x] `openspec validate --all --strict` — 26/26 specs pass
- [x] `grep -rln "androidx.compose.material.icons" --include="*.kt"` — zero production hits (only doc fixtures under `openspec/references/` retain references for design archives)
- [x] `./gradlew assembleDebug` — clean across all modules

## APK size

| Build | Size |
|---|---|
| Post-migration `app-debug.apk` | 62.4 MB |

Pre-migration comparison needs a separate `main` checkout for accuracy (APKs aren't in git). The subset font is ~77 KB; the dropped `material-icons-extended` artifact's contribution to the APK depends on which icons were tree-shakeable — typically tens to hundreds of KB. Net-net is expected to be near-flat or slightly smaller; the real win is **future-proofing** (the icons library is deprecated by Google) and **DX** (FILL-axis collapse, animated state transitions become trivial as a follow-up).

## Follow-up issues already filed

- `nubecita-pmk` (P4) — pin the subset script's `UPSTREAM_URL` to a SHA instead of `master` so contributors get reproducible builds across weeks.

Closes: nubecita-68g

## Summary

Three cohesive architectural deepenings plus seam enforcement, in service of "decisions in one place, callers in many places". `pipeline.ts` shrinks ~70%; `watcher.ts` shrinks from 241 lines to a thin chokidar adapter.

### 1. `VaultIndex` — canonical vault-state seam
- New `packages/core/src/vaultIndex/` with two adapters of one `VaultIndexSnapshot` shape:
  - `buildVaultIndex` — one-shot, for `pipeline.ts`
  - `createIncrementalVaultIndex` — mutable, for the dev watcher
- Replaces `packages/astro-integration/src/depGraph.ts` and the parse / slug / wikilink-index plumbing previously embedded in `watcher.ts`.
- VaultIndex never calls `classify` — privacy rule stays single-sited.

### 2. `renderPublicNote` — per-note privacy render unit
- New `packages/core/src/render/renderPublicNote.ts` cohesively applies: transclude → serialize → frontmatter allowlist → tag blocklist + gateTag strip → **raw** image extraction → attachment ref collection.
- Closure-naive on purpose — body image URL and frontmatter `cover`/`thumbnail` gating moves to Pass 3.

### 3. `attachmentClosure` — single owner for closure ops
- Renames `attachmentFilter.ts` → `attachmentClosure.ts` and consolidates three exports:
  - `collectAttachmentRefs` (pre-closure, per-note)
  - `buildAttachmentClosure` (cross-note decision)
  - `applyAttachmentClosure` (post-closure RenderedNote gating)
- No caller (audit CLI, dev middleware, build copier) can forget to apply the closure now.

### 4. Package seam — `@noteforge/core` barrel + ESLint enforcement
- `packages/core/src/index.ts` becomes an explicit public seam exporting every cross-package entry point.
- New `no-restricted-imports` rule blocks `@noteforge/core/<subpath>` imports outside the package, so future deepenings cannot regress silently.
- All external callers updated to import from `@noteforge/core`.

PR #9 (docs/a3-prep-drift-fix) 머지 시 stacked PR (#10, #11) 의 base branch (docs/a3-prep-drift-fix) 가 main 으로 squash 되면서 GitHub 가 두 PR 을 자동 \"MERGED\" 표시로 close 했으나 **실제 코드는 main 에 반영되지 않음**. 본 PR 이 PR #10 + #11 모든 변경을 다시 main 으로 머지.

## A2 ORM hotfix (PR #10 변경)

A2 PR #7 이 alembic raw DDL 만 작성하고 SQLAlchemy ORM 모델 파일을 완전 누락한 채로 머지됨. 17 개 파일이 `from app.db.models import ...` 호출 → ImportError. 본 hotfix 가 0001 migration 컬럼·CHECK·index 를 1:1 미러링하는 8 모델 추가 (User/AdminUser/UserConsent/UserCSOTraversal/BroadInterest/CSOTopic/Source/SourcePolicy). `.gitignore` 의 `models/` LLM weights 패턴이 ORM 디렉토리도 매치하던 문제는 negate pattern (`!backend/app/db/models/{,**}`) 으로 해소.

---

Phase 0b 의 마지막 모듈. CSO 3.4 14k 노드 임포트 + NetworkX 메모리 그래프 캐시 + `/topics/*` 7 endpoint 본문.

---

## Summary

- Programmatic marketing-video pipeline at `marketing/video/` — every video, voiceover, and key-art asset is a build artifact regenerable from `src/content/script.ts`
- **6 compositions** registered in Remotion: `Hook`, `BrandShow30`, `BrandShow15Portrait`, `HeroLoop30`, `Demo60`, plus a `KeyArt` still
- **100% local TTS** — Kokoro-82M default (pure Node), Higgs Audio V2 upgrade path (Python via `uv`)
- **Procedural placeholder music** synthesized via ffmpeg sines, with audio integration validated end-to-end
- Locked human-readable spec at `docs/marketing.md` mirrors `src/content/script.ts` as the single source of truth for all copy

Orthogonal to the dictation-shortcuts work on the primary branch — every file lives under `marketing/` plus the one `docs/marketing.md`. No app code touched.

## Why this exists

A traditional video editor freezes the script at export time; re-recording when copy changes is hours per change. With Remotion, every change to `script.ts` re-renders the video on the next `npm run render`. Marketing moves at engineering velocity.

The hook (`Dictate. Transcribe. Record meetings. One Mac app.`) leads with the three-modes category claim — no single-mode competitor (WisprFlow, MacWhisper, VoiceInk, Superwhisper, Voibe, TypeWhisper, FluidVoice) can match it without rebuilding their product.

## What ships in the box

### Compositions

| ID | Duration | Canvas | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Hook` | 5s | 1920×1080 | Brand mark + hook reveal (validation spike) |
| `BrandShow30` | 30s | 1920×1080 | Pop Warhol grid + black/white logo finale — for launches, anniversaries, social |
| `BrandShow15Portrait` | 15s | 1080×1920 | Reels / TikTok / X-mobile vertical sibling |
| `HeroLoop30` | 30s | 1920×1080 | Silent autoplay-muted hero for macparakeet.com (with screencast slots) |
| `Demo60` | 60s | 1920×1080 | Full explainer with per-scene VO + screencast slots |
| `KeyArt` (still) | n/a | 1200×1600 | Canonical 3×4 Warhol grid; renders at 2× for 2400×3200 press-grade PNG |

### TTS pipeline

- **Default**: Kokoro-82M via `kokoro-js` (#1 open-weight TTS by Artificial Analysis ELO, MIT licensed, ~80MB model, pure Node)
- **Premium**: Higgs Audio V2 via Python under `uv` (Llama-3.2-3B foundation, naturalness 9.5/10; opt-in)
- Voice audition script generates 8 brand-curated voice candidates for picking the right narrator
- All voice copy lives in `src/content/script.ts`; change a string → regenerate WAVs → re-render → ship

### Brand fidelity

- Pulls palette from `brand-assets/palette/palette.json` (12 contrast-validated Warhol pairs)
- Renders the canonical app icon (white parakeet on near-black) for the logo finale, matching `docs/brand-identity.md`
- Pop palette discipline: BrandShow30 uses the 6 highest-impact pairs in deliberate row rhythm, not all 12 (per palette.json guidance)

body:
This adds the website media library requested in ZLAP-STORY 10-3 without introducing a new storage platform. Website-scoped media metadata, organization, usage tracking, and UI now live in AI Publisher while reusing story 10-1 media storage and story 10-2 AI asset storage.

- **Data model + ownership boundaries**
  - Added `website_media_library_items` and `website_media_library_usage` in Supabase for website-specific media metadata, tags, associations, usage summaries, and safe delete/archive behavior.
  - Kept tenant and owner scoping in-product; raw storage paths remain internal.
  - Synced AI asset-backed media into the website library by reference instead of duplicating binaries.

- **Library workflows**
  - Added `lib/website-media-library/*` for schema, validation, permissions, storage, usage tracking, tags, and workflow orchestration.
  - Reused existing `lib/media/*` upload/signed URL/delete flows and existing `lib/ai-assets/*` asset lifecycle where library items point at AI-generated assets.
  - Deletion is usage-aware: items referenced outside library context are archived instead of hard-deleted.

- **API surface**
  - Added website media APIs for list, upload, detail, preview, delete, tags, and usage:
    - `GET /api/website-media-library/list`
    - `POST /api/website-media-library/upload`
    - `GET /api/website-media-library/[mediaId]`
    - `GET /api/website-media-library/[mediaId]/preview`
    - `DELETE /api/website-media-library/[mediaId]/delete`
    - `POST /api/website-media-library/[mediaId]/tags`
    - `GET|POST /api/website-media-library/[mediaId]/usage`
  - Preview/retrieval is signed-URL based; payloads stay metadata-light and paginated.

- **UI**
  - Added a dedicated website media library shell with:
    - upload
    - grid/list browsing
    - search / media-type / tag / status filters
    - preview dialog
    - tag editing
    - loading / empty / error states
    - responsive layout
  - Added a website-level route: `/websites/[id]/media`
  - Exposed the library from website management actions.

- **Editor integration**
  - Added a minimal selector flow for website editing: image-like section fields (`image.src`) can open the website media selector and insert a signed preview URL.
  - Recorded selection/insertion usage so media can be traced back to website/page/section contexts.

- **Docs**
  - Added architecture and scenario docs covering:
    - reuse of existing media + AI asset systems
    - DB model
    - API surface
    - upload / preview / select / delete flows
    - access control
    - MVP limits

Example of the new access pattern:

```ts
const response = await fetch(`/api/website-media-library/${itemId}/preview`);
const { preview } = await response.json();

// UI consumes signed preview URLs only.
img.src = preview.url;
```

author: tayvenb13
body:
## Summary

vmagent has not run on the cluster since PR #158 merged. vm-operator 0.69.0 (chart 0.62.1) translates our \`statefulMode: true\` + \`statefulStorage\` config into a StatefulSet whose \`spec.volumeClaimTemplates[0]\` is missing \`spec.resources.requests.storage\` — Kubernetes rejects the StatefulSet with \`Required value\`. The VMAgent CRD instance's status went \`failed\`; ArgoCD's view of the wrapper chart stayed \`Synced/Healthy\` because the CRD resource was successfully applied, **masking the downstream reconcile failure**.

**Consequence:** vmsingle's TSDB stayed at \`totalSeries: 0\` for ~24h. Every Grafana panel rendered "No data" because there was nothing to query. The user's report of blank dashboards was the symptom.

## Live fix already applied

\`\`\`bash
kubectl -n vm-system patch vmagent vmagent-chalupa --type=json -p='[
  {"op": "remove", "path": "/spec/statefulMode"},
  {"op": "remove", "path": "/spec/statefulStorage"}
]'
\`\`\`

vmagent pod went \`0/0 → 2/2 Running\` within 30s. Confirmed scraping cluster-wide via \`/api/v1/targets\`:

\`\`\`
 6 up   job=kubelet           (all 6 nodes)
 6 up   job=cadvisor          (all 6 nodes)
 3 up   job=prometheus-node-exporter  (3 workers)
 5 up   job=argocd-*-metrics  (all 5 ArgoCD components)
 3 up   job=external-secrets-*
 1 up   job=kube-state-metrics
 1 up   job=traefik-metrics
 1 up   job=cnpg-system/cnpg-system-cloudnative-pg
 2 up   job=vmsingle-vmsingle-chalupa  (self-scrape)
 2 up   job=vmagent-vmagent-chalupa    (self-scrape)
 1 up   job=grafana
 1 down job=grafana            (the crashlooping new pod from #163 migration; unrelated)
 1 down job=openbao-active     (needs the post-merge restart runbook from #162)
\`\`\`

vmsingle is now ingesting; dashboards populate within a minute.

## Why revert in git too

ArgoCD's \`automated.selfHeal: true\` (on the observability-apps ApplicationSet) will re-apply \`statefulMode: true\` from git on next reconcile unless we remove it there too. This commit aligns the wrapper template with the live patch.

## What about the WAL buffer

The 5 Gi WAL was always a nice-to-have for surviving multi-minute vmsingle outages. At homelab scale (single vmsingle, restarts in seconds, vmagent's in-memory buffer adequate for that window) the buffer wasn't load-bearing. The inline comment in the template documents the failure mode so a future operator who finds the right vm-operator 0.6x storage syntax can re-enable WAL.

## Process miss for future reference

I treated ArgoCD's \`Synced/Healthy\` as proof that a stack works. That's wrong — \`Synced\` only means \"the resources I created equal the manifest in git.\" For operator-driven CRDs (CNPG Cluster, VMAgent, etc.) you have to ALSO check the operator's downstream reconciliation succeeded (e.g., \`kubectl get vmagent\` status, \`kubectl get cluster\` status, the actual workload pods existing). I'll be more rigorous on post-merge cluster verification going forward — running a real \`get pods\` + a metric/query against the data plane, not just asking ArgoCD if it's happy.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI passes (depends on PR #165 — \`fix/ci-helm-render-api-versions-and-vm-crd-skip\` — landing first)
- [ ] After merge: \`kubectl -n vm-system get vmagent vmagent-chalupa\` status transitions from \`failed\` to a healthy state (operator updates on next reconcile)
- [ ] After merge: \`kubectl -n vm-system get pods\` still shows vmagent-vmagent-chalupa-* \`2/2 Running\`
- [ ] vmagent target health: \`curl localhost:8429/api/v1/targets\` (via port-forward) shows 30+ targets UP
- [ ] vmsingle TSDB: \`curl localhost:8429/api/v1/status/tsdb\` shows totalSeries climbing

body:
## Summary
Implements a new "HR split" feature that allows users to view and edit note content in a side-by-side layout by Ctrl/Cmd+clicking on horizontal rules (`<hr>` elements). This provides a convenient way to compare or work with related content simultaneously.

## Key Changes

- **New `hrSplitPlugin.ts`**: Core ProseMirror plugin that manages split state
  - Tracks which horizontal rules are "split-active" via ordinal indices
  - Applies CSS decorations to position blocks in left/right columns
  - Handles Ctrl/Cmd+click on `<hr>` elements to toggle splits
  - Persists active splits to localStorage via `onChange` callback
  - Reconciles stored state when HRs are deleted to prevent stale entries

- **New `assignColumns.ts`**: Pure column-assignment algorithm
  - Determines the role (left/right/divider/full-width) for each top-level block
  - Implements "first-wins" semantics: adjacent active HRs resolve independently
  - Inactive HRs between active ones act as separators, allowing independent splits

- **New `hrSplitStore.ts`**: localStorage persistence layer
  - Loads/saves active ordinals per note GUID
  - Validates and sanitizes stored data
  - Gracefully handles missing localStorage or quota exceeded

- **Updated `TomboyEditor.svelte`**:
  - Registers the HR split plugin via a new Extension
  - Seeds split state from localStorage when loading a note
  - Resynchronizes state before doc swaps to prevent cross-note contamination
  - Adds comprehensive CSS grid layout styling for split rendering

- **Test coverage**: Unit tests for `assignColumns` and `hrSplitStore` logic

## Implementation Details

- **State management**: Active splits are stored as a `Set<number>` of HR ordinals (0-based indices among HRs only), making them stable across content edits within blocks
- **Persistence strategy**: Uses `queueMicrotask` to batch onChange callbacks and avoids echoing loaded state back to storage
- **CSS grid layout**: Uses `grid-auto-flow: dense` to allow left/right columns of different heights while maintaining proper row alignment
- **Affordance**: All `<hr>` elements get a pointer cursor; visual "split me" styling is handled via CSS when the editor has active splits

body:
## Summary

Continuación del hotfix de PR #158. Después de mergear el fix de migration 0015, drizzle avanzó al siguiente fallo: migration 0017 (Factoring v1) crea un partial unique index con `WHERE expires_at > now()`, que Postgres rechaza porque `now()` no es IMMUTABLE.

\`functions in index predicate must be marked IMMUTABLE\`

## Cambio

Una línea:

\`\`\`diff
- CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_shipper_credit_decisions_vigente
-   ON shipper_credit_decisions(empresa_shipper_id)
-   WHERE expires_at > now();
+ CREATE UNIQUE INDEX uq_shipper_credit_decisions_vigente
+   ON shipper_credit_decisions(empresa_shipper_id, expires_at);
\`\`\`

La app code filtra por \`expires_at > now()\` en queries de lectura. La unicidad estricta a nivel BD ahora es por \`(empresa_shipper_id, expires_at)\` — permite múltiples rows por shipper, una por cada underwriting histórico.

## Verificación

- Migration 0017 nunca se aplicó exitosamente en prod (bloqueado por este bug). Sin estado parcial que limpiar.
- App code de factoring está flag-gated (\`FACTORING_V1_ACTIVATED\`) por lo que tampoco depende todavía del comportamiento exacto del índice.

author: kyya
body:
## Summary

This PR makes three coordinated changes to the skill's structure, motivated by a comparison with `tw93/kami`:

1. **Extract the inline `<style>` block out of `templates/tutorial-template.html` into `templates/styles.css`** — the stylesheet becomes the single source of truth for the visual language.
2. **Add `references/design.md`** — an English design rationale document covering color tokens, type scale, callout taxonomy, layout invariants, and an explicit do-not-cross list. This is the spec; `styles.css` is the implementation.
3. **Bundle fonts via download-on-first-run** — `scripts/install_fonts.py` fetches Noto Sans CJK SC + JetBrains Mono into `assets/fonts/`, and both build scripts auto-call it when fonts are missing. System font packages (`fonts-noto-cjk`, `fonts-symbola`) are no longer required for a fresh install.

## Motivation

The skill was carrying ~435 lines of inline CSS, no documented design rationale, and hard-coded dependencies on system-wide CJK font packages. Three follow-on problems:

- Iterating on the visual system meant editing a 510-line HTML template by hand; diffs were noisy and one CSS change could break three components with no record of intent.
- A new contributor had no way to know whether to add a fifth callout variant or to fold it into one of the existing four — the rules existed only in the maintainer's head.
- First-run friction was high: a user had to `sudo apt install fonts-noto-cjk fonts-symbola fonts-noto-color-emoji` before any PDF would render, which also blocked rootless containers and read-only CI environments.

## Changes

### `refactor(templates): extract inline CSS into templates/styles.css`

The `<style>` block (435 lines, lines 7–441 of the original template) moves to `templates/styles.css` verbatim. The template now references it via `<link rel="stylesheet" href="styles.css">`. A banner comment at the top of `styles.css` points readers at `references/design.md` for rationale.

The relative `href="styles.css"` resolves correctly both when WeasyPrint reads `templates/tutorial-template.html` directly and when the filled HTML is rendered from anywhere else (see the build-script change below).

### `docs(references): add design.md design rationale document`

A new `references/design.md` documents:

- **Color tokens** (17 hex values with their role).
- **Type scale** (10 size/weight/line-height entries) and the rationale for the 1.75 body line-height.
- **Font stack** and why this skill stays single-sans rather than going serif-led like editorial systems.
- **Layout invariants** (A4, page-margin asymmetry, TOC cap at 9, cover bleed).
- **Callout taxonomy**: four variants in escalating severity (`callout-tip` blue / bare `.callout` yellow / `callout-warn` red / `callout-cc` purple), with explicit notes on two non-obviousnesses: the bare `.callout` is the heads-up variant rather than the tip, and `callout-warn` is the *severe* red variant rather than the regular yellow warning.
- **Step component** spec.
- **Don'ts** list (no fifth callout variant, no `rgba()` for backgrounds because of the WeasyPrint double-rectangle bug, no Arabic chapter numerals, no line-height below 1.75).
- **Evolving the system**: tokens-first, then CSS, then smoke test.

Modeled on `tw93/kami`'s `references/design.md` but inverted in stance: where Kami is editorial and quiet, baomu is instructional and signal-heavy. The doc names that contrast explicitly so future edits do not drift toward generic editorial design.

### `feat(fonts): bundle Noto Sans CJK SC and JetBrains Mono via download-on-first-run`

- **`scripts/install_fonts.py`** — idempotent downloader. Fetches Noto Sans CJK SC Regular + Bold (from `notofonts/noto-cjk`) and JetBrains Mono Regular (from `JetBrains/JetBrainsMono`), all under OFL. ~33 MB total. Supports `--force` (re-download) and `--check` (exit 0/1).
- **`templates/styles.css`** — gains three `@font-face` declarations. Each uses `local("Noto Sans CJK SC"), local("Source Han Sans SC"), local("PingFang SC"), url("../assets/fonts/...")` so a pre-installed system font is preferred when present and the bundled file is the fallback. The mono font-family stack is updated to prefer `"JetBrains Mono"` before `"SF Mono"`.
- **`scripts/build_pdf.py`** and **`scripts/preview_all.py`** — switch WeasyPrint to inject the stylesheet via `stylesheets=[CSS(filename=...)]`. Because `CSS(filename=...)` sets `base_url` to the CSS file's directory, the relative `url("../assets/fonts/...")` in `@font-face` resolves to the skill's `assets/fonts/` regardless of where the user's filled HTML lives. Both scripts call a new `_ensure_fonts()` helper before rendering, which invokes `install_fonts.py` automatically when fonts are missing; a download failure logs a warning and falls back to system fonts rather than crashing the render.
- **`.gitignore`** — ignores `assets/fonts/*.{otf,ttf,woff,woff2}` so the ~33 MB of binary fonts never enter the repo.
- **`assets/fonts/README.md`** — placeholder documenting which files `install_fonts.py` populates and why they're not vendored.

User-facing impact: copy `templates/tutorial-template.html` to any working directory, fill in the placeholders, run `build_pdf.py`. No co-located `styles.css` needed. No system font packages needed. No `sudo` needed. First build on a fresh machine downloads ~33 MB; subsequent builds are instant.

## Verification

Tested with the following matrix:

| Scenario | Expectation | Result |
|---|---|---|
| Fresh repo, `assets/fonts/` empty, render from `/tmp/work/` with no co-located styles.css | Auto-download fonts, render PDF, four callouts correct, code in JetBrains Mono | ✅ |
| Fonts already installed, idempotent re-run | Skip download, render normally | ✅ |
| Delete `assets/fonts/`, re-render | Auto-restore on next build | ✅ |
| `python3 scripts/install_fonts.py --check` with all fonts present | exit 0 | ✅ |
| `python3 scripts/install_fonts.py --check` with fonts missing | exit 1, no download | ✅ |

Visual regression checked by rasterizing the rendered PDFs at 100 DPI and comparing the cover, TOC, and a content page with all four callout variants against the pre-refactor output. No differences observed.

## What this is not

- This PR does **not** change the visual design (colors, type scale, spacing). It refactors the structure so future visual changes have a clean place to live.
- It does **not** introduce new callout variants. The do-not-cross list in `design.md` codifies the existing four.
- It does **not** change how authors fill in the template — the placeholder syntax, chapter numerals, and structure are all unchanged.

## Related

Inspired by [`tw93/kami`](https://github.com/tw93/kami), particularly its external `styles.css`, `references/design.md`, and bundled-fonts approach. This skill remains positioned for instructional/tutorial content rather than editorial documents; the two design systems are complementary, not overlapping.

body:
### Description of the Change

Pulled the copy-pasted embedding logic that lived in the OpenAI, Azure, and Ollama classification providers into a single trait (EmbeddingsProviderTrait). Things like chunking, normalizing content, generating/storing post and term embeddings, similarity + term matching, threshold handling, and the preview AJAX handler now live in one place.

Each provider still owns its own API calls, auth, settings UI, and scheduler hooks—the trait only covers the parts that were basically the same three times, with small hooks for things like max tokens (Ollama still overrides that for model-specific limits).

Meta keys and filter names are still derived from each provider’s ID (classifai_{provider_id}_…), so existing integrations shouldn’t need to change.

Closes #889 

### How to test the Change

Use a dev/staging site with ClassifAI enabled. Have (or create) a few posts with real body text and at least one taxonomy (e.g. categories/tags) turned on for Classification.

**OpenAI Embeddings (Classification)**
1. Set Classification provider to OpenAI Embeddings, save settings, and complete auth if prompted.
2. Edit/save a term in an enabled taxonomy; confirm no PHP errors and term meta still behaves (embeddings regenerate or exist as before).
3. Edit a post, run classification / auto-suggest (whatever UI you normally use), and confirm suggested terms still appear and can be applied.
4. Open the embeddings preview in the classifier UI (the flow that hits `get_post_classifier_embeddings_preview_data`); confirm it returns term suggestions without a nonce or JSON error.
5. If you have the regenerate embeddings admin flow wired for OpenAI, run it once and confirm it finishes and you still get a success notice / redirect with no fatals.

**Azure OpenAI Embeddings (Classification)**
Switch Classification provider to Azure OpenAI Embeddings, configure endpoint/key/deployment, save. Repeat steps 3–5 (term save, classify post, preview). Confirm API errors still surface as before if credentials are wrong.

**Ollama Embeddings (Classification)**
Switch to Ollama, point at your local Ollama URL, pick a supported embedding model, save. Repeat steps 3–5 again. Pay attention to long posts: chunking should still behave (no silent empty embeddings if something broke in max-token handling).

**Recommended Content (OpenAI only in typical setups)**
Enable Recommended Content with OpenAI Embeddings, publish or update a post, and confirm related/recommended output still works (or embeddings still write to post meta without errors in logs).

**Regression pass**
With browser devtools or debug.log open, click through Classification settings save, term edit, and post classify for each provider you use; confirm no PHP warnings/notices tied to EmbeddingsProviderTrait or missing methods.

**Optional CLI**
If you use WP-CLI Classifai commands that hit embeddings for OpenAI/Azure, run one against a test post and confirm it still completes.

### Changelog Entry

> Changed - Refactored and cleaned up duplicate code for embedding providers

Props @zamanq

author: 14mdzk
body:
## Summary

End-to-end coverage for the Casbin watcher → enforcer notification loop shipped in v1.1 PR-03b. Two parallel `Adapter` instances share one watcher (or one Redis pub/sub channel); the test mutates policy on instance A, then asserts instance B sees the change within 1s — via the **incremental-apply path**, with the back-stop `ReloadInterval` disabled so the only propagation route is the watcher.

| Test                                      | Asserts                                                          |
|-------------------------------------------|------------------------------------------------------------------|
| `TestWatcherE2E_Memory`                   | `MemoryWatcher` add-policy: A mutates → B sees within 1s         |
| `TestWatcherE2E_Memory_Remove`            | `MemoryWatcher` remove-policy propagates A → B                   |
| `TestWatcherE2E_Redis`                    | `RedisWatcher` add via pub/sub propagates A → B                  |
| `TestWatcherE2E_Redis_Remove`             | `RedisWatcher` remove via pub/sub propagates A → B               |
| `TestWatcherE2E_Redis_IsolatedChannels`   | PR-19 `:v1` / `:v2` channel isolation — `:v1` subscribers do not hear `:v2` traffic |

Plus `TestRedisWatcher_UpdatePublishes` and `TestRedisWatcher_CallbackTriggered` for the lower-level send/receive primitives.

Closes v1.2 punch-list row #21. See [`docs/audit/pr-21-casbin-watcher-e2e-test.md`](./docs/audit/pr-21-casbin-watcher-e2e-test.md).

## Design notes

- A `notifyWatcher` wrapper intercepts `SetUpdateCallback` to expose `waitForUpdate()` for deterministic test synchronisation.
- A receive-only watcher variant prevents the publisher-and-subscriber-share-watcher cascade that races Casbin's non-thread-safe `Enforcer`. This was the failure mode that surfaced mid-implementation — the fix is documented inline in the test file.
- Redis tests use **`miniredis`** to avoid an external dependency. The watcher e2e does not need real network behaviour; pub/sub is in-process within miniredis.
- Back-stop reload is set to a very long interval so the watcher path is exercised in isolation.

## Out of Scope

- Wiring `RedisWatcher` into `internal/platform/app/app.go` (still a future task — PR-19 #44 was preventive).
- Real-Redis testcontainer coverage (miniredis is sufficient for the watcher contract).
- New watcher implementation.

## Test plan

- [x] All 7 tests in the suite pass on a clean checkout (`go test ./internal/adapter/casbin/ -run "TestWatcherE2E|TestRedisWatcher" -v`).
- [x] `make lint test` exit 0.
- [x] No production code touched.
- [x] `CHANGELOG.md` `[Unreleased]` under "Testing".
- [x] `docs/audit/v1.2-punch-list.md` row 21 → `in review`.

author: dcyfr
body:
## Summary

Unblocks the `Release` workflow which has failed on every push to main since the workflow was added. Adds the missing `.changeset/` directory and the three `changeset:*` npm scripts that the workflow already references.

## Root cause

[`.github/workflows/release.yml`](.github/workflows/release.yml) uses `changesets/action@v1` and `npm run changeset:{version,tag}`, but the repo was missing:
- `.changeset/config.json`
- `.changeset/README.md`
- the `changeset`, `changeset:version`, `changeset:tag` scripts in `package.json`

Every push to main produced:
```
Error: There is no .changeset directory in this project
```

## Fix

Mirrors the working setup in `dcyfr-labs/dcyfr-ai-agents`:
- `.changeset/config.json` — same shape, `repo` pointed at this sandbox, `access: "restricted"` since this package is `"private": true` (vs. `public` in ai-agents)
- `.changeset/README.md` — standard changesets explainer
- `package.json` — adds `changeset`, `changeset:version`, `changeset:tag` scripts

Since there are no unreleased changeset .md files in `.changeset/`, the action will exit cleanly with `published: false`, and the tag-creation steps (gated on `published == 'true'`) stay no-op. Future contributors cut a version by running `npm run changeset` and committing the resulting .md file.

## Verification

```
$ python3 -c "import json; json.load(open('.changeset/config.json'))" && echo ok
ok
$ python3 -c "import json; d=json.load(open('package.json')); assert all(k in d['scripts'] for k in ['changeset','changeset:version','changeset:tag'])" && echo ok
ok
```

CI on this PR (Lint / Type Check / Test) is independent of the changesets config — it just runs `npm install` + `npm run lint`/etc., none of which touch `.changeset/`. The Release workflow on main will re-run after merge and should succeed.

author: mytreya-rh
body:
## Summary

Fixes the sporadic timeout error in IstioCSR feature e2e tests where the IstioCSR object's Ready condition is missing, even though the deployment was successfully created and became ready.

## Problem

The IstioCSR controller's `Ready` condition was occasionally missing because multiple `updateStatus()` calls during reconciliation were overwriting the entire status using `DeepCopyInto()`, which erased previously set conditions.

### Root Cause

During reconciliation, the controller calls `updateStatus()` multiple times from different functions:
- `createOrApplyServices()`
- `createOrApplyServiceAccounts()`  
- `createOrApplyRBACResource()`
- `createOrApplyDeployments()`

Each `updateStatus()` call:
1. Fetches the latest IstioCSR object from the API server
2. Calls `changed.Status.DeepCopyInto(&current.Status)` which **overwrites the entire status** including Conditions
3. Updates the API server

This caused conditions set in earlier reconciliation steps to be lost when later status updates occurred.

## Solution

Modified the `updateStatus()` function in `pkg/controller/istiocsr/utils.go` to preserve existing conditions when updating individual status fields:

1. Save existing conditions before the `DeepCopyInto()` call
2. If no conditions are being updated, preserve all existing conditions
3. If conditions are being updated, merge them (new conditions override existing ones of the same type, but other existing conditions are preserved)

This ensures that conditions like `Ready` and `Degraded` are never lost during intermediate status updates.

## Testing

- Added comprehensive unit tests in `pkg/controller/istiocsr/utils_test.go` covering:
  - Preserving existing conditions when updating with no conditions
  - Merging new conditions with existing ones
  - Overriding existing conditions with same type
  - Setting new conditions when none exist

- All existing unit tests pass
- Code builds successfully
- go vet passes with no issues

## Files Changed

- `pkg/controller/istiocsr/utils.go` - Fixed `updateStatus()` to preserve conditions
- `pkg/controller/istiocsr/utils_test.go` - Added unit tests for condition preservation

## Summary

Bundles seven commits adding the PWA install shell, the redesigned Kitchen attention feed, and the supporting activity-provenance backend (visible as the new Activity tab grid).

## What changed

- **PWA**: installable on phones via `manifest.webmanifest` + service worker (network-first, never caches `/api/*`); shared `PWA_HEAD_TAGS` injected on every top-level page; nav rail auto-collapses after item tap on phone viewports.

- **Activity tab**: grid layout (time | badge | actor | summary | chevron) with always-visible absolute + relative timestamps, type-chip multi-select filter, date-range presets (1h/24h/7d/All), click-to-expand row showing full payload + run link.

author: uprightbass360
body:
## Summary

Spotted during hifi smoke test of arm-neu 18.2.0-rc (Kolchak BD folder rip, 6 titles). DB \`progress\` field stayed at 0.0 throughout a 37-minute multi-file encode, jumped to 100.0 only on job finalization. User experience: UI looked stuck. Not a regression from any recent change - this bug has likely been present since multi-file transcode was first supported.

## Root cause

The per-file transcoder functions (\`_transcode_file_handbrake\`, \`_transcode_file_ffmpeg\`) called \`_update_progress(job_id, file_progress)\` with raw 0..100% PER-FILE values. \`_update_progress\` has a rate-limiter that requires \`delta >= PROGRESS_UPDATE_THRESHOLD (=5%)\` to commit a write.

For a 6-title BD:
- File 0 progresses 0% -> 99%. \`_last_progress[226]\` ends at ~99.
- File 1 starts: file-boundary write tries \`progress=(1/6)*100 = 16.67\`. delta = \`16.67 - 99 = -82\`. **Suppressed.**
- File 1's HandBrake samples emit 0..100% PER-FILE values, all < 99. All **suppressed.**
- Same for files 2-5.
- Job finalization sets \`progress=100.0\` directly.

Result: progress field freezes at the file-0 high-water mark from start to end.

## Fix

Thread \`file_index\` and \`total_files\` through the per-file transcode functions. The handlers now compute overall job progress before calling \`_update_progress\`:

\`\`\`python
overall = (file_index + file_progress / 100.0) / total_files * 100.0
\`\`\`

Example for a 6-title job during file 3 at 50% file-progress:
- Before: \`_update_progress(226, 50.0)\` - blocked by rate limiter (delta = 50 - 99 = -49)
- After: \`_update_progress(226, 58.33)\` - passes; user sees monotonic climb

The file-boundary write in \`_transcode_files\` already used the same overall scale, so it remains correct and no longer fights with per-file values.

## Tests

4 new tests in \`TestMultiFileProgressScaling\` cover:
- File 0/3 at 60% per-file -> 20% overall
- File 3/6 at 50% per-file -> 58.33% overall
- Single-file default (file_index=0, total_files=1) is a no-op (regression guard)
- FFmpeg path applies the same scaling (parity with HandBrake)

Updated 3 fake-transcode test helpers in \`test_integration.py\` and \`test_transcoder_deep.py\` to accept the new kwargs.

**Suite: 789 pass.**

## Impact

- **No wire change** - the new params are keyword-only with sensible defaults, so any external callers of the per-file functions continue to work.
- **No behavior change for single-file jobs** - file_index=0, total_files=1 reduces to identity scaling.
- **Multi-file jobs (folder rips, multi-title discs)** now show smooth 0..100% UI progress.

## Smoke plan

After merge:
- Cut a transcoder RC, deploy on transcoder-server
- Run a multi-file folder rip from ARM
- Verify \`/jobs?limit=1\` shows \`progress\` climbing across the encode
- Verify single-title disc rips still work (file_index=0, total_files=1 path)

author: idolanuel5885
body:
Replaces the `addr_id → deal-info → street-deals` flow (PR #21 / B.14 v2) with the radius-scoped pipeline documented by [`nitzpo/nadlan-mcp`](https://github.com/nitzpo/nadlan-mcp). The previous flow returned only deals from the **single building** the address sat in, because `deal-info`'s `polygon_id` is parcel-scoped.

## What's new

**`real_estate/govmap_client.py`** — two public functions:
- `autocomplete_address(query)` — unchanged contract.
- `find_comparable_deals(point_x, point_y, radius_m=200, max_deals=10)` — single entry point. Pipeline:
  1. `GET /real-estate/deals/{x},{y}/{radius}` → polygon metadata (URL uses **comma**, not space-in-parens — this was the PoC fix).
  2. Top `_MAX_POLYGONS` (10) polygons by `dealscount`.
  3. For each, `GET /real-estate/street-deals/{polygon_id}`.
  4. Filter to `propertyTypeDescription == "דירה"`.
  5. Enrich each deal's address from the polygon (deal payload has `streetNameHeb=null` when `polygon_id` is `"{gush}-{parcel}"`).
  6. Sort by `dealDate` desc, take top `max_deals`.

Minimal headers (`Content-Type` + `User-Agent` only — matches nitzpo). Polygon-level failures are dropped silently (partial success); only the radius query raises `POLYGONS_FETCH_FAILED`. 0.2 s sleep between sequential street-deals calls.

**Web (`/shuma/comparables`)** — signature changes from `{addr_id, limit}` to `{itm_x, itm_y, radius_m, max_deals}`. Radius clamped 50–1000 m server-side; `max_deals` 1–50.

**UI (`shuma.html`)** — radius slider (50–500 m, default 200) added below the autocomplete input. Hidden inputs now store `itm_x` / `itm_y` (parsed from the autocomplete `POINT` field) instead of `addr_id`.

## What's removed

- `tests/poc_new_endpoints.py` and `GET /shuma/poc-test`
- The `addr_id → deal-info → polygon_id` step (and the helper for it)

## Tests

```
26 passed, 13 skipped
```

Coverage: autocomplete (parse / filter / fail), `find_comparable_deals` happy path with polygon-level address enrichment, apartment filter, sort+limit, partial success on polygon failure, empty radius, `_MAX_POLYGONS` cap, neighborhood fallback. Web endpoints (success / failure-with-error-code / `NO_DEALS_FOUND`). End-to-end report (outlier marker + balcony-column hiding) retained. Live smoke is `pytest.mark.skip`-d.

## Docs

- CLAUDE.md B.13 service table consolidated; B.14 rewritten end-to-end for the new flow.
- `nadlan_integration_report.md` gets "Iteration 4 — Final radius-based pipeline" with the PoC 1–13 summary, the three endpoints we landed on, and refreshed `curl` commands.

## Manual verification after merge + deploy

The user's accept-test addresses:
- `רוטשילד 1, תל אביב` @ 200 m → expect 5–10 apartments from multiple streets (אחד העם, הרצל, לילינבלום, מונטיפיורי, רוטשילד, …) in recent years.
- `אבן גבירול 50, תל אביב` @ 200 m → expect results.
- An address in חיפה / ירושלים → check coverage outside Tel Aviv.

Out of scope here:

No new dependencies.

author: hariprrasadias-collab
body:
💡 What: Refactored the `get_year_trends` endpoint in `backend/app/routes/seer.py` to use a single aggregated `GROUP BY year, subject` query instead of iterating through years and executing a separate count query for each.

🎯 Why: The original implementation suffered from an N+1 query bottleneck. For every distinct year, it executed an additional database query inside a loop, taking O(N) database calls. This becomes a significant bottleneck as the dataset grows.

📊 Impact: Reduces the number of database queries from O(N) (number of years + 2) to O(1) (exactly 3 queries total), while maintaining O(N) time complexity for processing the data in-memory. Benchmarks demonstrate an 8x speedup (~0.0084s -> ~0.0010s on a dataset of 100 years).

🔬 Measurement: Verifiable by executing `get_year_trends` manually with test datasets, and tracing the executed SQL queries to confirm the removal of the N+1 loop. Time performance can be tested locally using a python script to simulate large year distributions.

- `pkdx/.gitignore` の `_build/` / `.mooncakes/` / `target/` / `pkdx_*_test.db` をルート `.gitignore` へマージ
- `setup.sh` / `bin/pkdx` / `bin/pkdx.cmd` / `scripts/sync_version.sh` / `scripts/bench_branch.sh` / `.github/workflows/build-pkdx.yml` の `pkdx/` プレフィックス付きパスをすべて更新

モジュール名は `pkdxtools/pkdx` のまま据え置き。`moon.pkg` 内の `pkdxtools/pkdx/src/...` インポート文は `<module_name>/<relative_path_from_module_root>` 形式のため、`moon.mod.json` の位置だけが変わる本変更では書き換え不要。

`plans/` 配下の歴史的プラン文書は当時の構造を記録した snapshot のため意図的に未変更で残している。

### Motivation

- Allow frontend to capture an optional Level‑4 business category, a free‑text city of residence, and an optional referrer (user ID or referral code) during registration without breaking existing registration flows.
- Provide endpoints for driving the frontend dropdown flow (main categories → children) and a referral search to support referral selection by name/code.

### Description

- Added a safe PostgreSQL migration `2026_05_11_000001_add_registration_optional_fields_to_users_table.php` that conditionally adds nullable `business_category_id`, `city_of_residence`, and `referred_by_user_id` columns to `users` and adds foreign keys only when column types are compatible. 
- Extended `RegisterRequest` to accept `display_name`, `city_id`, `city_of_residence`, `business_category_id`, and `referred_by_user_id` (all optional) and added a `withValidator` post‑validation check to prefer validating that `business_category_id` is a Level 4 category when the `circle_categories.level` column exists. 
- Updated `AuthController::register` and `createRegisteredUser` to keep the existing registration logic intact (password hashing, Sanctum token, referral reward flow, joined categories/circle membership) while persisting `business_category_id`, `city_of_residence`, and the referrer mapping (stored into existing `introduced_by` or `referred_by_user_id` columns when present); response user payload is enriched with `business_category`, `city_of_residence`, and `referred_by` info. 
- Added V1 APIs for categories and referral search: `GET /api/v1/business-categories/main`, `GET /api/v1/business-categories/{parent_id}/children`, and `GET /api/v1/referrals/search?q=...`, and wired the routes in `routes/api.php`. 
- Added `BusinessCategoryController` to serve both self‑referencing and legacy level tables, enhanced `ReferralController` with a search method, and updated `User` model fillable/relations for the new fields. 
- Included Postman‑style documentation examples in `docs/api/register_business_categories_postman_examples.md` describing register payload and responses and the new endpoints.

### Testing

- Performed PHP syntax checks with `php -l` for modified/added files (`AuthController`, `ReferralController`, `BusinessCategoryController`, `RegisterRequest`, `User`, migration and `routes/api.php`) and they reported no syntax errors. 
- Ran `git diff --check` to ensure no whitespace/merge issues and it returned clean. 
- Attempted to run `php artisan route:list --path=api/v1/business-categories` but it could not run in this environment because `vendor/autoload.php` (composer dependencies) is missing; route additions were still validated via `php -l` and manual route file updates.

author: tim1016
body:
## Summary

Follow-up bugfix to PRs [#214](https://github.com/tim1016/learn-ai/pull/214) and [#216](https://github.com/tim1016/learn-ai/pull/216). When the IDE shell landed, the ticker-range-picker started overflowing horizontally inside the 320px-wide left rail and the From/To `<input type="date">` pair ended up clipped — the inputs rendered to the *right* of the rail, hidden by `.ide-rail-left { overflow-y: auto }`'s implicit `overflow-x: auto`.

**Symptom (user-reported):** "the date picker is not visible" on Data Lab / Engine Lab Configure. The Instrument card renders, then a gap where the Time-window card should be, then the next section card.

## Root cause

`.picker-v2__groups` used:
```scss
grid-template-columns: 1.1fr 1.4fr 1fr;       /* 3-col default */
&--no-sampling { grid-template-columns: 1.1fr 1.6fr; }  /* 2-col when hideSampling */
```
plus a `@media (max-width: 900px)` collapse to one column. The collapse fired on **viewport** width — so at viewport ≥900px the picker stayed multi-column even when mounted inside the 320px IDE rail, where the date-input track's min-content (~246px) couldn't fit. The time-window column expanded past the rail's right edge.

## Fix

- Declare `container: picker / inline-size` on `.picker-v2` so the inner grid layout is driven by the picker's own width, not the viewport.
- Default `.picker-v2__groups` to a single column (`grid-template-columns: 1fr`).
- Promote to the 2/3-column layout via `@container picker (min-width: 560px)`, using `minmax(0, …fr)` so columns can shrink without bursting their tracks.
- Drop the now-redundant `@media (max-width: 900px)` block.

## Verification

| viewport | rail / picker width | groups columns | date input visible? |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 (stacked) | 702px / 661px | 2 cols (253 / 368) | ✓ |
| 1100 (just above breakpoint) | 778px / 737px | 2 cols (284 / 413) | ✓ |
| 1366 (2-col IDE) | 320px / 269px | 1 col (280) | ✓ |
| 1600 (2-col IDE) | 320px / 269px | 1 col (280) | ✓ |
| 1920 (3-col IDE) | 320px / 268px | 1 col (288) | ✓ |

Used the `/_ide-sandbox` and `/data-lab` routes for live DOM inspection.

- `npx tsc --noEmit` — clean
- `npx eslint Frontend/src/ --max-warnings 0` — 171 warnings (baseline, unchanged)
- `npx ng test --watch=false` — 77 test files pass, 0 new failures vs. master

## Test plan

- [ ] Visit `/data-lab` and `/engine` (Configure tab) at 1920px. Confirm the left rail's "Backtest data" / "Instrument & Range" picker stacks Instrument + Time-window vertically and the From/To date inputs are visible inside the rail.
- [ ] Same at 1366px. Same expectation.
- [ ] At 1024px (stacked IDE mode), the picker has room for two columns side-by-side — confirm it now uses them.
- [ ] CI: lint + tsc + vitest green.

author: akarras
body:
## Summary

Combines **Phase 2** (webhook delivery) and **Phase 3** (frontend UI) into a single PR on top of the Phase 1 backend that shipped in #586.

After this lands, a logged-in user can:
1. Add an item to a List
2. Click the new bell icon on the item row
3. Pick a world/DC, set a price threshold, choose Discord DM or webhook delivery
4. Manage rules + view recent fires at `/alerts`

## What lands

### Phase 2 — Webhook delivery (backend, 3 commits)

- New `AlertDelivery::Webhook { url }` variant on the API type ([`ultros-api-types/src/alert.rs`](https://github.com/akarras/ultros/blob/feat/price-alerts-phase-2-3/ultros-api-types/src/alert.rs))
- New `EndpointConfig::Webhook { url }` variant + `send_webhook` helper in the dispatcher ([`ultros/src/alerts/delivery.rs`](https://github.com/akarras/ultros/blob/feat/price-alerts-phase-2-3/ultros/src/alerts/delivery.rs)). Payload is a Discord-shaped embed (`embeds[]` + `allowed_mentions: parse=[]` to suppress pings).
- Webhook URL validation in `create_alert` ([`ultros/src/web/api/alerts.rs`](https://github.com/akarras/ultros/blob/feat/price-alerts-phase-2-3/ultros/src/web/api/alerts.rs)) — rejects:
  - Non-`https` schemes
  - Hosts other than `discord.com`, `discordapp.com`, `ptb.discord.com`, `canary.discord.com`
  - Paths not starting with `/api/webhooks/`
- `list_alerts` now reads the actual delivery endpoint via a new `get_first_endpoint_for_alert` DB helper, so the response correctly reflects whether each alert is DM or Webhook (Phase 1 always reported DiscordDm).

### Phase 3 — Frontend (Leptos, 6 commits)

- **API client functions** in [`ultros-app/src/api.rs`](https://github.com/akarras/ultros/blob/feat/price-alerts-phase-2-3/ultros-frontend/ultros-app/src/api.rs): `get_alerts`, `create_alert`, `patch_alert`, `delete_alert`, `get_alert_events`. Adds a `patch_api` helper mirroring `post_api`.
- **Route registration** for `/alerts` in [`lib.rs`](https://github.com/akarras/ultros/blob/feat/price-alerts-phase-2-3/ultros-frontend/ultros-app/src/lib.rs) and a new **UserMenu nav link** with `i::BsBell` icon in [`apps_menu.rs`](https://github.com/akarras/ultros/blob/feat/price-alerts-phase-2-3/ultros-frontend/ultros-app/src/components/apps_menu.rs) (auth-gated, next to Lists).
- **`AlertConfigDrawer` component** ([`components/alert_config_drawer.rs`](https://github.com/akarras/ultros/blob/feat/price-alerts-phase-2-3/ultros-frontend/ultros-app/src/components/alert_config_drawer.rs)): modal form with `WorldPicker`, price threshold input, HQ-only checkbox, delivery radios (DM | Webhook), conditional webhook URL input, toast on success.
- **Bell icon on `ListItemRow`** ([`components/list/list_item_row.rs`](https://github.com/akarras/ultros/blob/feat/price-alerts-phase-2-3/ultros-frontend/ultros-app/src/components/list/list_item_row.rs)) — opens the drawer pre-filled with the item's ID and name. Wired into both view-mode and edit-mode action cells.
- **Alerts page** at `/alerts` ([`routes/alerts.rs`](https://github.com/akarras/ultros/blob/feat/price-alerts-phase-2-3/ultros-frontend/ultros-app/src/routes/alerts.rs)) — two sections:
  - Active rules with enable/disable + delete buttons (round-trip via `patch_alert` / `delete_alert`)
  - Recent fires (last 50) with item name, time, matched price, delivered/error state
  - Reactive refresh on action version change

### Docs

- README "Price Alerts" section updated to describe the UI flow + delivery methods
- Design spec gets an "Implementation status (2026-05-11)" addendum

## How it was built

Same approach as Phase 1: written plan ([`2026-05-11-price-alerts-phase-2-3.md`](https://github.com/akarras/ultros/blob/feat/price-alerts-phase-2-3/docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-11-price-alerts-phase-2-3.md)), executed via `superpowers:subagent-driven-development` over 9 tasks. Notable adaptations:

- **`reqwest` already a direct dep at 0.11 with `rustls-tls`** — no openssl-sys regression
- **Task 2 implementer added the Webhook arm to `create_alert`'s match preemptively** (since Task 1 introduced the new variant), bundling part of Task 3's work earlier
- **`AnySelector` is `Copy`** — explicit `serde_json::to_value(world_selector)` works without borrow or clone
- **`#[allow(clippy::result_large_err)]` on `validate_discord_webhook_url`** — `ApiError` already has a large variant (`DiscordTokenInvalid(PrivateCookieJar<Key>)`); not introduced by this PR
- **`Toasts: Copy`** — closures capture by copy, no `.clone()` needed
- **`tracked_data()` over `xiv_gen_db::data()` directly** — matches codebase convention for reactive locale tracking

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo check -p ultros -p ultros-db -p ultros-api-types -p ultros-app -p migration` passes
- [x] `cargo fmt --check` clean
- [x] `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` (per-crate) clean
- [ ] **Manual smoke test** (needs running server + Discord session — deferred):
  - Log in → navigate to a List → click bell on an item → fill out drawer with `delivery: Discord DM` → submit → verify alert appears at `/alerts`
  - Repeat with `delivery: Webhook URL` (paste a Discord channel webhook) — verify the alert fires post a message to the channel when a listing matches
  - Try invalid webhook URL (e.g., `https://example.com/foo`) → expect 400 with a useful error message
  - Toggle enabled / delete via the rule table — verify state round-trips

## Known follow-ups (not in this PR)

- **Per-list "alert defaults"** UI (small ergonomic add)
- **Top-bar badge** for unread fires (polish)
- **AlertConfigDrawer ad-hoc entry point** (not tied to a List item)
- **`list_alerts` N+1** — Task 3 introduces a per-alert endpoint lookup; should be a JOIN for users with many alerts
- **i18n** for the 14 new English UI strings (folds into the existing i18n sweep)
- **Live state refresh** in `PriceAlertTracker` — alerts created via the API still don't fire until app restart (Phase 1 known gap, separate effort)

## How this fits the roadmap

Phase 2+3 of the Price Alerts feature. After this PR, the only remaining work in the original spec is:
- **Phase 4**: AI-suggested watchlist items + threshold recommendations (separate plan)
- **% drop from median** trigger (requires median tracker, separate plan)

author: merkyorlynn
body:
Five independent commits from a 2026-05-10/11 Lynn engine (Blackwell sm_120) experiment session:

## What's in
1. **`engine/loader.py`** — single-file safetensors fallback for NVFP4 v8-RTN format
2. **`engine/full_forward.py`** — `LYNN_MOE_IMPL` env var for opt-in MoE fast paths (NOT default)
3. **`engine/incremental_decode.py`** — SDPA `enable_gqa=True` replaces explicit `repeat_interleave`
4. **`docs/`** — Phase 3.2 postmortem + STRATEGY updates + bilingual avoidance guide + nvfp4 multi-prompt harness
5. **`engine/incremental_decode.py`** — F2.1 cat-free RoPE (5 cat ops/layer eliminated, byte-exact verified, t/s within noise)

## What's NOT in
- ❌ No default MoE implementation change (still `optimized`)
- ❌ No new Triton kernel wired (`Phase 3.3` cancelled per profiler analysis)
- ❌ No CUDA Graph / functional state refactor (left for DGX, see STRATEGY.md scope hard rule)

## Universal review rule (new in STRATEGY.md)

> Single-prompt PASS does NOT endorse any default-impl change.
> All default switches require N≥14 multi-prompt exact-match gate to pass.

This rule is born from the bmm/indexed_bmm experience this session:
- Single prompt `The capital of France is`: 10/10 token exact match → looked production-ready
- Multi-prompt N=14: 11/14 (78.6%) → 3 prompts diverge on multi-meaning continuations
- Root cause: cuBLAS `gemm` vs `gemmStridedBatched` reduce schedule differs at BF16 ε; cascades through 40 layers

See [docs/PHASE3.2_POSTMORTEM.md](docs/PHASE3.2_POSTMORTEM.md) for the full debugging journey.

## Tested on
- RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (sm_120, 96GB GDDR7), CUDA 12.8, PyTorch 2.8.0+cu128
- Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 (HuggingFace `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8`)
- Multi-prompt N=14 gate, 8 tokens each, 3 impls compared



---

## 📝 知乎工程复盘(2026-05-11)

本 PR 的工程复盘已发布到知乎:

**[从零开始 Qwen 3.6 35B-A3B 写专用推理引擎踩坑心得分享](https://zhuanlan.zhihu.com/p/2036443846322680848)**

mega-post,~15-20k 中文字符,内容覆盖三部分:

- **Phase 2 早期工作**:NumPy / FP8 dequant / single-layer integration / 3 个 invisible bug
- **Phase 3.2 复盘**(本 PR 主体):bmm / indexed_bmm 为什么不能当默认 / Universal review rule(单 prompt PASS 不背书 default 切换)/ BF16 ε 精度坑(cuBLAS `gemm` vs `gemmStridedBatched` reduce schedule 在 40 层 cascade 后翻转)/ F2.1 cat-free RoPE 实测
- **NVFP4 量化路线决策**:为什么从 `compressed-tensors nvfp4-pack-quantized` 切到 `modelopt_fp4` / R6000 dry-run loader silent corruption(unrecognized weight 命名 fallthrough 产生 garbage)/ Phase 4 native NVFP4 接入清单 L1-L5
