author: turdjali
body:
### Motivation
- Improve realism of firearm capture scenes by modeling spent-casing ejection separate from the bore and align cinematic shell trajectories with weapon geometry.
- Expose per-weapon shell ejection offsets so different weapons can eject casings from realistic ports rather than the muzzle.
- Calibrate shoulder-camera and seated/first-person camera tuning to better frame capture cinematics and dice interactions.
- Ensure camera focus/follow priorities behave more deterministically during token/dice/capture flows.

### Description
- Added `shellEjectOffset` entries to `FIREARM_HAND_ATTACH_TUNING` (and a default) for multiple weapon IDs so a dedicated ejection port can be positioned independently of the muzzle.
- Created a `spentCasingEjectionPort` `Object3D` (`shellEject`) in `attachFirearmToRightHand` and returned it alongside `muzzle` and `offhandTarget` for use in capture sequences.
- Updated `matchProjectileDiameterToBarrel` to preserve authored `shellRadius` when present (`shellRadius: profile.shellRadius ?? barrelRadius`) and clarified intent in the comment.
- Implemented shell-ejection cinematics in the capture flow by computing `shellEjectOrigin`, `shellEjectDirection`, `shellRearDirection`, and using those to drive each shell`s world travel and landing instead of always spawning from the muzzle.
- Tuned cinematic camera offsets and muzzle/shoulder placement for firearms and adjusted left-arm IK timing for better contact (`solveSeatedLeftArmContactIK` timing change and camera pose/lift/side adjustments).
- Introduced `LUDO_CAMERA_ACTIVE_FOCUS_PRIORITY` and tightened camera-follow/focus logic by changing follow/force behavior and increasing focus priorities for dice, token movement, and helper flows.
- Small naming and metadata tweaks: named muzzle `muzzleBarrelExit` and shell ejection port `spentCasingEjectionPort`, and ensured `muzzle` exists when used.

### Testing
- Ran the project build with `yarn build` and the app compiled successfully without type or bundling errors.
- Executed the test suite with `yarn test` (unit/integration) and all automated tests passed.
- Performed automated smoke checks against the capture animation paths (shell spawn/update loops) as part of CI and observed no runtime exceptions.

author: martinmarsian
body:
## Summary

- Replaces the dynamic plist generation + `launchctl bootstrap/enable` approach with `SMAppService.agent()`, the modern macOS 13+ API for background agents
- wiredsyncd now runs **independently of the app** — launchd keeps it alive even when Wired 3 is closed, at login, and after system reboots
- wiredsyncd now appears in **System Settings → General → Login Items** so users can see and control it
- The LaunchAgent plist is bundled at `Contents/Library/LaunchAgents/fr.read-write.wiredsyncd.plist` — no more writing a plist to disk at runtime
- The daemon binary runs directly from `Contents/MacOS/wiredsyncd` — no more copying to `~/Library/Application Support/WiredSync/daemon/`
- **Proactive migration**: `ensureDaemonIsCurrentVersion()` now detects the old manually-managed LaunchAgent plist at startup and triggers the full migration automatically, even if the old daemon is still running. Previously the migration only fired on IPC connection failure, meaning an already-running legacy daemon would block the transition indefinitely.
- On first launch after update: old plist and daemon binary are removed, SMAppService takes over
- App updates work cleanly: send shutdown RPC → launchd's `KeepAlive` restarts wiredsyncd automatically with the new binary from the updated bundle

## Why SMAppService?

The old approach required the app to be running to bootstrap the daemon via `launchctl`, which meant sync would stop if the user quit Wired 3. `SMAppService` hands responsibility for the agent lifecycle to launchd, matching how other background sync tools (Dropbox, iCloud, etc.) work on macOS.

## Migration

Automatic on first launch after update:
1. Removes `~/Library/LaunchAgents/fr.read-write.wiredsyncd.plist` (old dynamic plist)
2. Removes `~/Library/Application Support/WiredSync/daemon/wiredsyncd` (old copied binary)
3. Registers via `SMAppService.agent(plistName:).register()`

Sync pairs and all user data in `~/Library/Application Support/WiredSync/` are untouched.

## Test plan

- [ ] Fresh install: wiredsyncd appears in Login Items after first launch
- [ ] Upgrade from pre-SMAppService build: old plist and binary removed automatically, daemon continues running from app bundle
- [ ] Quit Wired 3 — sync continues (check daemon log)
- [ ] Reboot — sync resumes automatically without opening Wired 3
- [ ] App update: shutdown RPC sent, launchd restarts daemon from new bundle path

author: cesarmanzocode
body:
Three coordinated fixes so a request like "imágenes, diagramas y gráficas
OBLIGATORIAS" produces all three in the final .docx instead of only one
image-class output.

1) Mermaid renderer
   - Chromium under the unprivileged container user was crashing with
     "chrome_crashpad_handler: --database is required" because HOME and
     the user-data-dir were unwritable. Dockerfile now provisions a
     dedicated HOME and XDG dirs for studymation and the puppeteer args
     pin --user-data-dir, --disable-crashpad and friends.
   - DiagramRenderer.render now cascades: local mmdc first, then a
     mermaid.ink HTTPS fallback. Preflight returns True whenever any
     renderer is reachable so the orchestrator stops warning when only
     the local binary is broken.

2) Visual auditor
   - Detects explicit user intent (gráficas/diagramas/tablas/etc.) in
     user_notes; scales the placement cap up to ~1 per section and tells
     the LLM in the system prompt that both types are obligatory.
   - If the auditor still omits the requested type, _force_placement
     reserves a slot in the best eligible section so the injector can
     generate it.
   - chart_extraction_system_prompt(force_generation=True) refuses to
     return null when the user asked for charts: synthesises illustrative
     data instead of skipping silently.

3) Image download
   - upload.wikimedia.org was returning 429 for the 3rd image in a row
     and we dropped it. _download_and_normalize_image now retries 429/5xx
     up to 3 times with exponential backoff and honors Retry-After.

Includes regression tests for user-intent detection, scaled placement
caps and the _force_placement fallback.

## Summary

- **Closes SCM-S3-D3** (the deferral from the Messenger PR): introduces a single FastAPI route at `/webhook/{channel_slug}` in `backend/nobla/gateway/channel_webhook_dispatcher.py` that resolves the channel via `get_channel_manager()` and delegates to `adapter.dispatch_webhook(request)`. Replaces the per-channel-route gap that previously left every webhook-mode adapter "webhook-ready but not actually wired."
- **Architecture: Open/Closed via base-contract push-down.** New optional `async dispatch_webhook(request) -> Response` method + `webhook_signature_headers: tuple[str, ...]` class attribute on `BaseChannelAdapter`. Per-channel signature semantics, body parsing, and challenge handling all live INSIDE each adapter — the dispatcher is a 30-line slug-to-adapter resolver, never a per-channel switchyard. Adding a new webhook channel is purely an adapter change going forward.
- **5 webhook adapters covered + 1 intentional carve-out:** Slack (POST-only signing-secret + URL verification in body), WhatsApp + Messenger (Meta-style GET verify + POST X-Hub-Signature-256), Teams (JWT Bearer via Bot Framework). Telegram intentionally inherits the base default (returns 405) — `python-telegram-bot` self-serves via its own internal aiohttp webhook server; carve-out is pinned by a source-grep guard test.

## Commit map (6 commits, 7 cycles — C5+C6 bundled)

body:
## Summary
- preserve string tab ids for `bb-browser open --tab`, including short ids, full CDP target ids, and numeric-looking short ids
- make `open --tab current` navigate the active/current daemon target instead of resolving `current` as a literal tab id
- prefer the short `tab` id in human `open` output while still showing the full target id separately
- fix the fallback short id for newly opened tabs
- add CLI and daemon regressions for the tab-targeting contract, including using returned `open` ids in a follow-up `eval` request

## Scope
This PR keeps the `open` lifecycle behavior unchanged: new tabs are still created in the background and `open` does not wait for page readiness. It only fixes the tab id contract so returned ids and explicit `--tab` values stay usable by the daemon resolver.

## Root cause
The CLI parsed `open --tab` as a number, which rejected full CDP target ids and could turn numeric-looking short ids into tab indexes. The daemon also treated `current` as an ordinary tab reference before the open handler had a chance to navigate the current tab.

## Validation
- pnpm --filter @bb-browser/cli test
- pnpm --filter @bb-browser/daemon test
- pnpm build
- pnpm lint
- pre-commit hook ran pnpm build and pnpm test
- synthetic merge-tree with #212 keeps a single activation helper and no `open` lifecycle changes

author: longcw
body:
## Summary

`session.interrupt()` was a silent no-op when fired before the realtime server had emitted `response.created`. The local `SpeechHandle` was marked interrupted, but `_realtime_reply_task` had already passed its auth-wait block and continued to call `rt_session.generate_reply()`, after which the server produced a response the agent then discarded. Reported in #5642 ([comment](https://github.com/livekit/agents/issues/5642#issuecomment-4417273612)).

Two changes fix it:

- **Activity-side race.** `_realtime_reply_task` now races the `generate_reply` future against `speech_handle._interrupt_fut` via `wait_if_not_interrupted`. On interrupt, the future is cancelled and the task returns.
- **Plugin-side cancel propagation.** Each realtime plugin's `generate_reply` future now wires an `add_done_callback` that, on cancellation, cleans up tracking state and signals the server (or drops the queued send) where the API supports it:
  - OpenAI (and xAI by inheritance): emits `response.cancel`. 
  - Google: calls `interrupt()` to send `activity_start` to Gemini.
  - Phonic: cancels the queued send task (Phonic has no programmatic server-side cancel).
  - Ultravox: sends a deferred barge-in (`urgency=immediate, defer_response=True`).
  - AWS Nova (experimental): cancels the queued send task (Nova handles in-progress interruption automatically).

Added `test_generate_reply_cancellation` in `tests/test_realtime/test_realtime.py` (parameterized over OpenAI/Azure) which cancels a `generate_reply` future immediately and verifies a subsequent `generate_reply` does not hit `conversation_already_has_active_response`.

Fixes #5642

## Summary

Adds an **Anki** download button (top-right toolbar, next to Quiz/Blind/Theme) that exports all Q&A as a tab-separated file Anki Desktop can import directly via `File → Import`.

Each card carries three tag dimensions, designed for targeted interview prep via Anki's filtered decks:

- **Topic** — `python::advanced::decorators` (from section)
- **Level** — `level::mid` + `level::senior` (ranges like `Mid → Senior` expanded into both, so a single-level filter catches mixed cards)

- `src/App.jsx` — adds `Download` icon import, `downloadAnkiDeck` import, and the toolbar button (passes `confidence`/`bookmarks`/`checked` so personal tags reflect current state).

## Summary

This pull request fixes an issue where transitive dependencies incorrectly trigger false version conflicts during package resolution, particularly affecting initial versions. The fix improves the stability and reliability of the dependency resolution process by handling transitive dependency version updates more carefully.

## Changes

**Dependency Graph and Resolution Engine Updates**

- Added a new `getNodeVersion()` method to `PackageDependencyGraphBuilder` to enable lookup of resolved package versions by organization and package name.
- Enhanced `ResolutionEngine` with more defensive dependency graph management during version resolution iterations:
  - When processing initial dependency graphs, the engine now removes dangling nodes before merging transitive dependencies, preventing false version conflicts.
  - When stale auto-locked versions cause incompatibilities, the engine reissues resolution requests with default locking behavior rather than immediately marking nodes as errors, allowing for recovery.
  - When updating resolved packages, the engine skips batch results from removed or replaced nodes and only removes dangling nodes when actual version changes occur, preventing unnecessary cycles.

**Test Coverage Expansion**

- Extended incompatible version scenario testing with nine new test cases (cases 0008–0015), each with detailed documentation describing:
  - Parent transitive dependency upgrades and how they replace child dependencies without false conflicts
  - Locked vs. central repository dependency chains and their interactions
  - Incompatible pre-1.0 child dependency handling during upgrades
  - Behavior across different resolution modes (HARD, MEDIUM, SOFT)

These changes enhance the robustness of package dependency resolution and reduce false positives when managing transitive dependencies across multiple resolution modes.

# Pull Request

## Actor

- Proposed by: agent, based on maintainer-reviewed private governance report
- Implemented by: agent
- Reviewed by: pending human maintainer; maintainer review comment addressed
- Merge authority: maintainer

## Linked Issues

Fixes #19

|---|---:|---|---|
| Add public agent governance roles, labels, identity boundary, and GitHub App adoption notes | #19 | yes | `git diff --check`; release validation |
| Add agent candidate issue template | #19 | yes | file review; release validation |
| Add pull request template with actor, scope, validation, rollback, and human decision fields | #19 | yes | file review; release validation |

## Necessity Assessment

- Why this is needed: the repository already uses issue-first agent-assisted maintenance, but public records do not yet expose the agent/human decision boundary clearly.
- Risk if not fixed: future agent-assisted issues and pull requests continue to look indistinguishable from direct maintainer authorship.
- Why now: before using the next review reports as real maintenance samples.
- Alternatives considered: wait until a GitHub App exists first; rejected because docs, templates, and labels are useful immediately and lower-risk.

- [x] No unrelated opportunistic edits
- [x] Public/private boundary checked
- [x] Documentation updated if needed
- [ ] Release metadata updated if needed

Release metadata is not updated because this is not a release preparation change.

Minimal governance labels were created and verified with `gh label list --repo Huangshier/agent-ecosystem`:

- `source:agent`
- `source:human`
- `triage:accepted`
- `triage:rejected`
- `triage:deferred`

Full `risk:*` / `scope:*` taxonomy is intentionally deferred until the maintenance load justifies it.

Hosted release validation passed after the review follow-up on run `25653631616`.

The MongoDB Go Driver Team is pleased to release version 2.6.0 of the official MongoDB Go Driver.

#### Release Highlights

> \[!IMPORTANT]
> Go Driver v2.6 will be the last minor version to support MongoDB 4.2. Go Driver v2.7 will require MongoDB 4.4 or newer.

This release adds support for MongoDB's [Intelligent Workload Management (IWM)](https://www.mongodb.com/docs/atlas/intelligent-workload-management) and ingress connection rate limiting features. The driver now gracefully handles write-blocking scenarios and optimizes connection establishment during high-load conditions to maintain application availability.

Two new methods of `ClientOptions` are available:

- `SetMaxAdaptiveRetries` - specifies the maximum number of times the driver should retry operations that fail with a server side overload error. If not invoked, the default is 2. `MaxAdaptiveRetries` can also be set through the "maxAdaptiveRetries" URI option (e.g. "maxAdaptiveRetries=5").
- `SetEnableOverloadRetargeting` - specifies whether the driver should enable overload retargeting for operations that fail with a server side overload error. If not invoked, the default is false. `EnableOverloadRetargeting` can also be set through the "enableOverloadRetargeting" URI option (e.g. "enableOverloadRetargeting=true").

body:
## Root cause
Tool discovery worked but every tool call threw `Error: Invalid URL`. The `??` operator only guards against `null`/`undefined` — if `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` is set to `""`, `"undefined"`, or a value without a protocol (e.g. `localhost:3000`), the fallback never triggered and `new URL(path, badValue)` threw.

## Fix
- `resolveBaseUrl()` validates the env var with `new URL()` and uses `u.origin` (always a valid URL), falling back to `https://hawkeye-sterling.netlify.app` on any failure
- `callApi()` wraps URL construction in `try/catch` so a bad path can never throw uncaught — returns a descriptive error object instead

author: wirabelle
body:
## Résumé

### Recette Symfony Flex
- Nouveau dossier `recipes/` avec `index.json`, `manifest.json` et `.mcp.json` template
- Quand un projet hôte déclare l'endpoint privé dans `composer.json` (`extra.symfony.endpoint`), un `composer require --dev quiche-lorraine/code-context` installe automatiquement `.mcp.json` à la racine
- README mis à jour avec la section de configuration du endpoint

### Correctifs des générateurs Markdown

**`entities.md`** (root cause : propriétés `private` filtrées avant que EntityExtractor les voie)
- `EntityExtractor` re-analyse chaque fichier entité avec un config temporaire `include_private=true` via la nouvelle méthode `Config::withIncludePrivate(bool)`
- Les attributs Doctrine des propriétés (`Column`, `Id`, `ManyToOne`…) apparaissent maintenant dans le MD, avec le préfixe `Doctrine\ORM\Mapping\` raccourci
- Nouvelle section **Enums** listant tous les enums du projet avec leurs cases

**`commands.md`** (root cause : dump brut de la string d'attribut)
- `ConsoleExtractor` extrait désormais `name` et `description` de l'attribut `#[AsCommand]` via regex (nommés ou positionnels)
- Rendu : `- **\`app:users:purge-deleted\`** (\`App\Command\PurgeDeletedUsersCommand\`) — Purge deleted users`

**`services.md`** (root cause : seules les entrées YAML explicites étaient listées, pas les milliers de classes autowirées)
- `ServiceExtractor` ignore maintenant les entrées YAML avec `resource:` (wildcards namespace comme `App\:`)
- Deux sections dans le MD : **Configurés** (entrées YAML concrètes) et **Autowirés** (toutes les classes concrètes du scan PHP, groupées par namespace)

### Modèle / Analyseur
- `ClassInfo` : nouveau champ `cases: list<string> = []` pour les noms de cases des enums
- `PhpAstAnalyzer` : détecte `Node\Stmt\EnumCase` dans `buildClassInfo` et peuple `ClassInfo::cases`
- `Config` : nouvelle méthode `withIncludePrivate(bool): self` pour créer une instance avec override ponctuel

## Plan de test
- [ ] Lancer `code-context generate` sur un projet Symfony avec des entités Doctrine privées → `entities.md` doit lister les propriétés avec leurs attributs ORM
- [ ] Vérifier qu'un projet avec des enums voit une section `## Enums` dans `entities.md`
- [ ] Vérifier `commands.md` : format `- **\`name\`** (\`Class\`) — description`
- [ ] Vérifier `services.md` : deux sections, les wildcards YAML absents de "Configurés"
- [ ] Tester l'installation Flex : ajouter l'endpoint dans `composer.json` d'un projet Symfony, puis `composer require --dev quiche-lorraine/code-context`, vérifier que `.mcp.json` est copié

Thanks for your contribution and we appreciate it a lot. The following instructions would make your pull request more healthy and more easily get feedback. If you do not understand some items, don't worry, just make the pull request and seek help from maintainers.

## Motivation

`bfloat16` is useful for AMP training because it has a larger exponent range than `float16`, which can reduce the risk of overflow and `NaN` loss during training.

For Mask2Former and other models that rely on multi-scale deformable attention, supporting a bf16 fallback path would make AMP training more stable and practical, while avoiding changes to the CUDA kernel itself.

## Modification

This PR  add a dtype check in `MultiScaleDeformableAttention`.

The PR would not add bf16 support to the CUDA operator directly. Instead, when the input dtype is `torch.bfloat16`, it would use the existing PyTorch implementation as a fallback.

Dependabot opened three separate `addons/docs-hub` PRs (#4883, #4884, #4885) that, if merged individually, would land mismatched pairs — `react-dom` ahead of `react`, and `@typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin` ahead of `@typescript-eslint/parser`. This consolidates them into one bump that preserves the required version pairing, and additionally fixes the previously-deferred missing-config / lint / typecheck failures in `addons/docs-hub`.

### Dependency changes (`addons/docs-hub/package.json` + lockfile)

- **React pair → 19.2.6**: `react` 19.1.0 → 19.2.6 alongside `react-dom`. Aligns with the rest of the SPA addons (canvas-toolkit already requires 19.2.6 for tldraw).
- **React types pair → 19.2.3**: `@types/react` + `@types/react-dom`.
- **typescript-eslint pair → 8.59.2**: bumps `parser` in lockstep with `eslint-plugin` (27-minor jump).
- **`unist-util-visit` → 5.1.0**: types-only minor.
- **New devDependencies**: `eslint@^9.27.0` and `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y@^6.10.2` (required by the new flat config).

### Tooling fixes

- Added `addons/docs-hub/tsconfig.json` (mirrors chat-spa: `target: ES2020`, `jsx: "react-jsx"`, `strict`, `isolatedModules`). This is what lets `tsc --noEmit` and vitest/rolldown parse `.tsx` correctly.
- Added `addons/docs-hub/eslint.config.js` — flat config that registers `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y` (recommended) plus `@typescript-eslint/eslint-plugin` so the existing `eslint-disable-next-line @typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` pragmas in the source tree resolve to a real rule.
- Removed the now-redundant `esbuild: { jsx: 'automatic' }` workaround from `vitest.config.ts` (the new `tsconfig.json` handles it).

### Source fixes surfaced by the new configs

- `flexsearch-adapter.ts`: store the FlexSearch `Document` instance as `unknown` to sidestep its `DocumentData` index-signature constraint without polluting the public `ManifestEntry` shape, and guard the inner add-loop against the `_index = null` reset path.
- `ContentArea.tsx`: structural cast for the rehype `ElementData` directive fields (`directiveName`, `hProperties`).
- `App.tsx`: cast `rootAttrs` so the `data-theme` attribute is accepted under `React.HTMLAttributes<HTMLDivElement>`.
- `RightTOC.tsx`, `Sidebar.tsx`: drop redundant `role="list"` from `<ul>`.
- `SearchBox.tsx`: add `tabIndex={-1}` and an `onKeyDown` (Enter/Space) handler to the result row that carries `role="option"`.

### Notes

- `assets/dist/docs-hub.js` rebuilt; gzipped bundle ≈ 205.7 KB, under the 250 KB ceiling in `.github/workflows/spa-bundle-size.yml`.
- `npm test` (14 ✓), `npm run typecheck`, `npm run lint`, and `npm run build` all pass cleanly.
- Advisory DB scan returned no vulnerabilities for any new version.
- Merging this should let Dependabot auto-close #4883, #4884, and #4885 as superseded.

author: aristocles
body:
# What changed

\`eh-hae-discovery-card.js\` no longer suppresses the entire card when
\`supportedCount === 0\` if there are undismissed unsupported metrics
pending. It renders a compact footer-only surface in that case.

Fixes #192.

# Why

Issue #170 added a \`supportedCount === 0\` early return to avoid
rendering an accent-bordered card containing nothing but an empty
state + footer. That addressed noise but overshot: once every
catalogue-supported HAE metric has a subscriber (which is the steady
state on any configured instance), the entire card disappears.

If the operator still has undismissed unsupported metrics (vo2_max,
respiratory_rate, etc.) sitting in \`discovered.json\`, they have no
way to dismiss them from Today view. On klebbtest this was 18
unsupported metrics with no accessible dismiss UI — confirmed during
2026-05-11 QA.

# How

One render branch change in \`eh-hae-discovery-card.js\`:

- Bail only when \`supportedCount === 0 && unsupportedCount === 0\`.
- When \`supportedCount === 0 && unsupportedCount > 0\`, return a
  compact shell that just wraps the existing \`_renderUnsupportedFooter\`
  (no headline, no intro, no category list).
- Normal code path unchanged when \`supportedCount > 0\`.

No CSS changes in this PR. The \`.card.footer-only\` class sits on the
wrapper so a future styling pass can shrink the surface if desired,
but the default card shell is already reasonable for this case.

# Testing

New spec \`tests-e2e/discovery-card-footer-only.spec.js\`:

- Loads Today view.
- Asserts \`eh-hae-discovery-card\` is visible.
- Asserts the toggle string (\"N metrics received but not supported
  yet\") renders.
- Expands the footer and asserts the seeded unsupported metric key
  is reachable.

The default E2E seed now writes \`auto-export/discovered.json\` with
one unknown metric (\`e2e_unsupported_metric\`), producing
\`supportedCount=0, unsupportedCount=1\` — the exact condition this PR
fixes.

- [x] Verified the new spec **fails against main** (stashed the fix,
      reran, confirmed 1 failed; restored, confirmed 7 passed).
- [x] \`npm test\` — 819/820 pass locally (same pre-existing Windows-
      local \`no-personal-refs\` flake; CI green)
- [x] \`npm run test:e2e\` — 7/7 pass

# Checklist

- [x] Commit messages follow conventions
- [x] \`CHANGELOG.md\` updated
- [x] Inline comment in \`render()\` explains the three-state guard
- [x] No personal identifiers or hardcoded paths introduced
- [x] No secrets or high-entropy tokens committed

# Follow-up

- #191 (CC embellishment chips don't persist across reload) is
  still open and touches the chat-widget surface. Next on M2.
- A future cosmetic pass could give the \`.card.footer-only\` surface
  a tighter layout — out of scope here.

author: dragonitebot
body:
GH Release: https://github.com/masagrator/SaltyNX/releases/tag/1.8.0

Changes:
```
tl;dr
Mainly technical stuff to fix a rare issue with homebrew/sysmodules hanging while SaltyNX is active.

Full changelog:
- IPC redesign
  - completely remove old libnx code from sysmodule 
    - main reason for using it was to retrieve sdmc handle that can still work after passing to Core, with how current libnx works it is not possible to do that
    - but this was causing rare issues with homebrew where FS would "forget" about homebrew when trying to write to/read from sdcard, resulting in process hanging. This happened only when multiple processes tried to do this at the same time. This change should technically fix the issue.
    - function for retrieving sdmc handle from sysmodule is now stubbed 
  - Add new IPC functions that are just wrappers around libc I/O functions that are exposed by Core (so plugins shouldn't be affected by this change as long as they didn't try to retrieve sdmc handle manually - which was not officially supported)
  - Rewrite most of IPC functions so they work only when request comes from Application with injected Core
  - Logging was redesigned for those calls
  - Since now most of I/O heavy lifting was moved to sysmodule, Cores got smaller
- Remove most of c++ unwinding and abort stuff to reduce sysmodule size
  - This way - after redesigning IPC - sysmodule RAM usage is bigger only by 12 kB
```

author: adhithyan15
body:
Adds **LM00** — the new LM (Language Model) namespace's foundation spec. Defines the abstract `LlmClient` trait every framework component uses to talk to LLMs. Cloud providers (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, Mistral) and local backends (Ollama, llama.cpp, vLLM) implement the same trait. Calling code is provider-agnostic.

## What it specifies

- **`LlmClient` trait**: `complete`, `complete_json`, `stream_complete`, `capabilities`, `identity`.
- **Request / response shapes**: `CompletionRequest`, `CompletionResponse`, `CompletionJsonResponse` with `TokenUsage`, `ProviderIdentity`, `FinishReason`.
- **Polyfills**: JSON-mode (prompt-wrap + parse + validate + retry), tool-use (union-schema JSON), streaming (single-element stream wrap).
- **Error taxonomy**: 8 `LlmError` variants, each carrying provider identity.
- **Retry / rate-limit policy**: `RetryConfig` with configurable defaults, per-request override.
- **Cost and telemetry**: per-call `TokenUsage`, cumulative `CumulativeUsage`, configurable price table.
- **Mock provider**: `MockLlmClient` for deterministic test runs.
- **Audit-trail integration**: every call emits an `LlmCallRecord` with prompt/response hashes for replay matching.
- **Role-based routing**: extractor / renderer / nli_judge / adversary / plausibility roles map to clients, supporting ADJ05's model-independence requirement.

## What it doesn't specify

- Provider implementations (Anthropic, OpenAI, Ollama, mock) — see [LM00a](LM00a-llm-provider-implementations.md), forthcoming.
- IR-generation primitives (extract_ir, render_node, entail, ...) — see [LM00b](LM00b-llm-primitives.md), forthcoming.

## Why a new namespace

The LLM gateway is independent of ADJ. It's infrastructure that ADJ uses, but it can equally power other framework components (probabilistic logic-engine extractors, future agents) without ADJ-specific assumptions baked in.

## Résumé

Remédiation complète des **31 alertes Dependabot ouvertes** (2 critical + 13 high + 10 moderate + 6 low, dont la plus ancienne datait de sept. 2021) → **0 vulnérabilité** restante via `npm audit`.

Stratégie : bumps de dépendances directes dev-only + overrides ciblés sur les transitives qu'on ne peut pas atteindre via les deps directes. Aucune modification du code addon (`addon/` / `app/`).

## Détail des changements

### Bumps directs (dev-only)

| Package | Avant | Après | Pourquoi |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ember-cli` | `~3.28.4` | `~4.12.3` | Dernière version compat avec l'API `bowerDependencies` appelée par ember-source 3.28 (supprimée dès ember-cli 5). |
| `@ember/optional-features` | `^2.0.0` | `^3.0.0` | Drop dépendance `inquirer` ancienne. |
| `@ember/string` | (absent) | `^3.1.1` | Ajouté pour satisfaire le peer de `ember-resolver@10` sur les try-scenarios Ember 4+ (sur 3.28 `Ember.String.*` est bundlé dans `ember-source`, le standalone est inutilisé). |
| `@ember/test-helpers` | `^2.4.2` | `^2.9.6` | Patch embroider build (`ember-cli-htmlbars` resolution). |
| `@release-it/keep-a-changelog` | `^2.2.2` | `^7.0.0` | Compat release-it 19. |
| `ember-auto-import` | `^2.2.0` | `^2.10.0` | Patches mineurs. |
| `ember-cli-babel` | `7.26.11` (pin strict) | `^7.26.11` (dé-pin) | Lever le pin strict pour résolution propre des `@babel/*` transitifs. |
| `ember-qunit` | `^6.0.0` | `^6.2.0` | Aligné avec test-helpers 2.9. |
| `release-it` | `^14.5.0` | `^19.2.4` | Drop `lodash`, `parse-url` (CRITICAL), `parse-path`, `form-data` (CRITICAL), `got`, `semver` chains. |

### Overrides (transitives résiduelles)

```json
"undici": "^7.24.5",
"@babel/runtime": "^7.26.10",
"@babel/helpers": "^7.26.10",
"tmp": "^0.2.5",
"got": "^11.8.6",
"diff": "^8.0.3",
"ansi-html": "npm:ansi-html-community@^0.0.8",
"braces": "^3.0.3",
"micromatch": "^4.0.8",
"markdown-it": "^14.1.1",
"clean-css": "^5.3.3"
```

Tous load-bearing (vérifié `npm ls <pkg>` post-bumps) : `got` via `ember-try`, `tmp` via `@embroider/compat` + `ember-cli-babel`, `diff` via `ember-cli@4`, `undici` via `release-it@19`, etc.

### Toolchain Node 16 → 20

- `engines.node`: `12.* || 14.* || >= 16` → `^20.9.0 || ^22.0.0`
- `volta.node`: `16.15.0` → `20.19.0`
- `.github/workflows/main.yml`: `NODE_VERSION` `16` → `20`

Pas d'impact runtime pour les apps consommatrices — l'addon publie du code transpilé. Impact **contributeur-only** : ceux qui clonent le repo doivent passer en Node 20+ (voir CHANGELOG).

## Vérifications locales

| Check | Résultat |
|---|---|
| `npm audit` | ✅ 0 vulnerabilities |
| `npm run lint` | ✅ pass |
| `ember test` (47 tests) | ✅ 47/47 |
| `ember try:one ember-lts-3.20` | ✅ pass |
| `ember try:one ember-lts-3.24` | ✅ pass |
| `ember try:one ember-classic` | ✅ pass |
| `ember try:one ember-default-with-jquery` | ✅ pass |
| `ember try:one ember-release` | ⚠️ fail (pré-existant sur master — ember-source 6.11 + ember-resolver 10 incompat `@ember/string`) |
| `ember try:one embroider-safe` | ⚠️ fail (pré-existant sur master — même erreur que ci-dessus) |
| `release-it --dry-run` | ✅ config parsée, changelog généré (7.1.0 → 7.1.1) |

Les deux scénarios qui échouent ont été testés sur master pour confirmer qu'ils sont **pré-existants** et non introduits par cette PR.

> **⚠️ Changement de workflow pour les releases futures**
>
> `@release-it/keep-a-changelog` passe de v2 (validation laxiste) à v7 (validation stricte). À partir de cette PR, **toute release exige une entrée non-vide sous `## [Unreleased]` dans `CHANGELOG.md`** — sinon release-it échoue avec `ERROR There are no entries under "Unreleased" section in CHANGELOG.md.`
>
> Cette PR contient déjà une entrée Unreleased (CVE remediation + Node bump), donc la prochaine release sera débloquée. Mais le réflexe à acquérir : ajouter une ligne au CHANGELOG avant tout `release-it`.
>
> En complément, `release-it` lui-même saute de 14 à 19 (5 majors). `--dry-run` passe, mais un smoke-test du flow release réel est conseillé à la première vraie release après merge.

## Test plan

- [x] CI GitHub : tous les jobs verts (lint, test, percy, floating, try-scenarios)
- [x] Percy : aucune régression visuelle (review humaine sur dashboard Percy)
- [ ] Dependabot : 0 alerte ouverte après merge

## Hors-scope

- Upgrade Ember 3.28 → 5.x : breaking pour consommateurs, à traiter dans une PR dédiée.
- ESLint 7 → 8 / Prettier 2 → 3 : pas CVE-driven, séparable.
- Versions des GitHub Actions (`checkout@v3`, `setup-node@v3`...) : EOL mais pas CVE — Dependabot les gérera.

body:
This adds an Android app for capturing input from a Bluetooth/HID barcode scanner such as the YHD-1100D and sending scan data to a configurable backend. The app supports optional expiry/manufacture dates, quantity, and API-driven location selection from branch/floor/shelf/box hierarchies.

- **Scanner capture workflow**
  - Adds a single-screen Android form optimized for HID-style scanner input into a focused barcode field
  - Supports optional metadata fields for expiry date, manufacture date, and item quantity
  - Keeps submission separate from scan input so operators can enrich the record before sending

- **Configurable backend integration**
  - Adds persisted settings for:
    - scan submission URL
    - locations lookup URL
  - Sends scan payloads as JSON to the configured endpoint

- **Hierarchical location support**
  - Adds location loading from a remote API
  - Parses nested location trees for:
    - `branches -> floors -> shelves -> boxes`
  - Also supports direct floor/shelf roots when the API does not include the full hierarchy
  - Submits the selected terminal location plus its resolved path

- **Core data model / parsing**
  - Introduces dedicated models for:
    - app settings
    - location nodes/types
    - scan submission payloads
  - Adds normalization logic for optional fields and flexible location payload formats

- **Project bootstrap**
  - Creates a minimal single-module Android project with Gradle wrapper and app resources
  - Documents the supported workflow in `README.md`

Example payload produced by the new submission flow:

```json
{
  "barcode": "4012345678901",
  "expireDate": "2026-01-31",
  "manufactureDate": "2025-12-10",
  "itemQuantity": 7,
  "location": {
    "id": "box-2",
    "name": "Box 2",
    "type": "box",
    "path": "Main branch > Floor 2 > Shelf 9 > Box 2"
  }
}
```

body:
### Motivation
- Unify the Pool Royale lounge to a single Murlan-style table with two chairs so both human players visually share the same table and sit on their own chairs. 
- Match human seating/pose and motion to the Murlan Royale reference and make Soldier fallback rigs read and walk more naturally and slightly slower. 
- Replace the placeholder ball floor blobs with HDRI-driven lighting and real shadowing so balls, players and table receive natural shadows from the environment. 
- Slightly reduce spin scaling and increase shot power to produce stronger but more controlled cue-ball behavior.

### Description
- Consolidated lounge furniture and seating: created a shared lounge table and adjusted chair placement/roots so both players use the same table; added `POOL_ROYALE_SHARED_LOUNGE_CHAIR_Z` and related layout changes in `webapp/src/pages/Games/PoolRoyale.jsx`. 
- Human rig / seated pose and walk tuning: updated seated pose to match Murlan reference, adjusted bone rotations for legs/arms, increased right-finger grip weight for held-cue, and slowed/weighted walk animation timing and `Walk` timescale scaling in `webapp/src/pages/Games/shared/humanRigCore.js`. 
- Held-cue behavior: made each human rig keep its own visible held cue and continuously align it from back→tip (`setFromBackTip`) so players always display their cue stick (`PoolRoyale.jsx`). 
- Shadows / lighting: removed the fake ball floor shadow discs, enabled `renderer.shadowMap.enabled`, made balls cast shadows (`mesh.castShadow = true`), added an HDRI floor shadow receiver mesh and tuned lighting preset intensity scaling so HDRI remains dominant (`PoolRoyale.jsx`). 
- Physics/tuning: reduced global spin scale (`SPIN_GLOBAL_SCALE`), increased `SHOT_GLOBAL_POWER_SCALE` (so strikes feel slightly stronger), and reduced some walk profile speeds (human logic profile `rpm-current.walkSpeed`) in `PoolRoyale.jsx` and supporting constants. 
- Misc: adjusted mobile lighting rig intensities and exposed the HDri floor shadow receiver and lighting preset multiplier used when applying lighting settings (`PoolRoyale.jsx`). 

### Testing
- Ran `npm run build` (Vite production build) which completed successfully and produced `dist/` assets. 
- Ran `git diff --check` (no whitespace/merge errors) and committed the changes. 
- Attempted an automated UI render capture with Playwright after installing browser dependencies (`npx playwright install` / `npx playwright install-deps chromium`), but the headless Chromium screenshot of the full Pool Royale WebGL scene timed out in this environment despite installing deps (succeeded in installing browsers/deps but screenshot capture failed due to headless rendering/timeout issues).

author: fhntvv
body:
## RFO — three distinct failure modes shipped in v0.4.0

### 1. Primary machine — dual-process collision (high confidence)

Two `windowmanager` processes were running simultaneously after the in-place upgrade: an old `.build/debug/windowmanager --debug` plus the `/Applications/WindowManager.app` build. Neither was v0.4.0 — the just-built binary was never installed (`launchd` plist points at `/usr/local/bin/windowmanager`, which doesn't exist on disk).

Both processes created `CGEventTap`s on `.cgSessionEventTap` / `.headInsertEventTap`. Either tap consuming a key it shouldn't dropped that key system-wide. No singleton check.

### 2. Second machine — Accessibility-wait zombie + EUI toggle risk

`AppCompositionRoot.init` blocked the main thread in `Thread.sleep(1)` until `AXIsProcessTrusted()` flipped. `AXIsProcessTrustedWithOptions(prompt: true)` only fires once per process lifetime — if the user dismissed the prompt, the process became a zombie until manually killed. Run loop was dead; no AppKit / system notifications could drive recovery.

In addition, v0.4.0 wrote `AXEnhancedUserInterface = false` to `AXUIElementCreateApplication(0)` whenever `AXUIElementGetPid` failed (never checked), targeting kernel_task/launchd. Combined with the 6 s default AX messaging timeout on a wedged target, this was a plausible (though unconfirmed) path to symptoms reported as "keyboard frozen."

### 3. Chrome / Chromium-based apps don't get a focused window at all

This wasn't visible until field testing. `getFocusedWindow` asked the AX framework `kAXFocusedApplicationAttribute` on the systemwide element. For raw Chrome (and any Chromium app not wrapped by Electron's Cocoa shell), that returns `kAXErrorNoValue` (-25212) because Chrome's AX tree is lazy-initialized — but the systemwide query won't yield an app element until Chrome has registered with AX. Closed loop.

## Fix — four commits

1. **PID guard + bounded AX messaging timeout.** `AXUIElementGetPid`'s return is checked; on failure or `pid <= 0` the entire app-element / EUI / zoom path is skipped. `AXUIElementSetMessagingTimeout(0.5)` on both the window element and the app element so a wedged target can't tie up the operation queue or hold the deferred `EUI=true` restore for 6 s.
2. **Pidfile singleton + structured startup log.** `~/Library/Application Support/com.windowmanager/instance.pid` with `kill(pid, 0)` liveness check. Bare terminal-launched dev builds (the actual stale process found in the field) are detected — `NSRunningApplication` would miss them. Startup log line emits `version pid executable bundle` so the running build is identifiable.
3. **Event-driven Accessibility wait.** `NSApp.run()` is reached immediately. TCC grant flips are observed via `DispatchSource.makeFileSystemObjectSource` on `~/Library/Application Support/com.apple.TCC` plus a 2 s safety Timer. Heavy services come up automatically on first observed grant, no relaunch.
4. **NSWorkspace-based foreground app resolution.** `getFocusedWindow` now uses `NSWorkspace.shared.frontmostApplication` to obtain the PID via AppKit (independent of AX), then synthesizes the AX element with `AXUIElementCreateApplication(pid)`. If `kAXFocusedWindowAttribute` fails, both `AXManualAccessibility` and `AXEnhancedUserInterface` are written to wake the Chromium AX tree and the read is retried. Verified working against Chrome.

Diagnostic logging added throughout: every `getFocusedWindow` outcome (success + failure) now records PID, bundle ID, app name, wakeUp flag, and AXError code. The blind-debugging loop that ate most of this PR's iterations was the missing logging — that was the meta-bug.

## Verified end-to-end

- Chrome: `ctrl+option+left` moves the window. Log shows `getFocusedWindow ok pid=... bundle=com.google.Chrome wokeUp=true` on first hotkey of a fresh Chrome launch, then `wokeUp=false` thereafter.
- Safari, Finder, kitty, Terminal: continue to work, no regression.
- `swift test`: 107/107 passing.

## Out of scope (intentionally)

- Developer ID signing. Stale-CDHash-after-rebuild remains the root cause of the painful regrant loop, but personal-tool repos without an Apple Developer subscription can't be helped here.
- `executeDisplayMove` shrink → move → resize refactor (still flagged TODO from v0.4.0).
- `install-launchagent.sh` upgrade hygiene.

author: oskar-ott
body:
## The complaint
> *my day and the job interface for tradies and leading hands still sucks not fixed*

Earned. I'd been doing polish PRs instead of looking at what a worker actually sees on a phone. Two concrete problems, two concrete fixes — net subtraction.

## What was wrong

**My Day Log Hours card** had THREE ways to enter the same number:
- Hours stepper (− / + / typed)
- Minute pills (00 / 15 / 30 / 45)
- Quick chips (4h / 6h / 7.5h / 8h / 9h)

For a once-a-day action that's cognitive overhead, not flexibility.

**Per-job dashboard for tradies + LH** stacked 7 sections (Compliance / Continue / KPIs / Quick actions / Needs attention / In progress / Module shortcuts) before the worker could even see *\"Open work areas\"*. The brief target is < 8s to a first task update; current flow is 5 taps + a scroll.

**Compliance banner** showed amber for any tag expiring within 30 days → permanent banner on every job with active tags, even when nothing was actually overdue.

## What changed

### My Day — chip-first
- New default: just chips + an *\"Other ↓\"* fallback. Tap **8h** → Save → done.
- *\"Other\"* expands the hours+minutes editor for rare custom values. Auto-expands when editing a non-standard entry so the controls match what's saved.
- Quiet visual style on the Other chip (muted, smaller) so it reads as an escape hatch, not a peer of the duration buttons.

### Per-job dashboard — drop the noise for workers
- Tradies + LHs no longer see KPI grid, Continue card, Module shortcuts, or In progress section.
- Admin keeps the full dashboard. Role-aware via `body.role-*` classes.
- Worker layout now: optional compliance banner → **Open work areas** full-width yellow CTA (56px, 16px bold) → Log hours + Raise snag side-by-side → Needs attention.
- At most 4 things on screen before the path to a task is visible.

### Compliance banner — tightened trigger
- Now: only renders **red** when something is past expiry.
- Approaching-due lives in the T&T tab badge (admin's problem), not as a chronic banner on every worker's dashboard.

## Out of scope, deliberately
- Backend changes
- Admin dashboard
- Snag modal, hours sheet, work-areas list — all touched in earlier PRs and working
- Adding new sections — this PR is purely a cut

## Test plan
- [ ] Open My Day as tradie — Log Hours card shows chips + 8h pressed by default + *\"Other ↓\"* on the right
- [ ] Tap 7.5h → *\"Save 7h 30m\"* button updates; Other panel stays hidden
- [ ] Tap *\"Other ↓\"* → hours stepper + minute pills appear; type 7 + tap 15 → Save 7h 15m
- [ ] Re-open Log Hours for an edited 7h 15m entry → Other panel auto-expanded, no chip pressed
- [ ] Open `/jobs/<id>` as tradie — see compliance banner (if any), full-width yellow **Open work areas → N**, Log hours + Raise snag below it, attention list — no KPI grid, no Continue card
- [ ] Same as LH — same layout
- [ ] As admin — full dashboard back (KPIs + Continue + Modules visible)
- [ ] Tag expiring within 30 days but not yet expired → NO banner. Tag past expiry → red banner

author: alinclamba
body: Fixes [VIDP-242](https://linear.app/a8c/issue/VIDP-242/videopress-add-new-video-button-disappears-after-first-uploaded-video) ## Context Two recent user reports in Zendesk (11192950-zd-a8c, 11201391-zd-a8c). On the legacy VideoPress admin dashboard, the "Add new video" button disappears once videos exist in the library. Got p1778325739637059/1778323869.151139-slack-C02LT75D3 from the VideoPress team for a Bug Blitz fix. ## Root cause At standard viewports, the hero collapses to 1px. The shared `.section-hero` has `overflow: hidden`, which in a flex column lets `min-height: auto` resolve to 0. All shrink pressure from siblings lands on the hero, which clamps to 0 and clips the button. Recent regression from PR #48244 (base-styles v1.2.0). My Jetpack had a similar regression fixed in PR #48578. ## Fix Wrap each `` in a local div with `flex-shrink: 0`. Shared component untouched, no blast radius on other admin pages using it (Backup, Search, Publicize, Protect, ~12 sites). Legacy code will be replaced by modernization work in #48506 at Phase 9 cutover. This fix goes away with it. **Note on the diff:** the TSX file shows 119 line changes due to JSX re-indentation when adding the wrappers. Toggle "Hide whitespace changes" in the GitHub diff view to see the actual fix: 2 wrappers + 1 Prettier-mandated multi-line reformat on `jp-admin-notices`. ## Testing Tested live on JN sandbox with the fix deployed: - Populated default viewport (1440x800) ✓ - Populated narrow viewport (1280x720) ✓ - Populated 80% zoom ✓ - Empty state unchanged ✓ - Build + lint + Stylelint clean **Not tested:** other admin pages using `AdminSectionHero`, mobile viewports, many videos (5+). **Test site:** https://ocelot-of-hydrozoans.jurassic.ninja/wp-admin/admin.php?page=jetpack-videopress ## Before / After The bug in numbers: at default viewport (1440x800) on the populated dashboard, the hero collapses to **1px** height while its content needs **285px**. That's the entire "Add new video" button (and storage meter) clipped out of view. **BEFORE (bug active):** baseline state. Hero collapsed to 1px, 284px of content clipped, including the upload button. Overlay shows the computed CSS values that cause it. **AFTER (fix applied via local override):** same page, `flex-shrink: 0` applied to wrapper. Hero renders at full 285px, button visible. Overlay shows `overflow: hidden` is preserved (we don't break the shared component's semantics). **Live verification on JN with the deployed fix:** dashboard after the fix was actually shipped to the sandbox, populated state, default viewport. ## Notes for reviewers This PR was built using an AI-assisted workflow (Claude Code + Chrome DevTools MCP for investigation and testing). I drove the process, AI helped with the heavy lifting on code investigation and live verification. Happy to walk through the workflow if useful.

body:
## Summary

Extracts the three inline gesture-listener objects out of `IsiActivity` into a new `ReaderGestureHandler` class, following the Host/Actions interface pattern established by REM-07's `VerseActionModeController`. Implements REM-06 from `docs/tech-debt-remediation.md`.

The handler combines three listeners that the reader screen wires up to its layout — `TwofingerLinearLayout.Listener` (split-root pinch + swipe), `GotoButton.FloaterDragListener` (drag-from-goto), and `Floater.Listener` (final ari selection) — and reads state through `ReaderGestureHost` / triggers actions through `ReaderGestureActions`. The handler holds no Activity reference.

- New files (3, in `Alkitab/src/main/java/yuku/alkitab/base/widget/`): `ReaderGestureHandler.kt` (125 lines), `ReaderGestureHost.kt` (38 lines), `ReaderGestureActions.kt` (27 lines).
- `IsiActivity.kt`: −81 net lines (2452 → 2371). Gesture-local state (`startFontSize`, `startDx`, `moreSwipeYAllowed`, `chapterSwipeCellWidth`, `floaterLocationOnScreen`) moves to the handler; 13 lines of host/actions overrides remain as the seam.

## Behavior preservation

All gesture behavior preserved verbatim:
- Pinch zoom (2f–42f clamp) → `Preferences.setFloat` + `applyPreferences()` + `textAppearancePanel?.displayValues()`
- One-finger left/right swipe → next/prev chapter
- Two-finger horizontal drag → multi-chapter skip with 24dp cell width
- Two-finger vertical drag → fullscreen toggle (still paired with `leftDrawer.handle.setFullScreen` under the new single `setFullScreenWithDrawerHandle` action, preserving the original pairing in the gesture path)
- Goto-button drag → opens the floater, hit-tests in floater-local coords, drops to jump to ari

## Test plan

- [x] `./gradlew assemblePlainDebug` passes
- [x] `./gradlew testPlainDebugUnitTest testPlainReleaseUnitTest` passes (all existing unit tests green; no new tests required — no characterization tests for gestures pre-existed)

body:
## Summary

Call malloc_trim(0) after each tool dispatch in handle_function_call() to return freed heap pages to the OS.

## Why

On long CLI sessions (100+ turns), Python heap can grow to 400+ MB RSS. malloc_trim(0) tells glibc to release freed pages.

## Implementation
- _maybe_trim_memory() via ctypes
- Called after every registry.dispatch()
- Linux-only, best-effort, silent failure

## Tested
- Syntax-validated in container
- Does not break tool dispatch
- 13 lines total

body:
## Summary

- Drop `export * from \"./editor\"` from `@tangle-network/sandbox-ui`'s root barrel (`src/index.ts`).
- `@tangle-network/sandbox-ui/editor` subpath is unchanged — consumers migrate from `import { TiptapEditor } from \"@tangle-network/sandbox-ui\"` to `import { TiptapEditor } from \"@tangle-network/sandbox-ui/editor\"`.
- Reduces root-barrel `.d.ts` surface (drops `@tiptap/*`, `yjs`, `@hocuspocus/provider` type chains from the default-import).
- Bumps `0.15.4 → 0.16.0` (breaking on root barrel; subpath unchanged).

## Problem → Solution

The editor surface is specialized collaboration tooling (Tiptap, yjs, hocuspocus), not a generic UI primitive. Exporting it from the package root drags heavy type chains into every consumer's default import, even those who only use other subpaths. The `@tangle-network/sandbox-ui/editor` subpath already exists and is the correct entrypoint for editor consumers; this PR routes the surface exclusively through it.

This closes the downstream half of a hygiene gap originally deferred during the Phase C re-export bridge migration (ISS-34). The upstream half — same shape on `@tangle-network/ui`'s own root barrel — is tracked separately.

## Impact

- **External (npm) consumers** using `import { TiptapEditor } from \"@tangle-network/sandbox-ui\"`: breaking. Migration recipe in CHANGELOG.
- **Internal monorepo consumers**: zero affected. Verified via grep across `blueprint-agent`, `agent-dev-container`, `tangle-website`, `tcloud`, `tangle-router`, `sandbox-ui` — no file imports from the `@tangle-network/sandbox-ui` root barrel for any editor symbol.

## Verification (all green locally)

- [x] `pnpm typecheck` — clean.
- [x] `pnpm build` — clean.
- [x] `pnpm test` — 247/247 passed across 19 files.
- [x] `pnpm test:bridge` — 13/13 re-export identity assertions pass (editor symbols still resolve `===` between `/editor` subpath and `@tangle-network/ui/editor`).
- [x] `dist/index.d.ts` no longer mentions `tiptap` / `hocuspocus` / `TiptapEditor` / `EditorToolbar` / `DocumentEditorPane` / `EditorProvider`.
- [x] `dist/editor.d.ts` still exports the full editor surface.
- [x] Runtime: `\"TiptapEditor\" in require(\"dist/index.js\")` → `false`; `\"TiptapEditor\" in require(\"dist/editor.js\")` → `true`. `Button` and `CommandPreview` still present at root.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI green on the PR.
- [ ] Post-merge: `npm view @tangle-network/sandbox-ui@0.16.0 version` returns `0.16.0`.
- [ ] Post-merge: in a throwaway install, `import { TiptapEditor } from \"@tangle-network/sandbox-ui\"` fails to resolve; `import { TiptapEditor } from \"@tangle-network/sandbox-ui/editor\"` resolves.

## Out of scope

Not touching the other shim re-exports at root (`./chat`, `./run`, `./files`, `./openui`, `./markdown`, `./auth`, `./tool-previews`). Editor is the heaviest case (tiptap+yjs+hocuspocus); broader root-barrel cleanup is a separate decision.

author: mateeullahmalik
body:
## Summary

Fixes the **empty active set deadlock** in the audit module: when all supernodes are simultaneously POSTPONED, the existing peer-port recovery rule in `shouldRecoverAtEpochEnd` becomes unsatisfiable by construction (zero probers ⇒ zero peer reports ⇒ no SN can recover). The chain cannot self-heal and recovery requires every validator key holder to perform a manual `deregister + re-register` cycle out-of-band — a distributed coordination problem on mainnet.

This PR adds a **bootstrap-recovery exception**: when the epoch's anchored active set is empty AND the POSTPONED SN submits a compliant self host-report, the SN recovers to ACTIVE.

## Why this matters (live mainnet evidence)

Queried `lumera.audit.v1.Query/Params` at mainnet height 5,001,129:

```
required_open_ports:            [4444, 4445, 8002]
consecutive_epochs_to_postpone: 1     ← one missed epoch postpones
peer_port_postpone_threshold_percent: 100
epoch_length_blocks: 400              (~40 min epochs)
```

Current state: **15 ACTIVE / 11 POSTPONED / 2 DISABLED** — thin active margin.

**Realistic upgrade-day trigger:** an upgrade-halt window plus rolling restart lag of >40 min for a subset of SNs ⇒ those SNs miss one epoch ⇒ POSTPONED in lockstep. If the surviving active set drops to zero, the deadlock locks in permanently.

Two **governance escape hatches that LOOK viable but DON'T WORK** were verified on devnet 2026-05-08 (gov proposal 33 PASSED on-chain but silently no-op'd):
- `MsgUpdateParams` with `required_open_ports=[]` is silently re-filled to defaults by `Params.WithDefaults()` (`x/audit/v1/types/params.go:406-407`)
- Even if step 1 were bypassed, `Params.Validate()` line 619 rejects empty list

The deadlock is a real protocol-level design gap, not a devnet quirk.

## What changed

`x/audit/v1/keeper/enforcement.go::shouldRecoverAtEpochEnd` — adds an 11-line branch that fires when `GetEpochAnchor(epochID).ActiveSupernodeAccounts` is empty, after the existing storage-truth / action-finalization redirects and after `selfHostCompliant`. A misbehaving SN cannot self-recover via this branch — self-compliance still gates it.

## Invariants preserved

| Invariant | Status |
|---|---|
| Determinism | ✓ Reads existing deterministic state (`EpochAnchor`) frozen at epoch start |
| Cosmos replay-safety | ✓ No new external calls, no wall-clock, no map iteration |
| Storage-truth recovery semantics | ✓ Redirect to `shouldRecoverFromStorageTruthPostponement` runs first, bootstrap branch NOT taken |
| Action-finalization recovery semantics | ✓ Redirect to `shouldRecoverFromActionFinalizationPostponement` runs first, bootstrap branch NOT taken |
| Self-compliance gate | ✓ Still mandatory before the bootstrap branch |
| Legacy peer-port recovery (non-empty anchor) | ✓ Unchanged when anchor has ≥1 active account |

## Test matrix (5 cells, all PASS)

`x/audit/v1/keeper/enforcement_empty_active_set_test.go`:

| Anchor active count | Self-report | Self-compliant | Peer all-open | Expected | Test |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | yes | yes | n/a | recover ✓ | `TestEnforceEpochEnd_EmptyActiveSet_PostponedRecoversViaBootstrapException` |
| 0 | no | n/a | n/a | NO recover | `TestEnforceEpochEnd_EmptyActiveSet_NoSelfReport_NoRecover` |
| 0 | yes | no (disk > min) | n/a | NO recover | `TestEnforceEpochEnd_EmptyActiveSet_NonCompliantSelf_NoRecover` |
| ≥1 | yes | yes | no | NO recover (legacy) | `TestEnforceEpochEnd_NonEmptyActiveSet_NoPeerObs_NoRecover` |
| no anchor | yes | yes | n/a | NO recover (legacy) | `TestEnforceEpochEnd_NoEpochAnchor_FallsThroughToLegacyPath` |

The pre-existing test `TestEnforceEpochEnd_EmptyActiveSet_PostponedCannotRecover` that asserted the deadlock is inverted to the new contract (`Times(2)` recovery instead of `Times(0)`).

## Risk

**LOW.** The bootstrap branch is reachable only when:
1. No storage-truth postponement at this epoch, AND
2. No action-finalization postponement at this epoch, AND
3. SN submitted a compliant self host-report, AND
4. Epoch anchor exists AND active set is empty

In any normal operating state (≥1 ACTIVE), the branch is skipped and the legacy peer-port path runs unchanged. Determinism preserved.

## Rollback

`git revert <commit>`. The legacy peer-port deadlock returns; recovery still possible via the documented `deregister + re-register` procedure (internal runbook: `lumera-supernode-postponed-recovery`).

## Migration / upgrade notes

None. Pure logic change in `EnforceEpochEnd`'s recovery branch. No state-key changes, no proto changes, no consensus version bump. Safe to ship as a minor-version logic patch (e.g. v1.20.x). Activates the moment the upgraded binary runs — no proposal-side toggle required.

## IBC / interop

N/A — audit module is not IBC-bound.

## Devnet rehearsal

Unit-level test matrix covers the bootstrap branch + the legacy-preservation cases with mocked supernode keeper. Live devnet rehearsal (force all SNs POSTPONED, wait for next epoch end, verify auto-recovery without manual deregister/register) is planned as part of the v1.20 upgrade-rehearsal gate.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- **PR-B** (deferred): allow governance to clear `RequiredOpenPorts` via a sentinel value. Currently blocked by `Params.WithDefaults` silently re-filling the list. With PR-A landed, this is less urgent.
- **PR-C** (deferred): bump `ConsecutiveEpochsToPostpone` default from 1 to 3 (or enforce a floor in `Params.Validate`). Reduces the probability of triggering the empty-set condition. Can be folded into the v1.12.0 upgrade handler (proposal not yet on chain) to apply at activation without a separate gov proposal.

## Files changed

- `x/audit/v1/keeper/enforcement.go` — +11 lines, bootstrap branch
- `x/audit/v1/keeper/enforcement_empty_active_set_test.go` — test matrix

author: mluena
body:
# Description

 Adds cross-subdomain Single Sign-On between MRTT and GMW. On app load MRTT silently checks for an active GMW session via a hidden iframe pointed at `/api/auth/sso/authorize`. If GMW has a session it 302s back to a silent-callback page with a `code`, which is `postMessage`-d to the parent window and exchanged for an
 MRTT token via `/api/auth/sso/exchange`. New MRTT logins (email/password) call `/api/auth/sso/sync` to set the shared cookie on GMW. Logout clears the shared cookie via `/api/auth/sso/logout`.

 Token is kept in React state only (no `localStorage`), removing the previous `useLocalStorage` flow. The Axios interceptor now reads the in-memory token via `setAuthToken` / `getAuthToken`.

 Depends on the corresponding GMW endpoints: `/api/auth/sso/authorize`, `/api/auth/sso/exchange`, `/api/auth/sso/sync`, `/api/auth/sso/logout`.

 Requires `REACT_APP_GMW_URL` env var pointing to the GMW base URL.

 Fixes # (issue)

 ## Type of change

 - [x] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality)
 - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)
 - [ ] Breaking change
 - [ ] This change requires a documentation update

 # Instructions

 1. Set `REACT_APP_GMW_URL` in `.env` (e.g. `https://staging.globalmangrovewatch.org`).
 2. Ensure GMW is running with the SSO endpoints deployed and both apps share a parent domain (e.g. `*.globalmangrovewatch.org`) so the SSO cookie is visible to both.
 3. `pnpm install && pnpm start`.

 # How Has This Been Tested?

 - [ ] **Silent SSO from GMW → MRTT**: Log in on GMW, open MRTT in a new tab → land authenticated on `/sites` without typing credentials.
 - [ ] **No GMW session**: Open MRTT in a clean browser → silent check times out (~4s), user sees login page.
 - [ ] **MRTT login → GMW**: Sign in via email/password on MRTT → open GMW → confirm shared session cookie is set and GMW recognizes user.
 - [ ] **Logout clears both**: Click logout in MRTT → confirm `/api/auth/sso/logout` is called and both apps return to logged-out state.
 - [ ] **URL `?code=` exchange**: Visit MRTT with `?code=<valid>` (full redirect flow) → code is consumed, URL is cleaned, session established.
 - [ ] **Token not persisted**: Refresh MRTT after login → re-bootstraps via silent SSO (not from `localStorage`).
 - [ ] **Iframe guard**: `useAuth` bootstrap skips when `window.top !== window.self` so the silent-callback iframe does not loop.

 # Checklist:

 - [ ] My code follows the style guidelines of this project
 - [ ] I have performed a self-review of my own code
 - [ ] I have commented my code, particularly in hard-to-understand areas
 - [ ] I have made corresponding changes to the documentation
 - [ ] My changes generate no new warnings
 - [ ] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
 - [ ] New and existing unit tests pass locally with my changes
 - [ ] Any dependent changes have been merged and published in downstream modules

 Files Touched (for reviewers)

 - src/hooks/sso.ts (new) — silentSsoCheck, exchangeCode, syncSession, ssoLogout, readAndStripCode, postSilentCallbackResult.
 - src/hooks/useAuth.js — bootstrap flow: read ?code=, else silent iframe check, else show login. In-memory state only.
 - src/views/Auth/SsoSilentCallback.js (new) — iframe target that posts the code to parent.
 - src/views/Auth/LoginForm.js — calls syncSession(token) after successful email/password login.
 - src/components/Header/HeaderMenu.js — logout calls ssoLogout() to clear shared cookie.
 - src/components/Auth/ProtectedRoutes.js — respects isChecking state during bootstrap.
 - src/library/auth/interceptor.js — setAuthToken / getAuthToken for in-memory token.
 - src/App.js — registers /auth/sso-silent route.
 - src/hooks/check-session.ts (removed), src/hooks/useLocalStorage.js (removed) — obsolete persistence path.
 - config-overrides.js, tsconfig.json — minor build/TS adjustments.

 Verification

 1. pnpm install
 2. pnpm start with REACT_APP_GMW_URL set.
 3. Walk through each test-plan checkbox above against a staging GMW.
 4. Confirm no localStorage token key is written (DevTools → Application).

body:
## Summary

- Add CNPG operator to base-infra (`cnpg-system` namespace, Helm chart 0.28.0 / operator 1.29.0)
- Add `PostgresInstance` Pulumi `ComponentResource`: CNPG `Cluster` CRD + adapter `Secret`
- Add ADR-017 and `docs/howto/deploy-database.md` with restore runbook

## What gets deployed

```
base-infra stack
└── cnpg (Helm, cnpg-system)

app stack
└── PostgresInstance
    ├── Cluster CRD  → pod, PVC, services, CNPG-generated secret
    └── adapter Secret  → POSTGRES_DB / POSTGRES_USER / POSTGRES_PASSWORD / DATABASE_URL
```

## Key decisions

- **Image-agnostic**: no paradedb defaults in the component; callers declare `postgresUID/GID`, `sharedPreloadLibraries`, `postInitApplicationSQL` explicitly
- **`postInitApplicationSQL`**: pre-installs superuser-only extensions at bootstrap so the app user never needs superuser
- **Adapter secret**: re-maps CNPG's key names (`uri`, `dbname`, …) to canonical env var names
- **Explicit Helm release name `"cnpg"`**: keeps CRD ownership annotations stable across Pulumi re-runs
- **`longhorn-persistent`** for all database PVCs (daily R2 backup, 7-day retention)

## HA path

`instances: 1 → 3` — no other changes required.

body: The ticker is composed from three custom blocks (`mercantile/ticker-lead`, `mercantile/ticker-track`, `mercantile/cart-tab`) but all of its CSS lived in the theme's root `style.css` — including blanket descendant resets (`.mh-ticker p`, `.mh-ticker > *` with `!important`) that reached across block boundaries to fight `theme.json` from the wrong layer. This PR makes each block own its own presentation: chrome that maps to block supports moves to `block.json` with theme.json-tokenized defaults, the rest moves to per-block stylesheets. ## Changes Per-block style.css - Added `blocks/src//style.css` for ticker-lead, ticker-track, cart-tab. - Each `index.js` imports its style.css so wp-scripts extracts to `build//style-index.css`. - Each `block.json` declares `"style": "file:./style-index.css"` so `register_block_type()` enqueues conditionally — only on pages that render the block. Block supports for wrapper chrome - `ticker-lead` declares `color`, `spacing`, `typography` (with `__experimentalFontWeight`), and `__experimentalBorder` supports. - `cart-tab` declares the same supports minus typography. - `apply_block_supports()` emits the equivalent classes/inline styles via `get_block_wrapper_attributes()` — verified against the rendered HTML. - Per-block `style.css` files now contain only what supports can't express: flex layout, gap, flex-shrink, anchor primitives, pseudos, animations. Theme.json tokens for dark surfaces - Added two color presets: `text-on-ink` (`#ecebe4`) and `divider-on-ink` (`rgba(255, 255, 255, 0.12)`). - Block defaults reference the presets — `textColor: "text-on-ink"` (emits `has-text-on-ink-color`) and per-side border color via `var:preset|color|divider-on-ink` (style-engine syntax). - The rgba divider survives because preset values are emitted as CSS custom properties on `:root` inside a `

## Summary

Closes gaps **#3 (Target pre-flight semantics)** and **#4 (Parallel pre-flight timing)** from `docs/scratch/test-coverage-gap-analysis.md`.

- **TargetPreFlightTests (8 tests)** — exercise `InspectionLevel.Target` semantics, the `WithMaxInspectionLevel(None)` escape hatch that replaces the legacy `SkipTargetInspection`, and the three maintainer-required slicing cases:
  - memory-only input slices (no filesystem probes on excluded producers)
  - slice-aware external/internal reclassification (a producer outside the slice makes its output external)
  - metadata attribution accuracy — explicit `Flow.Merge` regression net asserting each step still names its **pre-merge** flow, never a phantom "merged" attribution
- **ParallelPreFlightTests (3 tests)** — pin the structural concurrency guarantee:
  - independent inputs overlap in wall-clock time under `maxDegreeOfParallelism > 1`
  - the sequential default produces strictly non-overlapping windows
  - every per-input error survives the concurrent fan-out / sequential merge

`PreFlightPipeline.Run` gains a `maxDegreeOfParallelism` parameter (default `1`, preserving the prior sequential behaviour). The parallel branch uses a bounded `SemaphoreSlim` gate so errors aggregate identically regardless of dispatch order; distinct external inputs are de-duplicated by label before dispatch.

author: robin831
body:
## Changes

- **Hearth 2.0 queue grouped by anvil and status** - The Hearth web UI queue panel now groups beads under each anvil and splits them into collapsed Ready / Unlabeled / In progress buckets so multi-anvil setups stay scannable. Each header shows its count even when collapsed; empty buckets and anvils are omitted. (Forge-smhw)

## Original Issue (feature): Hearth 2.0: group queue by anvil and status, collapsed by default

The QueuePane in Hearth 2.0 renders a flat list of all queue items across all anvils. With multiple anvils and dozens of beads, this is hard to scan. Group hierarchically and collapse each group by default.

## Grouping

Two-level grouping:

1. **Anvil** (top level). One section per anvil that has any items. Anvil header shows the anvil name and the total item count across its status buckets.
2. **Status bucket** (second level). Within each anvil, group items into:
    - `Ready` — items where the bead has the anvil's `auto_dispatch_tag` (e.g. `forgeReady`) AND no blocker. The poller will dispatch these.
    - `Unlabeled` — items where the bead is dispatchable by `bd ready` semantics but lacks the auto-dispatch tag. These are candidates for the operator to label, but the daemon won't pick them up automatically.
    - `In progress` — items linked to an active worker (running pipeline). Today the QueuePane doesn't show running beads alongside queue items; the bottom of the queue panel is the natural place for them so the operator sees the full state of an anvil in one section.

Order within each bucket: priority ascending (P0 first), then created_at descending — same as today's flat list.

## Collapsing

Anvil sections collapsed by default. Status buckets inside an anvil are collapsed by default too. Each header shows the count even when collapsed (e.g. "forge ▸ Ready (3)") so the operator can see at a glance where the action is without expanding.

Expand state lives in component state (no localStorage). Persisting across mounts of the page is fine; persisting across full reloads is not required.

If an anvil has zero items across all buckets, omit it entirely. Same for empty status buckets within an expanded anvil.

## Backend

Where the data comes from depends on what the backend already exposes:

- `QueueItem` (`internal/web/frontend/src/api.ts:5`) already has `anvil`, `status`, `labels`, `priority` — sufficient to derive Ready/Unlabeled buckets client-side.
- For `In progress`, the workers list is exposed elsewhere (look at how the WorkersPane fetches active workers). Either:
    - Join client-side: fetch both, render workers under each anvil as a third bucket using the existing worker→anvil mapping.
    - Add a new bucket type to the QueueItem response server-side. Cleaner but more code.

Recommend the client-side join — keeps the backend untouched. If that proves messy, switch to a server-side bucket field.

## i18n / strings

The Hearth 2.0 frontend is a small SPA that doesn't appear to use react-i18next today. Add the new strings in English directly. If an i18n harness is introduced later, retrofit then.

New strings:
- "Ready ({count})"
- "Unlabeled ({count})"
- "In progress ({count})"
- "No queued work for {anvil}" (empty-anvil fallback if you decide to render empty anvils)

## Tests

The frontend test setup uses Vitest. Add `QueuePane.test.tsx` (or extend if it exists) covering:
- Mixed items across anvils render under the right anvil section.
- Items inside an anvil bucket correctly into Ready / Unlabeled / In progress based on labels + worker state.
- All sections start collapsed; click expands.
- Empty bucket is omitted.

## Acceptance

- `npm run lint`, `npm run build`, `npm test` in `internal/web/frontend/` all pass.
- QueuePane shows one collapsed section per anvil; expanding shows three nested collapsed buckets.
- Counts on each header reflect contents.
- Dispatching / retrying / stopping a bead still works (existing actions and ConfirmModal flow unchanged).
- Changelog fragment in changelog.d/ (category: Changed).

## Non-goals

- Sortable column headers per bucket. Default sort is enough.
- Filtering by anvil or status from a toolbar — group expansion is the filter.
- Migrating away from the existing flat QueueItem API.
- Persisting expand state to localStorage.

## Reference

- `internal/web/frontend/src/components/QueuePane.tsx` — current flat list rendering. The 290-line file is the entire target surface.
- `internal/web/frontend/src/api.ts:5` — `QueueItem` shape.
- `internal/web/frontend/src/pages/` — the dashboard page that hosts QueuePane and WorkersPane; the workers fetch lives there and is the source for "In progress" mapping.
- `internal/poller/poller.go` — `auto_dispatch_tag` semantics, for the Ready vs Unlabeled distinction.

author: developertheexplorer
body:
## Summary

**PR 1b of 2** for the eval-collections backend foundation. Stacks on top of **PR 1a ([#30224](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/pull/30224))** which lands the data layer. This PR builds the orchestration layer: service, REST controller, runner integration, and multi-main collection cancellation.

PR 1b → PR 2 ([TRUST-80](https://linear.app/n8n/issue/TRUST-80) — AI insights + frontend list/setup) → PR 3 ([TRUST-81](https://linear.app/n8n/issue/TRUST-81) — compare view + telemetry rollout).

Every new endpoint is gated 404 behind the `eval_collections` PostHog rollout flag (introduced in PR 1a); the existing single-run flow stays byte-identical when off (`TestRunsController` and its public contract are untouched).

### What lands

- **`EvaluationCollectionService`** (`packages/cli/src/evaluation.ee/evaluation-collection.service.ts`)
  - `createCollection` validates evaluation-config / workflow-version / reused-run compatibility, rejects mismatches between `workflowVersionId` and `existingTestRunId.workflowVersionId`, rejects unpinned legacy runs, snapshots `WorkflowHistory` for "current draft" entries, and kicks off runs through `TestRunnerService.startTestRun()` with the new collection options.
  - `getEvalVersions` powers the wizard's version-picker: one bulk run lookup (no N+1), metadata-only column select (skips fat `nodes`/`connections` JSON), three-way source label (Published / Named / Autosaved), in-memory `★ best` / `⚠ low` annotation.
  - `deleteCollection` broadcasts `cancel-collection` for any active runs before deleting.

- **`EvaluationCollectionsController`** (`packages/cli/src/evaluation.ee/evaluation-collections.controller.ee.ts`) — 7 collection routes + `GET /eval-versions`. Every route carries a `@ProjectScope` decorator (reads = `workflow:read`, mutations = `workflow:update`, create = `workflow:execute` since it schedules executions). A route-metadata regression test asserts the expected scope per handler and fails if a future route is added without one.

- **Runner integration** (`packages/cli/src/evaluation.ee/test-runner/test-runner.service.ee.ts`)
  - `startTestRun()` takes an optional `options` arg for the collection context. When `workflowVersionId` is set, loads workflow JSON from `WorkflowHistory.findVersion()` instead of the live workflow so the run is pinned for future comparability.
  - `cancelCollection()` mirrors `cancelTestRun`'s multi-main fan-out: requestCancellation on every active run, local abort what this main owns, publish `cancel-collection` for foreign mains, DB-fallback for runs not held locally.

- **`WorkflowHistoryService.snapshotCurrent()`** — thin idempotent wrapper around `saveVersion`. Returns the existing version if a row already exists for the workflow's `versionId`; otherwise inserts a new snapshot with `authors: 'eval-snapshot'`.

- **Pubsub** — new `cancel-collection` event type registered in both `pubsub.event-map.ts` and `pubsub.types.ts`. The event type union in `@n8n/decorators` is extended accordingly.

- **Telemetry**
  - Extends the existing `Test run finished` event with `collection_id` + `is_part_of_collection`.
  - New events: `Eval collection created` (workflow_id, collection_id, evaluation_config_id, version_count, existing_run_count, new_run_count, dataset_id, user_id) and `Eval collection deleted` (workflow_id, collection_id, runs_unlinked, user_id). Both add `user_id` beyond what the spec's §10 table lists — flagging here for the telemetry stakeholder before rollout.

- **Tests** — 121 unit tests across 4 suites: `evaluation-collection.service.test.ts` (orchestration + validation + telemetry), `evaluation-collections.controller.test.ts` (flag gating + scope decorators), `workflow-history.service.test.ts` (snapshotCurrent idempotency), `test-runner.service.ee.test.ts` (collection context + cancelCollection multi-main).

### Size

857 non-test lines + 849 test lines = 1706 total against the PR 1a base.

### How to test

Backend-only PR — no UI yet. Smoke via curl with the `eval_collections` flag on for the user:

```bash
# List collections (empty)
curl -s -H "Cookie: $N8N" http://localhost:5678/rest/workflows/$WF_ID/eval-collections | jq

# Version picker
curl -s -H "Cookie: $N8N" "http://localhost:5678/rest/workflows/$WF_ID/eval-versions?evaluationConfigId=$CFG_ID" | jq

# Create — mixes one existing run with one new run on "current draft"
curl -X POST -H "Cookie: $N8N" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  http://localhost:5678/rest/workflows/$WF_ID/eval-collections \
  -d '{
    "name": "Manual smoke",
    "evaluationConfigId": "'"$CFG_ID"'",

author: jonathanmoregard
body:
## Problem

`research-agent-mcp.research(depth='fast')` failing with:

```
{"status":"error","error":"direct: exa call failed",
 "timings_ms":{"agent":36,"scan":0,"total":36}}
```

Root cause confirmed empirically: `api.exa.ai` sits behind Cloudflare. CF blocks Python stdlib `urllib`'s TLS / HTTP-2 fingerprint with `error code: 1010` ("browser signature banned") even when User-Agent is browser-shaped.

```
$ curl ... → 200
$ python3 -c 'urllib.request.urlopen(...)' → 403 + body 'error code: 1010'
```

Key was valid; fingerprint wasn't.

## Fix

curl_cffi is already in the dev container's `Dockerfile` (line 35) for this exact reason, but the MCP server's `_direct_exa` runs on the host and was still using stdlib urllib. Bring host-side parity:

- Add `curl-cffi>=0.7` to `pyproject.toml` dependencies.
- Rewrite `_direct_exa` to use `curl_cffi.requests.post(..., impersonate='chrome')` — replays Chrome's TLS cipher order, ALPN, H2 SETTINGS frame, header order. CF can't distinguish at the wire level.

Error opacity preserved (status code only on >=400, opaque on exception) — same scanner-bypass-prevention rationale.

## Verified

```
$ EXA_API_KEY=... uv run python3 -c 'from mcp_server.server import _direct_exa; print(_direct_exa("..."))'
ok= True
# Direct Exa Search
...
```

## Risk

Low. Single function rewrite, same external contract. Adds curl-cffi dep (~6MB with vendored libcurl-impersonate). Wheel exists for Python 3.12.
