author: amiya167
body:
Closes #11. Closes #12. Closes #14.

## Summary

Lands the three remaining Stage-1 follow-up domains in one PR (per umbrella #8) so the monolith reaches Stage-1 closing condition for Repo / Issues / MR / Wiki / Insight + the SSH cross-cutting item. Pipelines (#13) and GitHub OAuth (#15) stay separate; the CI workflow (#17) already shipped.

### Wiki (#11)
- Per-project Markdown wiki backed by a dedicated bare Git repo at `<RepoRoot>/<orgID>/<projectID>/wiki.git`, created lazily on the first `PUT`.
- All edits flow through libgit2 — two new wrapper entries `wg_repo_commit_file` and `wg_repo_delete_file` build a fresh in-memory index from the parent tree, swap the blob (or remove it), write the tree, and create a commit on `refs/heads/main`. Works for first-commit (no parent) and nested paths like `docs/usage.md`.
- REST under `/api/v1/orgs/{org}/projects/{proj}/wiki`: list pages, GET/PUT/DELETE single page, history. Markdown rendered with `yuin/goldmark` (GFM) and sanitized via `bluemonday.UGCPolicy()` — XSS payloads in user content end up stripped.

### Insights (#12)
- New `repo_commit_index` table populated asynchronously after every successful `receive-pack` (HTTP and SSH), with `ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` so re-pushes are idempotent. Walk is capped at 5000 commits per branch tip.
- Three GETs under `/api/v1/orgs/{org}/projects/{proj}/insights`:
  - `activity?since=30d` — per-day rollup driven by `issues`/`merge_requests` plus the new commit index.
  - `contributors?repo=<slug>&since=30d&limit=20` — SQL aggregation keyed on `LOWER(author_email)` so `BOB <BOB@X>` and `bob <bob@x>` collapse.
  - `languages?repo=<slug>&ref=<branch>` — libgit2 tree walk with extension-based language detection (Go, Rust, TS, Markdown, Dockerfile, ...). Capped at 10k blobs.

### SSH transport (#14)
- Embedded SSH server (`gliderlabs/ssh` + `golang.org/x/crypto/ssh`) on `:2222` by default. ed25519 host key auto-generated to `var/ssh/host_ed25519` (mode 0o600) on first boot, overridable via `WULING_SSH_HOST_KEY` (or disable the listener with `WULING_SSH_ENABLED=false`).
- New `user_ssh_keys` table; auth is a SHA256-fingerprint lookup against `ResolveSSHKeyByFingerprint`. PATs aren't involved — the private key *is* the credential.
- Sessions parse `git-upload-pack '<path>'` / `git-receive-pack '<path>'` themselves (no shell) and `exec.Command` directly. Path argument is restricted to `[A-Za-z0-9_/.-]` as defense in depth even though there's no shell expansion path.
- Authorization reuses `userstore.MemberRole` (write requires membership; read on public repos is open, identical to the HTTP smart-transport handler).
- Same post-push hooks as HTTP: `MarkRepoNotEmpty` plus `insights.IndexAsync`, so `git push` over SSH and over HTTPS keep insights consistent.

### Cross-cutting bits
- New REST surface for SSH key management under `/api/v1/auth/ssh-keys` (POST/GET/DELETE). Keys are parsed with `gossh.ParseAuthorizedKey` and re-serialised canonically so what's stored matches what gets handed to OpenSSH.
- `internal/git` (the libgit2 wrapper) grows `CommitFile`/`DeleteFile` plus a shared `buildCSignature` helper. cgo and `CGO_ENABLED=0` stub both compile.
- `internal/server.New` wires Wiki/Insights/SSH-keys handlers and passes the insights store to `githttp.Handler` as the `CommitIndexer`. Guarded against the Go nil-interface trap when insights are disabled.
- `cmd/wuling-api/main.go` boots the SSH listener alongside HTTP with shared error and shutdown plumbing.
- `api/openapi.yaml` extended with all 11 new paths and 8 new schemas. `info.description` moves Wiki / Insight from "Planned" to "Implemented" and notes the SSH listener.
- `dbtest.Reset` truncates `user_ssh_keys` and `repo_commit_index` so package-scoped tests stay isolated.

## Test plan

- [x] `go vet ./...` clean
- [x] `go build ./...` (cgo + libgit2) clean
- [x] `CGO_ENABLED=0 go build ./...` clean — stub path compiles
- [x] `go test ./...` green locally (with Docker for testcontainers). New coverage:
  - `internal/git/git_commit_test.go` — libgit2 round-trip for CommitFile (init + nested + update), DeleteFile, and the "not found" error path.
  - `internal/wikistore/store_test.go` — path validation (traversal, depth, control chars, suffix).
  - `internal/wikihttp/handler_test.go` — PUT/GET/LIST/HISTORY/DELETE with XSS sanitisation; membership 404.
  - `internal/insightstore/lang_test.go` + `store_test.go` — language detector + idempotent indexer + activity/contributors/languages aggregation.
  - `internal/sshd/hostkey_test.go` + `session_test.go` — generate/load round-trip, file mode, command parser including shell-metachar / control-char rejection.
  - `internal/userstore/sshkeys_test.go` — CRUD, fingerprint-uniqueness Conflict, cross-user 404, `TouchSSHKey`.
- [x] `bash -n scripts/smoke.sh` passes; smoke now exercises wiki PUT/GET/DELETE/history, insights (polled for the async index), and an end-to-end SSH `clone` + `push` (skips cleanly when the local sshd port is closed or openssh isn't installed).
- [ ] CI green on this PR.

## Out of scope (deliberately deferred)

- Pipelines (#13), GitHub OAuth (#15) — separate issues.
- Wiki PR/preview workflow (commit on a branch, open a wiki MR) — Stage 2.
- Linguist-grade language parity — extension-based is enough per #12.
- Per-key SSH scopes (read-only keys, deploy keys), anonymous SSH for public repos — Stage 2; HTTP remains the anonymous-public-read path.

author: stumason
body:
## Summary

Closes #159.

`env_vars list` responses previously included plaintext `value` (and `real_value` on the full projection), exposing secrets to any MCP client / LLM that called the tool. Now masked with `'***'` by default; callers opt in with `reveal: true` on the list action when they explicitly need the value (e.g. "what is FOO set to right now?").

Per @daniel-rudaev's option 1 in #159 and @StuMason's scope notes (masking at the boundary, both `EnvVarSummary` and `EnvironmentVariable` shapes, opt-in reveal on list, metadata untouched).

## Changes

- Added `MASKED_VALUE` sentinel + `maskEnvVar()` / `maskEnvVarSummary()` helpers in `coolify-client.ts`. Applied at the boundary on the list endpoints — masking doesn't run inside the projection step, so both summary and full projections share one default policy.
- `listApplicationEnvVars(uuid, { summary?, reveal? })` and `listServiceEnvVars(uuid, { reveal? })` — `reveal` defaults `false`.
- `env_vars` MCP tool: added `reveal: z.boolean().optional()` to the schema and plumbed through to both `list` branches. Updated tool description.
- `bulkEnvUpdate` was **already safe** — returns `BatchOperationResult` with `{ uuid, name, error? }` only, never echoed env var values. No code change there, noted in CHANGELOG for completeness.
- `diagnoseApplication` calls `listApplicationEnvVars` without options, so its env-var aggregator now consumes masked data — but the diagnostic only projects `key` / `is_buildtime` / `is_runtime` (never `value`), so user-visible output is identical.
- Tests:
  - 5 new tests covering masked default + reveal=true paths for both list methods, on both summary and full projections, plus `real_value` masking.
  - 2 existing tests rewritten — they asserted the leaked plaintext `value`. Those assertions were the bug surface.

## Breaking (behavioural)

Callers that relied on `value` being present in `env_vars` list responses must now pass `reveal: true`. This is documented as a Security entry in CHANGELOG.

## Test plan

- [x] `npm test` — 297/297 passing
- [x] `npm run lint` — clean
- [x] `npm run build` — clean
- [x] Client coverage: 98.79% lines, 86.74% branches
- [x] Both `reveal: true` and `reveal: false` paths exercised for codecov patch coverage

### Motivation
- Diagnose a large delay between the Firestore write resolving and the app receiving/recognizing the `onSnapshot` update for actions like `DRAW_CARD` on mobile.
- Determine whether the listener is being recreated frequently, whether local cache snapshots are being ignored, and whether the perf panel is correlating snapshots to actions correctly.
- Provide minimal, gated diagnostics (no DB writes, no gameplay changes) so the root cause can be observed in the field before proposing an optimistic UI.

### Description
- Add lifecycle instrumentation for the game document listener including listener instance ids and events (`created`, `unsubscribed`, `error`) and expose them via the perf system (`listenerEvents`) so listener churn can be observed at runtime. The listener now records `fromCache` and `hasPendingWrites` by calling `onSnapshot` with `includeMetadataChanges: true` and emits metadata for each snapshot. (`src/App.jsx`) 
- Add action markers and snapshot↔action correlation helpers (`getPerfGameCounts`, `getPerfActionMarker`, `doesPerfSnapshotReflectAction`) to better match snapshots to tracked actions such as `DRAW_CARD`, `CAST_SPELL`, `PLAY_LAND`, `COPY_STACK_ITEM`, and stack resolution actions without writing any extra data to Firestore. (`src/App.jsx`) 
- Improve snapshot recording to separate the timing of: first snapshot seen after a write, first snapshot that reflects the action, and first server-confirmed snapshot that reflects the action; store these per-action fields and expose them to the perf UI. (`recordPerfSnapshot` updates in `src/App.jsx`) 
- Update the Performance Debug panel to show the new timings, snapshot metadata (cache/pending status), whether local snapshots were ignored, last-log info, and recent listener lifecycle events so the delay’s nature is visible in the UI. (`src/App.jsx`)

🚨 Your current dependencies have known security vulnerabilities 🚨 This dependency update fixes known security vulnerabilities. Please see the details below and assess their impact carefully. We recommend to merge and deploy this as soon as possible!
Here is everything you need to know about this upgrade. Please take a good look at what changed and the test results before merging this pull request. ### What changed? #### ✳️ next (15.2.6 → 15.5.18) · [Repo](https://github.com/vercel/next.js)
Security Advisories 🚨

🚨 Next.js has a Middleware / Proxy bypass in App Router applications via segment-prefetch routes - Incomplete Fix Follow-Up

Impact

It was found that the fix addressing CVE-2026-44575 did not apply to middleware.ts with Turbopack. Refer to CVE-2026-44575 for further details.

References

  • CVE CVE-2026-44575

🚨 Next.js's Middleware / Proxy redirects can be cache-poisoned

Impact

Next.js uses the x-nextjs-data request header for internal data requests. On affected versions, an external client could send this header on a normal request to a path handled by middleware that returns a redirect.

When that happened, the middleware/proxy could treat the request as a data request and replace the standard Location redirect header with the internal x-nextjs-redirect header. Browsers do not follow x-nextjs-redirect, so the response became an unusable redirect for normal clients.

If the application was deployed behind a CDN or reverse proxy that caches 3xx responses without varying on this header, a single attacker request could poison the cached redirect response for the affected path. Subsequent visitors could then receive a cached redirect response without a Location header, causing a denial of service for that redirect path until the cache entry expired or was purged.

Affected scenarios

This affects applications that:

  • use middleware or proxy redirects
  • are deployed behind a caching CDN or reverse proxy
  • allow 3xx responses on those paths to be cached without differentiating internal data requests from normal requests

Fix

The fix stops trusting x-nextjs-data by itself for middleware redirect handling. A request is now treated as an internal data request only when it is validated as such by internal routing state, preserving legitimate data-request redirect behavior while preventing external header injection from changing normal redirect responses.

Workarounds

Before upgrading, users can reduce risk by:

  • configuring the CDN or reverse proxy to vary its cache key on x-nextjs-data for affected responses

🚨 Next.js vulnerable to cross-site scripting in App Router applications using CSP nonces

Impact

App Router applications that rely on CSP nonces can be vulnerable to stored cross-site scripting when deployed behind shared caches. In affected versions, malformed nonce values derived from request headers could be reflected into rendered HTML in an unsafe way, allowing an attacker to poison cached responses and cause script execution for later visitors.

Fix

We now reject or ignore malformed nonce values before they are embedded into HTML and apply stricter nonce sanitization so request-derived nonce data cannot break out of the intended attribute context.

Workarounds

If you cannot upgrade immediately, strip inbound Content-Security-Policy request headers from untrusted traffic.

🚨 Next.js vulnerable to cache poisoning via collisions in React Server Component cache-busting

Impact

React Server Component responses can be vulnerable to cache poisoning in deployments that rely on shared caches with insufficient response partitioning. In affected conditions, collisions in the _rsc cache-busting value can allow an attacker to poison cache entries so users receive the wrong response variant for a given URL.

Fix

We strengthened the _rsc cache-busting mechanism to make practical collisions significantly harder and to better separate response variants that should not share cache entries.

Workarounds

If you cannot upgrade immediately, ensure intermediary caches correctly honor Vary for RSC-related request headers, or disable shared caching for affected RSC responses until you can deploy a patched release.

🚨 Next.js has cross-site scripting in beforeInteractive scripts with untrusted input

Impact

Applications that use beforeInteractive scripts together with untrusted content can be vulnerable to cross-site scripting. In affected versions, serialized script content was not escaped safely before being embedded into the document, which could allow attacker-controlled input to break out of the intended script context and execute arbitrary JavaScript in a visitor's browser.

Fix

We now HTML-escape serialized beforeInteractive script content before embedding it into the page, preventing attacker-controlled content from breaking out of the inline script boundary.

Workarounds

If you cannot upgrade immediately, do not pass untrusted data into beforeInteractive scripts. If that pattern is unavoidable, sanitize or escape the content before embedding it.

🚨 Next.js vulnerable to Denial of Service via connection exhaustion in applications using Cache Components

Impact

Applications using Partial Prerendering through the Cache Components feature can be vulnerable to connection exhaustion through crafted POST requests to a server action. In affected configurations, a malicious request can trigger a request-body handling deadlock that leaves connections open for an extended period, consuming file descriptors and server capacity until legitimate users are denied service.

body:
Citations-side half of the schema simplification. Pairs with [SchemaSync PR #86](https://github.com/labki-org/SchemaSync/pull/86) which makes the matching changes on `Category:Publication`. Both should land before the next `discovery.approve` run.

## The three tagging axes on a publication entry

| BibTeX field | Wiki property | Cardinality | Source |
|---|---|---|---|
| `project=` | `Has project` | Usually one | Auto from LLM `suggested_project` |
| `paper_type=` | `Has paper type` *(new)* | One | Auto from LLM `paper_type`, Title Case |
| `keywords=` | `Has keyword` | Many, comma-sep | Manual from vocabulary.yaml during triage |

`Has publication type` (Journal Article / Preprint / Thesis) stays auto-derived from BibTeX entry type — orthogonal axis, no work.

## vocabulary.yaml + suggestion mechanism

New file at repo root. Single source of truth for the values that can appear in `project=` / `paper_type=` / `keywords=`. The LLM agent and human curator both read from it. When something needs a tag that isn't in the vocab, they append to `pending_suggestions:` at the bottom instead of inventing free-text terms inline. The curator reviews periodically and either promotes the entry to its target list or rejects it.

Starter keyword vocabulary: 20 tags covering imaging technique, behavior/cognition, recording context, brain regions, and cross-cutting tech (Wire-Free, Open-Source). Grows organically as we triage papers.

## Code changes

- **`discovery/approve.py`** — reads `suggested_project` (with `suggested_component` fallback for not-yet-migrated YAMLs), normalizes `paper_type` lowercase → Title Case via new `_canonical_paper_type`, joins `suggested_keywords` list → comma-sep string via new `_format_keywords`. Drops the component/technique override path.
- **`scripts/bib_to_wikitext.py`** — `FIELD_MAP` swap: drops `component`/`equipment`/`technique` → has_*; adds `paper_type` → `has_paper_type`.
- **`discovery_config.yaml`** — `wiki_component:` → `wiki_project:` on each tool entry (documentation field; no Python code reads it).
- **`.claude/commands/analyze-citation.md` and `run-discovery.md`** — agent prompts reference vocabulary.yaml, emit `suggested_project` and `suggested_keywords` from controlled vocab, escalate gaps via `pending_suggestions`.
- **README.md / discovery/README.md** — updated tables and docs.

## Data migration

Rename `suggested_component:` → `suggested_project:` in all 23 `pipeline/reviewed/` YAMLs (in-place, top-level field only — does not touch reasoning prose). The 58 `pipeline/rejected/` YAMLs are terminal and not migrated. `approve.py` keeps the legacy fallback so any not-yet-migrated YAML still works.

## Tests

112/112 pass (was 101 → 112; added 11 tests for the new helpers and legacy fallback).

## Order of operations

1. Land SchemaSync #86 first (so the wiki accepts `Has paper type`).
2. Land this PR.
3. Begin triage of the 16 high-confidence `pipeline/reviewed/` papers using the new vocab.
4. Run `python -m discovery.approve` to push approved entries into `references.bib`.

body:
## Summary

Closes the WASM unsafe-pointer audit finding (CRITICAL-1 in AUDIT_2026_05_06.md) by adding a second compile-time layout guard + runtime regression test on top of the existing size assertion.

The audit's recommended fix — \"replace unsafe pointer math with `pqc_dilithium` public API\" — is **not directly achievable**: `pqc_dilithium 0.2.0` exposes no constructor that takes raw SK bytes, and the lower-level `crypto_sign_signature(sig, msg, sk)` is only `pub use`'d under `#[cfg(dilithium_kat)]` (a build-time cfg, not a Cargo feature). This PR takes the alternative path: harden the layout-dependent unsafe block so any future upstream rewrite or compiler change that breaks the invariants trips the build before runtime, AND document the upgrade path explicitly for whenever audit H-13's pqc_dilithium pin gets revisited.

## What changes

`crates/evaporchain-crypto-wasm/src/lib.rs`:

### Two compile-time asserts, was one

| Const | Pins | Catches |
|---|---|---|
| `_ASSERT_KEYPAIR_SIZE` (was `_ASSERT_KEYPAIR_LAYOUT`) | `size_of::<Keypair>() == PK + SK` | future padding additions |
| `_ASSERT_KEYPAIR_PUBLIC_AT_ORIGIN` (NEW) | `offset_of!(Keypair, public) == 0` | future field reorder |

Together they imply `secret` is at offset `PUBLICKEYBYTES` — the only place it can be given (a) total size = PK + SK, (b) `public` at offset 0, (c) no padding (because both fields are `[u8; N]` arrays with alignment 1).

Cannot directly assert `offset_of!(Keypair, secret) == PK` because `secret` is a private field upstream (1.77+ privacy check fires). The two compile-time asserts here are sufficient via implication.

`_ASSERT_KEYPAIR_LAYOUT` alias preserved (`#[allow(dead_code)]`) so out-of-tree code referencing the old name still compiles.

### Docstrings rewritten

- `reconstruct_keypair` doc now lists **three** layout guards explicitly + a \"Why not call upstream `crypto_sign_signature` directly?\" section that captures the cfg-flag investigation so a future maintainer doesn't re-walk it.
- Both inline SAFETY comments updated to reference both assertion constants and explain the (a) + (b) implication chain.

### New runtime test

`keypair_layout_invariants_hold_at_runtime` triples the signal sources:

1. Compile-time: `_ASSERT_KEYPAIR_SIZE`
2. Compile-time: `_ASSERT_KEYPAIR_PUBLIC_AT_ORIGIN`
3. **Runtime: this test**, observing both invariants AND demonstrating empirically that the first `PUBLICKEYBYTES` bytes of a real `Keypair` equal its `public` field — pinning that the layout assumption is correct in practice, not just by spec.

## Why not upgrade pqc_dilithium?

`crates/evaporchain-crypto/Cargo.toml`:
> Pinned exact (=) per audit H-13 — `pqc_dilithium` upstream is unaudited.

A version bump is itself an audit-flagged action requiring re-audit of the upstream changes. The hardening here is the right tradeoff: preserve the audited pin, strengthen the gates around the unsafe block, and document the upgrade path explicitly for whenever H-13 gets revisited.

## Empirical validation (Mini 1)

```
$ cargo test --release  -p evaporchain-crypto-wasm  (worked via crate dir)
test result: ok. 12 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored

  test tests::keypair_layout_invariants_hold_at_runtime ... ok        ← NEW
  test tests::zeroizing_keypair_drop_zeroes_underlying_bytes ... ok
  test tests::zeroizing_keypair_drop_runs_on_panic_unwind ... ok
  test tests::reconstruct_round_trip_signs_and_verifies_with_original_pubkey ... ok
  test tests::keypair_layout_matches_byte_arrays ... ok
  test tests::zeroize_keypair_actually_zeros_bytes ... ok
  ... + 6 existing tests
```

All previous CRITICAL-1 hardening tests (ZeroizingKeypair Drop, panic-unwind safety, round-trip) continue to pass — no regression.

## Files

| File | Δ |

| `crates/evaporchain-crypto-wasm/src/lib.rs` | +146 / −25 |

- [x] `cargo test --release` in `crates/evaporchain-crypto-wasm/` — 12/12 pass on Mini 1

body:
## 🎯 Summary

Resolves the two open **CodeQL `actions/missing-workflow-permissions`** alerts surfaced after the repo went public. Both workflows now declare an explicit top-level `permissions:` block, scoped to the minimum each job needs.

| Workflow | Permission | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `ci.yml` | `contents: read` | Only checks out code and runs tests — no writes |
| `release.yml` | `contents: write` | GoReleaser creates the GitHub Release |

The repo-level default is already `read`, but CodeQL flags any workflow that doesn't make the contract explicit per file. Making it explicit also documents intent and prevents a future job from silently inheriting unwanted scopes.

## Summary
- Drops the double-v from gibson-bootstrap release tags. Next bootstrap release will tag as `gibson-bootstrap-v1.0.1` (clean), not `gibson-bootstrap-vv1.0.0`.
- Adds `workflow_dispatch` to the bootstrap image workflow so an operator can manually publish the tag-specific image when release-please's tag push doesn't fire downstream workflows (a GitHub Actions limitation when using the default `GITHUB_TOKEN`).

## Why
The 0.38.0 / gibson-bootstrap-1.0.0 release surfaced two issues:
- `tag-separator: "-v"` + release-please's automatic `v` prefix on versions produced `gibson-bootstrap-vv1.0.0`. The publish workflow's `tag_pattern: gibson-bootstrap-v(.*)` regex captured `v1.0.0` instead of `1.0.0` — yielding `:v1.0.0` as the image tag if the tag had fired the workflow at all.
- The tag did NOT fire the workflow. GitHub Actions intentionally suppresses `on: push: tags:` events for tags pushed by `GITHUB_TOKEN`. The image was only published as `:main` / `:latest` / `:sha-<sha>` from the push-to-main trigger.

## Test plan
- [x] Next bootstrap release-please run produces `gibson-bootstrap-vX.Y.Z`.
- [x] `gh workflow run gibson-bootstrap-image.yml -f ref=gibson-bootstrap-vv1.0.0` will publish `:v1.0.0` from the existing (double-v) tag, demonstrating the dispatch path.

## Summary
- 작업 대시보드에 **즐겨찾기(★)** 기능을 추가했습니다. 별 아이콘으로 즐겨찾기를 토글하면 해당 작업이 목록 가장 위에 고정됩니다. 상태는 `localStorage`(`task-manager.dashboard.favorites`)에 저장되어 백엔드 스키마 변경 없이 동작합니다.
- 작업 개수가 늘어 대시보드 창을 넘기면 **헤더/요약/빠른 추가 영역은 그대로 두고 작업 리스트만 스크롤**되도록 레이아웃을 flex 컬럼으로 정리했습니다 (`.dashboard-page`는 `height: 100vh; overflow: hidden`, `.dashboard-task-list`는 `flex: 1 1 auto; overflow-y: auto; min-height: 0`).
- 각 최상위 작업 행에 **"오늘 진행 기록"** 북마크 버튼을 노출했습니다. `dayTasks.createSnapshot` / `dayTasks.deleteSnapshot`을 그대로 이용하므로 `TaskDetail`의 동일 버튼과 동일하게 캘린더/히스토리에 흔적이 남습니다. 오늘 생성된 미완료/미폐기 최상위 작업에만 표시됩니다.

## Implementation notes
- 즐겨찾기는 표시용 정렬에만 사용하며, 원본 `dayTasks.tasks`의 순서는 건드리지 않습니다. 정렬은 `useMemo` 안에서 favored / rest 두 버킷으로 안정 정렬 형태로 처리합니다.
- 자식 작업에는 즐겨찾기/스냅샷 버튼을 노출하지 않아 행이 복잡해지지 않도록 했습니다.
- `is_snapshot` 행에서는 즐겨찾기/스냅샷을 숨겨, 이관된 진행 기록 행이 다시 기록을 만들지 않게 했습니다.

## Test plan
- [ ] `npm run verify:dashboard` 통과 (이미 로컬에서 확인)
- [ ] `npm run build` 통과 (이미 로컬에서 확인)

body:
## Summary

Pulls two DeepSeek-V4-related changes to `sparse_mlp.py` off the `aknezevic/ds4` branch into `main` so they can be reused outside the V4 bringup branch. Both are additive — main's existing `use_dense_matmul` and tile-padding code are preserved untouched.

### 1. SwiGLU clamp bound (`swiglu_limit`)

Cherry-picked from [`4e77a3c0d`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-xla/commit/4e77a3c0d) (sparse_mlp.py portion only).

Adds an optional `swiglu_limit` parameter through `_moe_activation`, `_sparse_expert_forward`, `_SparseForwardMixin.sparse_forward`, and `A2aSparseMLP.__init__`. When `swiglu_limit > 0` and `activation_type == ACTIVATION_DEEPSEEK`, gate is clamped to `max=swiglu_limit` and up to `[-swiglu_limit, swiglu_limit]` — matching `DeepSeek-V4-Flash Expert.forward` semantics.

Default `0.0` (no clamp) preserves existing behavior for all current callers.

`create_a2a_from_deepseek_v3_moe` reads `config.swiglu_limit` if present (also defaulting to `0.0`).

### 2. `*extra_args` / `**extra_kwargs` plumbing

Cherry-picked from [`a4e62f500`](https://github.com/tenstorrent/tt-xla/commit/a4e62f500) (sparse_mlp.py portion only).

Threads `*extra_args, **extra_kwargs` through:

- `A2aSparseMLP.forward` / `A2aSparseMLP._cpu_forward`
- `A2aSparseMLP`'s router call
- `DeepseekV3MoEToA2AAdapter.forward`
- `A2aSparseMLPWithSharedExperts.forward`

Needed for DeepSeek-V4-style MoE forwards that take positional tensor extras (e.g., `input_ids` alongside `hidden_states`). In `DeepseekV3MoEToA2AAdapter`, when 3D hidden_states are flattened to 2D, matching tensor extras with `ndim >= 2` are also `.flatten()`-ed so they line up — mirrors `DeepSeek V4 MoE.forward` behavior.

## What is NOT in this PR

The `aknezevic/ds4` branch carries more changes (V4 tests, weight loaders, kernel helpers, tt_forge_models / tt-mlir submodule bumps). Those are V4-bringup-specific and not in scope here.

## Test plan

- [ ] CI on `main` passes (no behavior change for existing callers — defaults preserve current paths)
- [ ] Verify on `aknezevic/ds4` that re-basing onto a `main` with this PR merged keeps the DS4 tests green (round-trip check)
- [ ] Spot-check that GPT-OSS / GLM-4 / DeepSeek V3 sparse MoE paths still work (they don't set `swiglu_limit` and don't pass extras → unchanged behavior)

The \`<details><summary>\` blocks at the bottom of the Google wizard (Connection details, View setup guide, OAuth client settings) were rendering with the browser default — plain text + a tiny native triangle. Easy to miss as clickable.

This PR adds card-style hover affordance via a \`details.disclosure\` class:

- Summary looks like a card (grey background, rounded border)
- Hover turns the border green and the caret too
- Caret is right-aligned and rotates 90° on open
- Body is wrapped in \`.disclosure-body\` with a matching border so open and closed look like one cohesive card

Targets \`.disclosure\` specifically so the inner wizard-step \`<details>\` elements (used by all 4 setup steps and reused inside the read-only \"View setup guide\" disclosure) keep their existing card styling untouched.

Four call sites wired to the new class + body wrapper:
- Connection details (state 2 + state 3)

- View setup guide (state 3)

author: depfu[bot]
body:
🚨 Your current dependencies have known security vulnerabilities 🚨 This dependency update fixes known security vulnerabilities. Please see the details below and assess their impact carefully. We recommend to merge and deploy this as soon as possible!
Here is everything you need to know about this upgrade. Please take a good look at what changed and the test results before merging this pull request. ### What changed? #### ✳️ eslint-config-next (15.1.3 → 15.5.18) Sorry, we couldn't find anything useful about this release. #### ✳️ next (15.1.3 → 15.5.18) · [Repo](https://github.com/vercel/next.js)
Security Advisories 🚨

🚨 Next.js Vulnerable to Denial of Service with Server Components

A vulnerability affects certain React Server Components packages for versions 19.x and frameworks that use the affected packages, including Next.js 13.x, 14.x, 15.x, and 16.x using the App Router. The issue is tracked upstream as CVE-2026-23870.

A specially crafted HTTP request can be sent to any App Router Server Function endpoint that, when deserialized, may trigger excessive CPU usage. This can result in denial of service in unpatched environments.

🚨 Next.js's Middleware / Proxy redirects can be cache-poisoned

Impact

Next.js uses the x-nextjs-data request header for internal data requests. On affected versions, an external client could send this header on a normal request to a path handled by middleware that returns a redirect.

When that happened, the middleware/proxy could treat the request as a data request and replace the standard Location redirect header with the internal x-nextjs-redirect header. Browsers do not follow x-nextjs-redirect, so the response became an unusable redirect for normal clients.

If the application was deployed behind a CDN or reverse proxy that caches 3xx responses without varying on this header, a single attacker request could poison the cached redirect response for the affected path. Subsequent visitors could then receive a cached redirect response without a Location header, causing a denial of service for that redirect path until the cache entry expired or was purged.

Affected scenarios

This affects applications that:

  • use middleware or proxy redirects
  • are deployed behind a caching CDN or reverse proxy
  • allow 3xx responses on those paths to be cached without differentiating internal data requests from normal requests

Fix

The fix stops trusting x-nextjs-data by itself for middleware redirect handling. A request is now treated as an internal data request only when it is validated as such by internal routing state, preserving legitimate data-request redirect behavior while preventing external header injection from changing normal redirect responses.

Workarounds

Before upgrading, users can reduce risk by:

  • configuring the CDN or reverse proxy to vary its cache key on x-nextjs-data for affected responses

🚨 Next.js vulnerable to cache poisoning via collisions in React Server Component cache-busting

Impact

React Server Component responses can be vulnerable to cache poisoning in deployments that rely on shared caches with insufficient response partitioning. In affected conditions, collisions in the _rsc cache-busting value can allow an attacker to poison cache entries so users receive the wrong response variant for a given URL.

Fix

We strengthened the _rsc cache-busting mechanism to make practical collisions significantly harder and to better separate response variants that should not share cache entries.

Workarounds

If you cannot upgrade immediately, ensure intermediary caches correctly honor Vary for RSC-related request headers, or disable shared caching for affected RSC responses until you can deploy a patched release.

🚨 Next.js vulnerable to cross-site scripting in App Router applications using CSP nonces

Impact

App Router applications that rely on CSP nonces can be vulnerable to stored cross-site scripting when deployed behind shared caches. In affected versions, malformed nonce values derived from request headers could be reflected into rendered HTML in an unsafe way, allowing an attacker to poison cached responses and cause script execution for later visitors.

Fix

We now reject or ignore malformed nonce values before they are embedded into HTML and apply stricter nonce sanitization so request-derived nonce data cannot break out of the intended attribute context.

Workarounds

If you cannot upgrade immediately, strip inbound Content-Security-Policy request headers from untrusted traffic.

🚨 Next.js has cross-site scripting in beforeInteractive scripts with untrusted input

Impact

Applications that use beforeInteractive scripts together with untrusted content can be vulnerable to cross-site scripting. In affected versions, serialized script content was not escaped safely before being embedded into the document, which could allow attacker-controlled input to break out of the intended script context and execute arbitrary JavaScript in a visitor's browser.

Fix

We now HTML-escape serialized beforeInteractive script content before embedding it into the page, preventing attacker-controlled content from breaking out of the inline script boundary.

Workarounds

If you cannot upgrade immediately, do not pass untrusted data into beforeInteractive scripts. If that pattern is unavoidable, sanitize or escape the content before embedding it.

🚨 Next.js vulnerable to Denial of Service via connection exhaustion in applications using Cache Components

Impact

Applications using Partial Prerendering through the Cache Components feature can be vulnerable to connection exhaustion through crafted POST requests to a server action. In affected configurations, a malicious request can trigger a request-body handling deadlock that leaves connections open for an extended period, consuming file descriptors and server capacity until legitimate users are denied service.

F

author: magi-9
body:
This pull request introduces several improvements and fixes across the product data import, API, and catalog data extraction pipeline. The major themes are: more precise handling and validation of product parameters, improved category visibility filtering based on a new `visible_categories.txt` file, and a refactor of catalog option extraction logic to use labeled key:value pairs mapped by exact product reference (SKU).

**Key changes:**

### Product parameter validation and API improvements

* Added robust validation for the `parameters` field in `ProductSerializer`, ensuring it is a valid JSON object and that any `details` subfield is also a JSON object. This is accompanied by new tests covering valid, invalid, and edge-case inputs for `parameters`. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-01b600f111f1c60f28f02e40fb14115674ee2da960f618c1f2170a18801ce526R135-R153) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-282a0e94e84de8db9799c55e50ee1d956fba818a0be9e5cb5f55a26e4c6eac17R38-R101)
* The product import logic now only marks products as visible if their category is active, using an explicit `is_active_from_categories` check.

### Category visibility and filtering

* Introduced a new `_load_allowed_categories()` utility that loads and normalizes allowed categories from `visible_categories.txt`. This is now used to filter categories in API endpoints and when calculating category counts, ensuring only permitted categories are exposed to non-admin users. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-367435e6e37aee13800c239455075f62b5175a80a082fce495fb4209281b670eR684-R715) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-367435e6e37aee13800c239455075f62b5175a80a082fce495fb4209281b670eR736-R746) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-367435e6e37aee13800c239455075f62b5175a80a082fce495fb4209281b670eR787-R803)
* Updated tests to patch `_load_allowed_categories` for predictable results and to ensure new filtering logic is covered. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-9c8b20c4d20e047b8a69613b410c67ee52cece4dd0081d5462e5d4229edae0a4R266) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-9c8b20c4d20e047b8a69613b410c67ee52cece4dd0081d5462e5d4229edae0a4R285) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-60885dfe7932c7160b37b7942348193803cccf7b158935747c72730d7eb87a67R5-R6) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-60885dfe7932c7160b37b7942348193803cccf7b158935747c72730d7eb87a67R254)

### Catalog option extraction and data pipeline refactor

* Refactored `extract_option_tokens` to output labeled key:value pairs (e.g., `αS:43º|GH(mm):0.3`) instead of ambiguous tokens, with special handling for different product types and sections. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-50e03fbe77940d1cecdad7688b9debc0d14ae4024531e4a9b8a9d9452d279569L206-R212) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-50e03fbe77940d1cecdad7688b9debc0d14ae4024531e4a9b8a9d9452d279569L217-R279)
* Updated catalog parsing to support DYNAMIC 3TIBASE sections and CH headers, and to map option tokens by exact reference SKU rather than by family code. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-50e03fbe77940d1cecdad7688b9debc0d14ae4024531e4a9b8a9d9452d279569L253-R321) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-50e03fbe77940d1cecdad7688b9debc0d14ae4024531e4a9b8a9d9452d279569L393-R463) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-50e03fbe77940d1cecdad7688b9debc0d14ae4024531e4a9b8a9d9452d279569L506-R566) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-50e03fbe77940d1cecdad7688b9debc0d14ae4024531e4a9b8a9d9452d279569L529-R589)
* Adjusted tests for catalog parsing and option extraction to match new output formats and mapping logic. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-2c16c831eb34c79d2956a0e661cc80ab2848da0e684871c2c9eb7a7639e0159aR50-R77) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-2c16c831eb34c79d2956a0e661cc80ab2848da0e684871c2c9eb7a7639e0159aL65-R112)

### Data source file changes

* Replaced usage of `categories.txt` with `visible_categories.txt` throughout the data pipeline and validation scripts, aligning with the new category filtering logic. [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-50e03fbe77940d1cecdad7688b9debc0d14ae4024531e4a9b8a9d9452d279569L27-R27) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-50e03fbe77940d1cecdad7688b9debc0d14ae4024531e4a9b8a9d9452d279569L560-R620) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-74c9ac70403ce5ccd87f1efdd160aa7d4ea3328f6766e39718bf5eedc17b9383L23-R23)

---

These changes collectively improve data integrity, ensure only intended product categories are exposed, and make catalog option data more structured and precise for downstream use.

author: darren0724
body:
Closes #25.

## Summary

Two parallel tracks landed together: **ETL stability** (the four roadmap acceptance criteria — e2e harness, chaos tests, throughput bench, DLQ inspection CLI) and **observability improvements** (structured per-feature log splits, async non-blocking tracing, per-iteration timing instrumentation, worker triage runbook). Plus a Task B refresh fix that the new timing logs surfaced.

---

## Stability deliverables

### Integration & chaos tests
- `etl-rs/crates/etl/tests/e2e_pipeline.rs` (192 lines) + `tests/common/mod.rs` (464 lines of testcontainers helpers): spins up Redis + Postgres + Neo4j and exercises `block ingest → stream publish → worker drain → graph + PG assertions`. Runs serial in CI (each test owns its Docker stack).
- `etl-rs/crates/etl/tests/chaos.rs` (503 lines, 4 scenarios): Redis frozen mid-loop, Postgres killed mid-transaction, Neo4j frozen mid-loop, poison-message → DLQ. Uses `docker pause` + `XPENDING` invariants to verify no data loss.

### Throughput bench + baseline
- `etl-rs/crates/etl/benches/ingest_throughput.rs`: 10k mock blocks through `ingest_block_range_pipelined` at `fetch_concurrency=16`, chunk size 100.
- Initial numbers in `etl-rs/bench/baseline.md`: **2,275 blocks/sec**, per-chunk p50/p95/p99 = 43 / 46 / 46 ms (WSL2 + Docker Desktop, 2026-04-29).
- CI bench job label-gated on `run-bench`.

### DLQ inspection CLI
- `ingest dlq {list,replay,drop} --stream <name> [--id <id> | --all]`. Operators can finally triage poison messages instead of having them silently accumulate. Three argument-parsing unit tests included.

---

## Observability deliverables

### Structured logging refactor
- New `etl::logging` module replaces the previous `etl::observability` tracing setup. Uses `tracing_appender::non_blocking` so the call site doesn't block on stdout I/O.
- Default `LOG_DIR=./logs` with auto-mkdir; container override via env. `compose/etl.yml` mounts `/var/log/chain-analysis` to host `./etl-rs/logs/` so operators don't need `docker exec`.
- Four daily-rotated sinks per binary:
  - `{log_dir}/{service}.log` — full log
  - `{log_dir}/{service}.error.log` — `WARN`+ only
  - `{log_dir}/{ingest,pipeline,sinks,consumers}/{service}.log` — per-feature splits (filtered by target prefix)

`tail -F logs/consumers/worker.log` to watch only stream-consumer activity; `logs/{service}.error.log` for triage.

### Per-iteration / per-call timing
- Worker tasks A/B/C each log per-iteration `iter` + `elapsed_ms`.
- `ingest_address_capped` logs `fetch_ms` / `write_ms` / `total_ms` per address.
- `run_neighborhood` logs per-hop `ingest_ms_total` / `peer_scan_ms_total` / `elapsed_ms` and a final `run done` summary. **Surfaced the deep-trace bottleneck immediately**: hop-1's sequential 20-peer loop is ~60s of an otherwise ~65s run.

### Operator SOP
- `docs/runbooks/worker-triage.md` (228 lines): how to read the new logs, which task each metric corresponds to, what to do when X.

---

## Bug fixes (caught by chaos tests)

- `fix(consumer): read pending entries before new ones in read_all_batches` — without this a worker that crashed mid-batch would silently leave its in-flight messages stuck in `XPENDING` forever. Caught by the Redis-pause chaos test asserting `XPENDING == 0` after recovery.
- `fix(consumer): surface unparseable batch as Err so DLQ ladder routes it` — the consumer was treating deserialize failure as an empty batch (silent success), so the retry → DLQ machinery never fired. Caught by the poison-message chaos test timing out with an empty DLQ.

## Task B refresh cap

- `refresh.rs` now caps each address at 500 txs via `REFRESH_TX_LIMIT_PER_ADDR` (default 500). Whales (Binance hot wallet, 1inch router, etc.) were timing out with "error decoding response body" after 60s of trying to pull the full history; the cap composes with per-address `effective_from_block` resume so refresh ticks incrementally advance instead of failing.
- `QueuedSpec::Addresses` gains optional `tx_limit` (serde-default None for backward compat with old queue payloads).

## CI

- `rust-etl` job runs unit + integration + chaos (`cargo test --workspace --tests -- --ignored --test-threads=1`).
- `rust-etl-bench` job is label-gated on `run-bench`.
- Release build + ingest/worker docker images verified.

## Test plan

- [x] CI green (rust-etl: unit + integration + release build)
- [x] `cargo test --workspace --tests -- --ignored --test-threads=1` runs all 4 chaos + 1 e2e tests locally
- [x] `cargo bench -p etl --bench ingest_throughput` reproduces baseline within ±30%
- [x] `target/release/ingest dlq list --stream ingested_txs` works against a running stack
- [x] Empirically verified: clicking Deep Trace produces `Picked up targeted entry task_id=Some(N)` log line with `tx_limit=Some(500)` and a final `run done elapsed_ms=…`
- [x] `tail -F etl-rs/logs/ingest/worker.log.<today>` shows per-feature timing entries; root `worker.log` still has the full stream

## Follow-ups

- Latest-first ingest with bidirectional `[L, R]` fill. ~2 hours including Alembic migration.
- Frontend `Fetch Transactions` route (`pipeline.py`) still uncapped — could reuse the 500 cap or get rewritten via the `[L, R]` follow-up.
- Hop-1 parallelization (`buffer_unordered`) would 3-4× deep trace, but requires `TransactionWriter` refactor; bundled with worker scaling.

## Summary

Adds the Wave 3 plan for the Agent Operating Model migration, per spec § 17.

Plan file: \`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-05-11-agent-operating-model-w3.md\`

## Scope of W3

- **Section A** — Skill auto-injection production wiring (Vertex embedding matcher + telemetry, 8 tasks).
- **Section B** — Executive migration with 10% shadow-traffic infrastructure (14 tasks; shadow router + agent file refactor + shadow rollout gate).
- **Section C** — Marketing migration following financial-pilot template (7 tasks).
- **Section D** — Data migration following financial-pilot template (7 tasks).
- **Section E** — Validation, lint, staging soak, PR (5 tasks).

Total: ~40 tasks. Estimated 3-4 weeks calendar time given parallelization (A and B.i in parallel; C and D in parallel after B.iii clears the shadow gate).

## Why this is its own PR

The plan is a strategy doc, not implementation. Keeping it separate from PR #25 (W1/W2 implementation + reviewer fixes) means:

1. The plan can be reviewed/iterated on a shorter loop than the implementation PR.
2. W3 execution can begin against an approved plan without waiting for the W1/W2 PR to land.
3. The implementation PR stays focused on shipped code, not future work.

## Acceptance

This PR ships only a planning document. The plan itself defines its acceptance criteria for the implementation PRs to follow.

- [ ] Reviewer reads § 1 (Goal + success criteria) and confirms it matches W3 intent from spec § 17.

body:
Clarifies an inaccurate docs description. Description was previously updated to say:

```
Setting `enable_parallel_replicas = 1` is needed when using this setting.
```

However this is an over-simplification.

Source: https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/blob/master/src/Interpreters/ClusterProxy/executeQuery.cpp (`isSuitableForInsertSelectWithParallelReplicas` function). introduced in https://github.com/ClickHouse/ClickHouse/pull/78041.

As I see it:

Source | Behavior
-- | --
Distributed table | Each shard executes the query locally. No additional settings required.
s3Cluster, gcsCluster, hdfsCluster | Files are distributed across replicas. No additional settings required.
ReplicatedMergeTree / SharedMergeTree | Uses parallel replicas to distribute the read. Requires enable_parallel_replicas = 1, allow_experimental_analyzer = 1, and cluster_for_parallel_replicas to be configured. Available from v25.4.

author: ekin-kahraman
body:
## Highlight: third real-data validation, all three premises hold

Real end-to-end run on **10x PBMC granulocyte-sorted 10k human multiome** (11,620 cells, 26,341 genes, 143,887 peaks) on top of the prior PBMC 3k (v0.3.9) and brain E18 5k (v0.3.10) runs. Apple M5, 10 cores, Python 3.13.9.

**Speed**: full `pipeline.run` end-to-end in **38.1 min wall**. GRN at `n_estimators=100` dominates 78% of wall (29.9 min). Topics K=15 in 5.3 min. cistarget plus enhancer-link plus eRegulons plus AUCell together in under 2 min.

**Memory**: peak RSS **5.39 GB** for the seven-stage pipeline at 11.6k cells. Scenicplus stack's reference number at comparable scale is reported above 40 GB.

**Linearity across three real datasets, same install, same hardware family**:

| Dataset | Cells | Peaks | Wall | Peak RSS | GRN edges | eRegulons |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| PBMC 3k (v0.3.9) | 2,767 | 81,156 | 7.5 min | 3.67 GB | 2,223,404 | 1,091 |
| Brain E18 5k (v0.3.10) | 4,770 | 172,193 | 13.8 min | 4.01 GB | 2,739,545 | 1,125 |
| PBMC granulocyte 10k (v0.4.3) | 11,620 | 143,887 | 38.1 min | 5.39 GB | 2,840,537 | 486 |

4.2x cell scale-up produces 5.1x wall (slope ~1.21x, slight cache-effect superlinearity in GRN) and 1.47x peak RSS (strongly sub-linear). GRN dominates wall at every scale.

**Biology**: 10 of 10 canonical PBMC plus granulocyte transcription factors recovered by name in the active regulon set. Myeloid axis SPI1, CEBPA, CEBPB, CEBPE, IRF8; lymphoid axis PAX5, EBF1, GATA3, TBX21, FOXP3. Strongest biology signal of any rustscenic real-data run on record; the brain E18 5k run recovered 9 of 9 cortex TFs.

**Installability**: single `pip install rustscenic[validation]` on Python 3.13 with the validation extras (igraph, leidenalg, scikit-learn) worked first try. The pyscenic plus arboreto plus pycisTopic reference stack this project replaces does not install on Python 3.10 through 3.13 in current envs without setuptools downgrades.

**v0.4.3 PipelineResult field contract verified on real data**, not just synthetic fixtures:
- `result.pruned_regulons_path is None` when `motif_annotations` not supplied (the bug fixed in this PR)
- `candidate_regulons_path` set, `regulon_source` non-empty, `n_regulons == n_candidate_regulons` on the no-pruning path

Artefact: `validation/multiome_pipeline_run_v0.4.3_pbmc_granulocyte_10k.json`. Schema compliant per the evidence policy in `memory/project_rustscenic.md` (dataset MD5s, command, version, hardware, time, memory, outputs, biology, caveats, supported claims, open gates).

---

## Cleanup PR contents

Bundles three code fixes, three doc softenings, and two release-infrastructure improvements that fell out of the post-v0.4.2 end-to-end audit. No new features.

### Code fixes
- **`pipeline.py`**: `pruned_regulons_path` is now `None` on the failed-pruning fallback path. Previously the pipeline wrote an empty-dict `pruned_regulons.json` and set the `PipelineResult` field to that path even when motif-annotation pruning removed every candidate. Test added asserting `result.pruned_regulons_path is None` and `pruned_regulons.json` absent on the fallback.
- **Six validation scripts**: drop `pd.NA` before `int(s.replace("Topic_", ""))` and set-construction. v0.4.2 changed zero-mass cells to surface as `NA` rather than being silently routed to `Topic_0`; the old pattern would have raised `AttributeError` on any real atlas hitting a degenerate cell. ARI comparators in `real_scatac`, `gensim`, and `atac_synthetic` now mask both sides of the comparison to the same cell subset.
- **CHANGELOG v0.4.2 sentinel string**: corrected from `"candidate_fallback"` to `"candidate_grn_top_targets_after_failed_pruning"` (the value the code actually emits on `PipelineResult.regulon_source`).

### Doc softenings
- AUCell wall-time rows and per-cell Pearson row in README now read `measured 2026-04 pre-v0.4.x; refresh deferred to v0.5` rather than `refresh tracked for v0.4.x`. v0.4.x has shipped without the refresh.
- Open-followups list moves the six-dataset benchmark sweep target from v0.4.x to v0.5+, adds NES to the follow-up roster, version-pins the 100k and 200k synthetic memory rows to `(measured v0.3.10, 2026-04-27)`.
- CHANGELOG v0.4.2 motif-pruning wording softened from "closes the regulon-pruning gap" to "addresses the regulon-pruning gap; validated on synthetic fixtures, real-data Kamath rerun under pruning tracked as a v0.4.3+ follow-up".
- README per-stage table now lists three real-data multiome runs (PBMC 3k, brain E18 5k, PBMC granulocyte 10k) alongside the synthetic 100k and 200k rows.

### Release infrastructure
- **`release.yml`**: PyPI publish now gates the GitHub release (was the reverse). `github-release` needs `publish-pypi.result` in {success, skipped} so tag pushes still produce a GH release when `vars.PYPI_TRUSTED_PUBLISHING != 'true'`. `always()` keeps the if-condition evaluated when the publish job is skipped. Avoids the failure mode where a successful tag push produced release notes referencing wheels that never reached PyPI.
- **`dependabot.yml`**: `rand` semver-major ignore added. Dependabot PR #67 (rand 0.8 to 0.10) fails CI with 23+ rustc errors because statrs 0.18 still depends on rand 0.8 and rand 0.10 renames `gen` to `random`, `gen_range` to `random_range`, `Rng` to `RngExt`, and moves `RngCore` to `rand_core`. Resume major bumps once statrs catches up.

### Version bump
`0.4.2 -> 0.4.3` across `pyproject.toml`, workspace `Cargo.toml`, README current-release line, `docs/what-rustscenic-is.md`, and the validation-report issue template.

## Test plan
- [x] `python -m pytest -x -q`: 186 passed, 1 skipped (no regression vs v0.4.2).
- [x] `cargo check --workspace`: green at 0.4.3.
- [x] `cargo clippy --workspace --exclude rustscenic-py --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- [x] `cargo test --workspace --exclude rustscenic-py`: 57 inline tests pass.
- [x] `python -m py_compile` on the four .py validation scripts: green.
- [x] Heredoc-extracted Python from the two .sh validation scripts: compiles.
- [x] `release.yml`, `dependabot.yml`, `validation_report.yml`: valid YAML.
- [x] Fresh-context code-reviewer audit of the branch diff: one finding caught (cross-tool ARI mask in `validate_topics_atac_synthetic.py:111`), fixed before commit; no remaining block-push or fix-before-tag findings.
- [x] **Real-data end-to-end on a third public multiome (PBMC granulocyte 10k)**: all 7 SCENIC+ stages non-empty, all 4 PipelineResult v0.4.3 field-contract checks pass, 10 of 10 canonical PBMC plus granulocyte TFs recovered. 38.1 min wall, 5.39 GB peak RSS.

## Follow-up after merge
1. Tag v0.4.3, release.yml triggers the PyPI plus GitHub release publish under the new ordering.
2. Open the separate NES feature PR for Fuaad's review (targeting v0.4.4).
3. Close dependabot PR #67 with a comment pointing at the new dependabot.yml ignore.

author: henrikfaul
body:
Two root causes blocked employees from saving their daily site/office:

1. RLS policies on enterprise_shift_assignments only allow owner/resourceAssistant to INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE — regular member-role users were silently blocked.
2. The shift_role_or_skill CHECK constraint (business_role IS NOT NULL OR skill_id IS NOT NULL) was always violated because upsertSiteAssignment never passed either field.

Fix: two SECURITY DEFINER RPCs (attendance_upsert_site_assignment, attendance_remove_site_assignment) that bypass RLS while verifying membership ownership server-side, populate business_role from the member profile (fallback 'employee'), and use an atomic ON CONFLICT upsert keyed on uq_shift_user_date. api.ts updated to call the RPCs instead of writing the table directly.

Test result: 133/133 pass. 0 TS errors. Build clean.

author: ibejesusprince-unpuzzle
body:
## Problem (regression in PR 30b)

After opening **Open responsibility** or **Open project** from the agenda task popup, pressing the browser Back button required **two presses** to reach the day-overlay:

- Press 1 — no visible change (URL stayed at `/responsibilities/:id` or `/projects/:id/edit`)
- Press 2 — returned to overlay

## Root cause

`clearPopup()` did `replaceState(overlay=)` followed by `pushState(/responsibilities/:id)`. The `replaceState` URL was **identical** to the prior history entry pushed when the overlay opened, so the history stack contained two adjacent duplicate entries. Back from the destination landed on the second duplicate (no visible change) before finally reaching the overlay.

## Fix

Replaced `clearPopup()` with `popPopupThen(next)`:

1. Calls `history.back()` to **truly pop** the popup history entry
2. Listens once for `popstate`
3. Then runs `next()` (which pushes the destination route)

No duplicate adjacent entries; single Back from `/responsibilities/:id` or `/projects/:id/edit` now returns to the day-overlay layer; a second Back unwinds to bare agenda.

## Files

- `client/src/hooks/use-agenda-url-state.ts` — `clearPopup` → `popPopupThen(next)`
- `client/src/pages/agenda.tsx` — destructures `popPopupThen`
- `client/src/components/agenda-task-view-modal.tsx` — `onNavigateAway` signature `() => void` → `(next: () => void) => void`; handlers call `onNavigateAway(() => navigate(path))`

## Verification (Playwright with instrumented history)

```
=== OPEN RESPONSIBILITY ===
[HIST] back()
[HIST] popstate → overlay=#/agenda
[HIST] pushState → overlay=#/responsibilities/28
=== BACK #1 ===
[HIST] popstate → overlay=#/agenda   (overlay visible)
=== BACK #2 ===
[HIST] popstate → #/agenda           (bare agenda)
```

Same pattern verified for the project flow (`/projects/10/edit`).

Type-check clean. Build clean.

author: erenari
body:
## Summary

Upgrade the bpffs pin watchdog from **warn-only** to **self-healing**. When the heartbeat tick observes a missing pin (operator \`rm\`, \`bpftool link detach\`, kernel-module reload, etc.), the watchdog re-issues \`bpf_link__pin()\` on the still-live userspace \`bpf_link*\`, restoring the bpffs entry in place.

**No kernel attach syscall is invoked** — the kernel link object survived the missing-pin window because userspace held an fd to it; only the bpffs path needs rewriting. This is the intended fail-safe semantics (link object stays alive while *any* ref holds it: bpffs ref or userspace fd ref), and it side-steps the integration-test gap that motivated deferring auto-reattach in the parent PR.

Closes the "auto re-attach intentionally deferred" follow-up from #144.

## What's in scope

- \`AEGIS_PIN_HEAL\` env var (default \`1\` whenever \`AEGIS_ENFORCE_PIN_LINKS=1\`); set to \`0\` to fall back to warn-only verify
- \`heal_pinned_hooks()\` in \`src/bpf_link_pin.cpp\` + counters in \`BpfState\` (\`pin_heal_{attempts,successes,failures}\`)
- Heartbeat in \`src/daemon_runtime.cpp\` dispatches to heal vs verify based on \`state.enable_pin_heal\`
- Each successful heal emits \`INFO Pin healed — bpffs entry restored\` with cumulative count → SIEM can alert on "heal rate non-zero" as drift detection
- Orphan-pin path (entry with \`link == nullptr\`) emits ERROR but does NOT count an attempt → stats remain a faithful measure of active heal effort
- 3 new GTests (\`HealPinnedHooks{ReportsZeroOnHealthy,ReportsMissingWhenLinkIsNull,LeavesHealthyEntriesUntouched}\`); 18/18 \`BpfLinkPin.*\` pass locally
- \`docs/HARDENING.md\` + \`docs/CHANGELOG.md\` updated

## Stacking note

This PR is **stacked on \#144** (\`feat/bpf-link-pin-watchdog\`). When #144 merges to \`main\`, GitHub will auto-rebase this PR's base. Merge order: #144 → this.

## Out of scope (deferred to follow-up PRs)

- Cold-start re-attach when daemon comes up to existing pins with no userspace \`bpf_link*\` handle (would need a full \`bpf_program__attach()\` + a kernel-equipped CI runner)
- Per-hook heal-failure cooldown / exponential backoff (current heartbeat retries every tick — correct behaviour without telemetry on permanent vs transient failures)
- Prometheus exposure of \`pin_heal_*\` counters (daemon doesn't yet expose its own HTTP metrics endpoint)

## Test plan

- [x] \`aegisbpf_test --gtest_filter='BpfLinkPin.*'\` — 18/18 pass locally
- [x] \`clang-format-18 --dry-run --Werror\` clean on all 6 modified files
- [x] Default-OFF when \`AEGIS_ENFORCE_PIN_LINKS\` not set — no behaviour change
- [ ] CI: lint, build, test, sanitizers green
- [ ] Manual on a real host: \`mount -t bpf bpf /sys/fs/bpf && AEGIS_ENFORCE_PIN_LINKS=1 systemctl restart aegisbpfd && rm /sys/fs/bpf/aegisbpf/handle_execve\` → next heartbeat should re-pin and log INFO

body:
🚨 Your current dependencies have known security vulnerabilities 🚨 This dependency update fixes known security vulnerabilities. Please see the details below and assess their impact carefully. We recommend to merge and deploy this as soon as possible!
Here is everything you need to know about this upgrade. Please take a good look at what changed and the test results before merging this pull request. ### What changed? #### ✳️ @​opentelemetry/sdk-node (0.33.0 → 0.217.0) · [Repo](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-js) · [Changelog](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-js/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)
Security Advisories 🚨

🚨 Prometheus exporter process crash via malformed HTTP request

Summary

A single malformed HTTP request crashes any Node.js process running the OpenTelemetry JS Prometheus exporter. The metrics endpoint (default 0.0.0.0:9464) has no error handling around URL parsing, so a request with an invalid URI causes an uncaught TypeError that terminates the process.

You are affected by this vulnerability if either of the following apply to your application:

  • you directly use @opentelemetry/exporter-prometheus in your code through its built-in server.
  • your OTEL_METRICS_EXPORTER environment variable includes prometheus AND
    • you use @opentelemetry/sdk-node
    • you use @opentelemetry/auto-instrumentations-node via --require @opentelemetry/auto-instrumentations-node/register/--import @opentelemetry/auto-instrumentations-node/register

Impact

Denial of service. Any application using the OpenTelemetry Prometheus exporter’s built-in server can be crashed by a single unauthenticated network packet sent to the metrics port. No authentication, special privileges, or prior access is required.

Remediation

Update to the fixed version

Update @opentelemetry/exporter-prometheus and @opentelemetry/sdk-node to version 0.217.0 or later.
Update @opentelemetry/auto-instrumentations-node to version 0.75.0 or later.

This release adds proper error handling around the URL constructor, returning an HTTP 400 response on parse failure rather than allowing the exception to propagate and crash the process.

npm install @opentelemetry/exporter-prometheus@latest

Do Not Expose the Endpoint to Untrusted Users

Important

The following mitigations reduce exposure but do not fully remediate the vulnerability. Any client that can reach the metrics endpoint - including your own Prometheus scraper host if compromised - could still trigger the crash. Updating to 0.217.0 is the recommended resolution.

If updating is not immediately feasible, restrict access to the metrics endpoint so that it is not reachable by untrusted or unauthenticated network clients. For example:

  • Bind to localhost only by setting the host option to 127.0.0.1 when configuring the PrometheusExporter, so the port is not exposed on public or shared network interfaces

  • Use a firewall or network policy to restrict access to port 9464 (or whichever port you have configured) to only trusted Prometheus scrape hosts

  • Place the endpoint behind a reverse proxy that filters or validates incoming requests before they reach the exporter

Details

In PrometheusExporter.ts, the _requestHandler calls new URL(request.url, this._baseUrl) without any error handling. Node's HTTP parser accepts absolute-form URIs (e.g. http://) for proxy compatibility, including malformed ones. When request.url is "http://", the URL constructor throws TypeError: Invalid URL. Since there is no try-catch in the handler, the exception propagates as an uncaught exception and crashes the process.

The Prometheus metrics endpoint is unauthenticated by design (Prometheus scrapes it) and binds to 0.0.0.0 by default, meaning it is reachable by any network client that can connect to the metrics port.

Proof of Concept

Start any Node.js application with the Prometheus exporter running on the default port 9464, then send a single raw TCP packet:

echo -ne 'GET http:// HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: localhost\r\n\r\n' | nc localhost 9464

The process crashes immediately with:

TypeError: Invalid URL
    at new URL (...)
    at PrometheusExporter._requestHandler (...)
#### ✳️ @​opentelemetry/api (1.2.0 → 1.9.1) · [Repo](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-js) · [Changelog](https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-js/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md)

author: lautaropetaccio
body:
## Why

The existing Playwright suite is mature for happy-path login flows, but several critical surfaces had **no e2e coverage**:

- `/auth/setup` (the new `SetupPage` registered at `src/main.tsx:88`) had zero tests, even though it's a real onboarding path.
- The production-default routing under `dapps-onboarding-to-explorer = true` was only *implicitly* exercised — no spec asserted the URL the user lands on after login.
- `eth_sendTransaction` requests in `RequestPage.tsx` branch three ways (NFT transfer, MANA transfer, generic fallback) and none of them were tested.
- OAuth callback edge cases, wallet runtime events (`accountsChanged`/`chainChanged`/`disconnect`), and cached-session corruption were uncovered.

A second, structural gap: every existing spec mocked the auth-server (`/v2/requests/**`). That meant **no test ever exercised real recover/outcome behaviour** — the dapp's HTTP contract with the auth-server was never validated end-to-end.

This PR fills both gaps in one branch.

## How

### 1. New helpers in `e2e/helpers/setup.ts`

| Helper | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `injectFullSession(context)` | Generates a real `viem` keypair per test and uses `@dcl/crypto`'s `Authenticator.initializeAuthChain` to produce a structurally valid `AuthIdentity`. Pre-populates `decentraland-connect-storage-key` and the SSO storage key so the dapp restores the session on first load. The ephemeral key is real, so any later `Authenticator.signPayload` produces a signature that passes server-side ECDSA verification. |
| `createAuthServerRequest({method, params, identity?})` | `POST https://auth-api.decentraland.zone/requests` to mint a real `requestId`. For `eth_sendTransaction` it includes the auth-chain (`SIGNER` + `ECDSA_EPHEMERAL`) in the request **body** (not headers — that was the discovery that unblocked these tests). |
| `captureWalletTransactions(context)` | Exposes `window.__e2eRecordTx` so the mock provider's `eth_sendTransaction` / `eth_sendRawTransaction` cases journal every submission into a Node-side array. Tests assert on it after clicking Allow. |
| `pollForOutcome(requestId)` | Polls `GET /requests/{id}` (the auth-server returns `204 No Content` while pending, `200` with `{sender, result}` once the dapp posts the outcome). Mirrors the pattern from `auth-e2e-tests` so behaviour is consistent. |
| `mockCatalystDeployRoute`, `mockNewsletterRoute`, `mockReferralRoute` | For the `SetupPage` deploy path, with body-capture for assertions. |

### 2. Three Playwright projects (`playwright.config.ts`)

| Project | Target | Mocks |
|---|---|---|
| `local` (default) | Local Vite preview on `localhost:5174` | Full HTTP mocking — auth-server, Catalyst, feature flags, Segment, Thirdweb |
| `real-auth` | `https://decentraland.zone/auth` + live `auth-api.decentraland.zone` | Wallet only; everything else is real |
| `real-oauth` | Same as `real-auth` + real Google OAuth | None — auto-skips without `E2E_GOOGLE_EMAIL` / `E2E_GOOGLE_PASSWORD` |

`webServer.timeout` was bumped from 30s to 180s (Vite cold start was timing out). `SKIP_WEBSERVER=1` env guard added so projects that target deployed dapps don't spin up a local server.

### 3. Mock provider extended (`e2e/fixtures/ethereum-provider.ts`)

`eth_sendTransaction` and `eth_sendRawTransaction` now:
1. Journal `{method, params, ts}` via `window.__e2eRecordTx` (no-op if not registered).
2. Return a deterministic fake hash (`0x` + `'ab'.repeat(32)`).

This means tests can verify the dapp's tx forwarding without actually broadcasting on Polygon — broadcasting would either cost real money or clutter the testnet.

### 4. Three-layer verification for request-types specs

Each `request-types-*` spec checks:

1. **Display** — does the dapp's decoded UI match the data we encoded? (e.g. MANA tip title contains `"5 MANA"` after decoding our `transfer(addr, 5e18)` payload.)
2. **Forwarding** — when the user clicks Allow/Confirm, are the tx params the dapp hands to the wallet **byte-equal** to what we POSTed to the auth-server? (`expect(txLog[0].params[0]).toMatchObject(txParams)`.)
3. **Outcome** — does the auth-server record the (stubbed) tx hash under the connected wallet's address? (`pollForOutcome` returns `{sender, result}`.)

Together these catch: decoder regressions, accidental tx mangling, missing outcome submission, wrong sender reporting, dropped recover calls.

## What's new

11 new spec files, 32 new tests:

| Spec | Project | Tests | Adds coverage for |
|---|---|---|---|
| `setup-flow.spec.ts` | local | 11 | `/auth/setup` validation, deploy, newsletter, referral, error UI |
| `feature-flag-onboarding-to-explorer.spec.ts` | local | 2 | URL routing under production-default flags |
| `wallet-runtime-events.spec.ts` | local | 3 | `accountsChanged` / `chainChanged` / `disconnect` mid-session |
| `otp-edge-cases.spec.ts` | local | 4 | Wrong OTP, send failure, paste-distribute, keyboard navigation |
| `cached-session-edge-cases.spec.ts` | local | 3 | Malformed connection JSON, expired identity, quota-exceeded `setItem` |
| `social-callback-edge-cases.spec.ts` | local | 3 | Direct `/callback` navigation, `server_error`, malformed state |
| `request-types-sign-message.spec.ts` | real-auth | 2 | `dcl_personal_sign` auto-sign + verification-code branches |
| `request-types-generic-transaction.spec.ts` | real-auth | 1 | `eth_sendTransaction` generic fallback view |
| `request-types-mana-donation.spec.ts` | real-auth | 1 | `eth_sendTransaction` decoded as MANA transfer |
| `request-types-nft-gift.spec.ts` | real-auth | 1 | `eth_sendTransaction` decoded as ERC721 transferFrom |
| `magic-google-real-oauth.spec.ts` | real-oauth | 1 | Real Magic + Google OAuth round-trip (nightly, auto-skips without env) |

## Trade-offs and gotchas

- **`real-auth` specs need the dapp deployment to be reachable.** They use `decentraland.zone/auth` and `auth-api.decentraland.zone`; CI should run them on a separate job that doesn't need the local Vite server.
- **Picking a `to` address matters.** Real DCL contract addresses (e.g. the canonical MANA token) live in `decentraland-transactions`' registry, which routes the dapp through the meta-tx path. The transaction specs deliberately use a clearly-random address (`0x1111...1111`) so the dapp takes the regular `eth_sendTransaction` path that our journal observes.
- **NFT view falls back to generic.** With an arbitrary `to`, the on-chain `tokenURI` lookup fails and `RequestPage` falls back from `WALLET_NFT_INTERACTION` to `WALLET_INTERACTION`. The spec accepts either terminal Allow CTA. To assert the actual NFT view, a real Decentraland Wearables contract on Amoy would be needed.
- **`local` regression.** All 26 new local-project tests + the 76 existing tests pass with `CI=true npx playwright test --project=local`.

## Test plan

- [ ] `CI=true npx playwright test --project=local --workers=1` passes (full local-project regression).
- [ ] `SKIP_WEBSERVER=1 npx playwright test --project=real-auth --workers=1` passes (5 tests against live dev auth-server).
- [ ] `SKIP_WEBSERVER=1 npx playwright test --project=real-oauth` auto-skips without env vars.
- [ ] Manual: set `E2E_GOOGLE_EMAIL` + `E2E_GOOGLE_PASSWORD` and run `--project=real-oauth` once headed to verify the OAuth flow renders correctly.
- [ ] Read through `e2e/README.md` for project descriptions, env-var requirements, and known caveats.

## Summary

- Gates `/home/saved-cards` (page + nav entry) behind a new `requiresCardCustomer` route meta.
- The flag is derived from already-loaded subscriptions (`paymentMethod === CARD` or `paymentProvider === BRAINTREE`) with `/webapi/2/history/payments/` as a fallback — so it flips immediately after a successful card purchase, no race with the payments endpoint.
- Fresh accounts (and accounts that only paid by crypto/paypal) are redirected to `/home/subscription`; the "Payment methods" tab is hidden in the account nav.

Motivation: someone has been creating throwaway accounts and using the add-card UI as a card-testing oracle. This raises the bar for that abuse. Backend enforcement on `/webapi/payment/btr/cards/` is still needed as a follow-up — the frontend block alone is bypassable by anyone hitting the endpoint directly.

- [x] `pnpm typecheck`

author: nanookclaw
body:
## Summary

Task registry maintenance now treats cron active-job liveness as non-authoritative until cron startup reconciliation exits. This prevents a pre-start maintenance sweep from marking persisted cron task records lost while the process-local active-job set is still empty after restart.

The change keeps the boundary narrow:

- `activeJobIds` starts non-authoritative after process boot
- `cron.start()` marks liveness reconciling at entry and authoritative in `finally`
- task maintenance preserves only mapped cron tasks while cron liveness is non-authoritative
- once cron start exits, missing active-job state is trusted again

This is AI-assisted.

## Proof

Real setup: local checkout of `openclaw/openclaw`, branch rebased onto `origin/main` at `435e1a74fa`.

Commands run after the rebase/conflict resolution:

```bash
git diff --check
node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p tsconfig.core.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/core.tsbuildinfo
pnpm exec vitest run src/cron/service/ops.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.config.ts
pnpm exec vitest run src/tasks/task-registry.maintenance.issue-60299.test.ts src/tasks/task-registry.test.ts --config test/vitest/vitest.config.ts
```

Observed result:

- `git diff --check`: passed
- core tsgo: passed
- `src/cron/service/ops.test.ts`: 13 passed
- `src/tasks/task-registry.maintenance.issue-60299.test.ts`: 21 passed
- `src/tasks/task-registry.test.ts`: 63 passed

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed:** Task registry maintenance should preserve mapped stale cron task records while cron active-job liveness is non-authoritative during startup, then resume marking missing mapped cron tasks `lost` after cron startup exits and liveness is authoritative.

**Real setup tested:** Local `openclaw/openclaw` checkout on the PR branch, using an isolated temporary state root under `/tmp/openclaw-pr-80707-proof-*` and the repository's TypeScript runtime via `node --import tsx`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
node --import tsx .artifacts/pr-80707-real-proof.mjs
```

The script seeds 10-minute-stale mapped cron task records with `runtime: cron` and `sourceId`, runs task maintenance once while cron active-job liveness is non-authoritative, then runs task maintenance again after liveness is marked authoritative.

**Evidence after fix:** Redacted terminal output from the isolated local state-dir run:

```json
{
  "stateRoot": "/tmp/openclaw-pr-80707-proof-s9f07s",
  "scenario": "mapped stale cron task maintenance across cron startup liveness authority",
  "staleAgeMs": 600000,
  "beforeStartupExit": {
    "livenessAuthoritative": false,
    "maintenance": {
      "reconciled": 0,
      "recovered": 0,
      "cleanupStamped": 0,
      "pruned": 0
    },
    "task": {
      "runtime": "cron",
      "sourceId": "proof-cron-before-startup-exit",
      "status": "running",
      "endedAtPresent": false
    }
  },
  "afterStartupExit": {
    "livenessAuthoritative": true,
    "maintenance": {
      "reconciled": 2,
      "recovered": 0,
      "cleanupStamped": 0,
      "pruned": 0
    },
    "task": {
      "runtime": "cron",
      "sourceId": "proof-cron-after-startup-exit",
      "status": "lost",
      "endedAtPresent": true,
      "error": "backing session missing"
    }
  }
}
```

**Observed result after fix:** The pre-start/non-authoritative maintenance pass left the stale mapped cron task `running` with `reconciled: 0`. The post-start/authoritative maintenance pass marked the stale mapped cron task `lost` with `error: "backing session missing"`.

**Not tested:** I did not run the full monorepo `pnpm build && pnpm check && pnpm test` locally.

This shows the fixed behavior: task maintenance does not mark a mapped stale cron task lost during the pre-start/non-authoritative window, and does mark mapped stale cron tasks lost after startup liveness becomes authoritative again.

Also ran a focused Codex review against the rebased diff; it reported no blocker. I did not run the full monorepo `pnpm build && pnpm check && pnpm test` locally.

author: aka-hogelog[bot]
body:
PR builds were stamped with `versionCode=1` because the tag-counted monotonic formula in `app/build.gradle.kts` only triggered when `RELEASE_VERSION` was set. As a result PR APKs uploaded to DeployGate shared the same versionCode and couldn't be installed as updates over each other.

## Changes

- `app/build.gradle.kts`: introduce `versionForCode` — `RELEASE_VERSION` if set (main/release builds), else `baseVersionName` when `PR_NUMBER` is set, else null (local). PR builds now go through the same `MAJOR*1_000_000 + MINOR*10_000 + PATCH*100 + commitsSinceTag` path as main builds. `versionName` logic is untouched, so PR APKs keep their `-pr-N-shortrev` suffix.
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml`: add `fetch-depth: 0` to the build job's checkout so `git describe --tags` and the commit count work (mirrors `main.yml` / `release.yml`).

Lint/test jobs intentionally keep their shallow checkout — they don't ship artifacts, and the `commitsSinceTag in 0..99` gate stays safe with `git rev-list --count HEAD = 1`.

author: ritzylab-dev
body:
## What this PR implements

Item 1 from the EmbedIQ work queue: MISRA-C:2012 CI enforcement.
Implements as specified in next_session.md — cppcheck wrapper, warning-only,
deviation rationale documented. No C code changes in this PR.

## Why this is sequenced here

Items 1, 3, and 8 have no dependencies in the work queue and can land in any
order. Item 1 is sequenced first because it directly unblocks the LF and
Golioth pitch conversations — the answer to 'what quality enforcement do you
have?' is now concrete and verifiable: MISRA-C:2012 scan runs on every PR,
deviations documented in docs/MISRA_COMPLIANCE.md.

## Tool choice rationale

cppcheck (open-source, GPL-3.0) is the industry-standard community MISRA
checker. It is not a certified tool. docs/MISRA_COMPLIANCE.md states this
explicitly. cppcheck runs as an external CI subprocess — its GPL-3.0 licence
applies only to the tool binary on the CI runner; no cppcheck source or
binary is linked into any EmbedIQ build artefact, so the framework's
Apache-2.0 licensing (R-04) is unaffected. For formal safety certification a
certified tool is required — that is a future upgrade path documented in the
compliance doc.

## Scan results at time of PR

- cppcheck version: Cppcheck 2.20.0 (Homebrew local; CI installs latest apt candidate on Ubuntu)
- Files scanned: 16 (.c files under core/src/, fbs/drivers/, fbs/services/, hal/posix/, osal/posix/)
- Total violations found: 0 MISRA rule violations; 90 [misra-config] analysis-incompleteness warnings
- Most frequent rules: N/A — no MISRA rule violations were emitted by the local invocation. The 90 config warnings are notes that cppcheck could not fully resolve macros/includes for some files; they do not represent MISRA rule defects. CI invocation can be tightened later by passing -I and -D flags through the script.

## How to verify

```
sudo apt-get install -y cppcheck    # or: brew install cppcheck (macOS)
python3 tools/ci/check_misra.py
```
Expected: exits 0, prints violation summary.

## Verification check

```
gh pr view <N> --json baseRefName -q .baseRefName
```
Must return: dev
