author: astralitics
body:
## Summary

Upgrades the project assistant from \"summarizer with stuffed context\" to **\"answers recall queries by querying the data.\"**

The v1 assistant could only see what we packed into the system prompt (project facts + recent specs / bills / invoices / activity). v2 gives it **read-only tools** over the full data graph: rooms, assets, materials, specs, bills, invoices, activity. \"What fridge in the kitchen?\" now actually works — v1 didn't have assets in the prompt at all.

## Tools (7, all project + org scoped, read-only)

- \`list_rooms\` — every room in the project
- \`list_assets\` — per-instance items (manufacturer, model, **serial**, install date, warranty)
- \`list_materials\` — per-batch items (manufacturer, product code, color, **lot number**, attic stock)
- \`list_specs\` — planning + procurement layer with lifecycle state
- \`list_bills\` — money the firm owes vendors, with computed \`overdue\` flag
- \`list_invoices\` — money clients owe the firm, with computed \`overdue\` flag
- \`list_activity\` — recent project-level audit log entries

## Mechanics

- **Multi-turn loop** in \`chat.send\`. Anthropic returns content blocks; if \`stop_reason === 'tool_use'\` we execute each \`tool_use\` block server-side, append \`tool_result\` blocks as a user message, call again. Bails after \`MAX_TOOL_ITERATIONS=6\` to bound cost.
- **Slim system prompt** (~500 tokens vs v1's ~3000) — project facts + a brief tool catalog. Deep data is pulled on demand.
- **Token accounting summed** across iterations — chat_messages row records the total per turn. \`audit_log\` payload includes \`toolsUsed: string[]\`.
- **Tool errors are recoverable** — a handler throw becomes a \`tool_result\` with \`is_error: true\`. The assistant decides how to handle it; the loop never crashes the whole turn.
- **Persistence stays simple** — only user message + final assistant text are persisted. Intermediate tool calls are implementation detail. Trade-off: re-asking triggers fresh tool calls. Simpler state.

## UI tweak

Pending state was a dimmed \"…\" bubble; now a **ThinkingBubble** that cycles \"Thinking… / Looking things up… / Cross-checking… / Putting it together…\" so the wait (which can be a few seconds with tool calls) doesn't feel dead.

## Test plan

- [ ] \`pnpm typecheck\` passes (all 4 packages).
- [ ] With \`ANTHROPIC_API_KEY\` set, open Assistant on a project that has data and ask:
  - [ ] \"What rooms are in this project?\" → calls \`list_rooms\`, answers concisely.
  - [ ] \"What fridge did we install in the kitchen?\" → calls \`list_rooms\` then \`list_assets\` filtered by the kitchen room.
  - [ ] \"Are any bills overdue?\" → calls \`list_bills\` with \`overdue_only: true\`.
  - [ ] \"What's the paint lot for the primary bath?\" → calls \`list_materials\` with room filter.
  - [ ] Confirm \`audit_log\` shows \`chat.turn\` row with \`toolsUsed\` array in the payload.
- [ ] Empty-state question (\"what fridge?\" on a project with no assets) returns a gracefully-worded \"no data\" answer, not a hallucination.

author: davisdelivery
body:
## Why

PR #12 fixed the deployment defect — schedule registration now works. But once we got the functions actually running, a deeper Phase 1 design flaw surfaced: each of the 6 multi-universe functions scans 4 universes sequentially with a 14-min budget per universe. Worst case is 56 min total. Netlify caps background functions at 15 min. So no function ever finished all 4 universes; russell2k alone could blow the cap and leave zero snapshots.

This is what Chad observed: "everything but catalyst scanned." Catalyst was just where the timeout hit loudest (4 providers per ticker + setup detection = russell2k alone is 12+ min). The other 6 also failed silently — /api/health showed all snapshots null after his manual runs.

## Fix

One function per `(board, universe)` pair. Each gets its own 15-min container, scans ONE universe, writes ONE snapshot, returns. Russell2k now has 15 minutes for itself instead of competing with sp500/ndx/dow for the same 15 minutes.

## New function layout (23 new + 1 unchanged = 24 scheduled functions)

| Board | New functions | Schedule |
|---|---|---|
| target-board | `scan-target-board-{sp500,ndx,dow,russell2k}` | `0,30 13-21 * * 1-5` |
| prophet | `scan-prophet-{largecap,russell,all}` | `0,30 13-21 * * 1-5` |
| williams | `scan-williams-{sp500,ndx,dow,russell2k}` | `0,30 13-21 * * 1-5` |
| catalyst | `scan-catalyst-{sp500,ndx,dow,russell2k}` | `0,30 13-21 * * 1-5` |
| insider | `scan-insider-{sp500,ndx,dow,russell2k}` | `30 21 * * 1-5` |
| lynch | `scan-lynch-{sp500,ndx,dow,russell2k}` | `0 22 * * 1-5` |
| earnings | `scan-earnings` *(unchanged — already single-universe, calendar-driven)* | `30 11,21 * * 1-5` |

## Deleted

- `scan-target-board.ts`, `scan-prophet.ts`, `scan-williams.ts`, `scan-catalyst.ts`, `scan-insider.ts`, `scan-lynch.ts`

## Per-universe file shape (~80 lines each)

```ts
import { schedule } from "@netlify/functions";
import { runCatalystScan, type CatalystUniverseKey } from "./shared/scan-catalyst";
import { writeSnapshot, FRESHNESS_BUDGETS_MS, type UniverseKey } from "./shared/snapshot-store";

const PER_SCAN_BUDGET_MS = 14 * 60_000;
const UNIVERSE: CatalystUniverseKey = "russell2k";
const STORE_KEY: UniverseKey = "russell2k";

export const handler = schedule("0,30 13-21 * * 1-5", async () => {
  const scan = await runCatalystScan({ universe: UNIVERSE, scanBudgetMs: PER_SCAN_BUDGET_MS, ... });
  const { snapshotId } = await writeSnapshot("catalyst", STORE_KEY, { ... });
  return { statusCode: 200, body: JSON.stringify({ ok: true, ..., picks: count }) };
});
```

Shared scan runners (`shared/scan-target.ts`, `shared/scan-prophet.ts`, etc.) are unchanged — only the per-board scheduled wrappers were split.

## Concurrency consideration

For each "every 30 min" board, 4 universes now fire concurrently every half-hour. That is 16 simultaneous function containers across the 4 hot boards. Netlify free-tier concurrency cap is ~125 — comfortably under. Each function maintains its own internal `concurrency: 7-10` against Polygon/Finnhub/Quiver, identical to before; total API pressure per board is the same since the same work is done, just in parallel containers instead of sequential within one container.

## Pass2Max preservation for target-board

Original `PASS2_MAX_BY_UNIVERSE` map kept inline per file (sp500=100, ndx=75, dow=30, russell2k=200) — no shared map needed since each function is single-universe.

## Verification

- `npx tsc --noEmit` clean
- `npm test` → **290 passing**
- `npm run build` → clean

## Post-merge plan

1. Wait for Netlify deploy (~2-3 min)
2. Verify all 24 scan-* functions appear in `/api/v1/sites/.../functions` with non-null schedules
3. Manually invoke all 24 to seed initial snapshots (cron next fires at the next :00 or :30 ET market-hours slot)
4. Verify `/api/health` flips from all-null to all-populated within ~15 min
5. Verify each board endpoint serves `source: snapshot` instead of `source: fallback-partial`
6. Phase 4b unblocked (it reads `backtestRuns/`, not snapshots, so was unblocked anyway — but boards now functional)

- Ensure the game canvas scales and fills the window/screen correctly when the player changes display settings so the view is not cropped.

author: teravinointelligence
body:
## Resumen

Nueva pantalla **`/restock/consolidables`** (admin) que agrupa los pedidos de restock aprobados **por proveedor** y permite generar **una sola OC** con la suma de unidades pedidas por todos los vendedores.

### Ejemplo del spec
Emmanuel pide 12 Fluxus Naranja + Felix pide 24 Fluxus Naranja → una sola OC a Discográfica Vinícola por 36, con ambos restocks marcados como `convertida_oc` al crearse.

### Cómo funciona
- `/restock/consolidables` lista los `restock_requests` en status `aprobada`, agrupa los `restock_request_items` por `supplier` (snapshot), y por cada proveedor muestra: tabla de productos con cantidad total agregada (suma de `quantity_approved`, fallback `quantity_requested`) y origen por vendedor/folio.
- Botón **"Generar OC consolidada"** → `/transito/nueva?from=req1,req2&supplier=X` con líneas precargadas.
- `PurchaseOrderForm` ahora acepta `initialSupplier` / `initialLines` para precarga.
- En el formulario, Sabrina ajusta cantidades/costos/destino y crea la OC; al guardar, los restocks origen pasan a `convertida_oc` (ya existía).
- Acceso desde `/restock`: nuevo botón "Consolidables por proveedor" visible solo para admin.

## Test plan

- [ ] Como admin, aprueba 2 restocks de vendedores distintos que incluyan el mismo producto del mismo proveedor → `/restock/consolidables` muestra la suma agregada.
- [ ] Click "Generar OC consolidada" → `/transito/nueva` precargado con proveedor y líneas; ajustar costos; crear OC → los 2 restocks origen quedan `convertida_oc`.
- [ ] Productos sin proveedor caen en grupo "Sin proveedor" (sin botón de OC).

author: zaidbuilds
body:
💡 **What:**
Implemented a `threading.local()` cache to lazily initialize the `pyttsx3` engine inside the `_pyttsx3_fallback` function. Removed the `engine.stop()` call after playback, and added a defensive wrapper to reset the thread-local engine cache if a runtime error occurs (e.g., from an interrupted or broken engine state).

🎯 **Why:**
The previous implementation called `pyttsx3.init('sapi5')` on *every single speech request* that used the fallback engine. Because Windows SAPI5 uses COM objects, initializing the engine is exceptionally slow and creates a massive latency bottleneck before any audio begins. Furthermore, Windows COM objects are strictly apartment-threaded. We cannot cache the engine globally because calling it from multiple threads raises `pywintypes.com_error`. By caching it per-thread, we satisfy SAPI5's threading requirements while completely eliminating the initialization latency on all subsequent TTS requests for a given thread.

📊 **Impact:**
Massive latency reduction for offline/fallback TTS. The initial speech request per thread retains the standard engine load time, but all subsequent responses are effectively instant, bypassing the expensive COM initialization step.

🔬 **Measurement:**
Run Jarvis with no network connection or without `edge_tts` installed to force the `pyttsx3` fallback. Time the latency from command issuance to the first audio playback across multiple consecutive offline commands. The first will have normal latency, while subsequent commands will be nearly instantaneous.

author: thiagotigaz
body:
## Summary

Two parts:

### \`@mergecrew/config-yaml\`

- New \`safeParseMergecrewYaml(source)\` — non-throwing variant of \`parseMergecrewYaml\` that returns either \`{ ok: true, parsed }\` or \`{ ok: false, issues: [...] }\`. Each issue carries \`message\`, \`line\` (1-indexed, derived via \`LineCounter\` for YAML errors and via \`doc.getIn(...)\` for Zod issues), \`path\` (dotted), and \`kind\` (\`yaml\` | \`schema\`). This lets editors surface inline markers without a server round trip.

### Lifecycle editor (apps/web)

- The source tab used to be a read-only \`<pre>\`. It's now a \`SourceYamlEditor\` client component with:
  - Textarea bound to the YAML string.
  - Debounced revalidation (200ms) using the new \`safeParseMergecrewYaml\`.
  - Issue list with click-to-jump: each issue's "L42" button focuses the textarea and selects the failing line.
  - Save button disabled while issues exist or the file is empty.
- New \`upsertLifecycleYamlAction\` calling the existing \`PUT /v1/.../lifecycle\` endpoint. Server-side validation is unchanged and acts as the second wall on save.
- \`apps/web\` picks up \`@mergecrew/config-yaml\` as a workspace dep so the same parser implementation runs in both layers.

Closes #270.

## Test plan

- [x] \`pnpm --filter @mergecrew/config-yaml --filter @mergecrew/web typecheck\` clean.
- [x] \`pnpm --filter @mergecrew/web build\` succeeds.
- [ ] Manual: edit \`mergecrew.yaml\` in the source tab; introducing a YAML syntax error or a bad enum value disables Save and lists the issue with a line number that resolves correctly when clicked.

author: esk3nder
body:
## Summary

Two ship-blocker bugs in `runCheckpoint`, both still live on `main` after the recent merges:

### Bug 1 — `git add -A` bundles unrelated dirty work (`checkpoint.ts:174`)
`commitInRepo` runs `git add -A`, which stages every dirty file in the repo, not just the ISA. Combined with `--no-verify`, this also bypasses pre-commit secret scans on accidentally-staged files (`.env`, credentials, scratch notes). The commit subject names the ISC; the diff is whatever happened to be pending.

### Bug 2 — sidecar idempotency lie (`checkpoint.ts:299`)
`committedIds.push(isc.id)` runs unconditionally after the inner `for repo of allowlist` loop, regardless of whether any repo actually committed:
- Empty allowlist → sidecar records ISC as committed → `newlyCompletedISCs` filters it out forever after.
- All repos missing or `commitInRepo` returning null → same silent loss.

## Fix

- `commitInRepo` now takes the ISA path and runs `git add -- <isa>` — staging is scoped to the file we actually intended to commit.
- `runCheckpoint` gates each repo with `isPathInside(repo, isa)`; repos that don't contain the ISA are skipped with a stderr line.
- `committedIds.push` now only fires when at least one repo successfully committed (the multi-repo "at-least-one-success" T1.2 rule).
- The cross-repo "snapshot pending work in an unrelated repo with an ISC subject" semantic is gone — that needs explicit design, not the auto-commit default.

## Test plan

- [x] New tests: `isPathInside` boundaries (equal, child, trailing slash, siblings, ancestor-as-child, prefix-not-path)
- [x] New tests: ≥1 repo commits + others skipped → ISC IS recorded (partial-success)
- [x] New tests: 0 repos commit (ISA outside all) → ISC NOT recorded (retry-able)
- [x] New tests: `commitInRepo` returns null for every repo → ISC NOT recorded
- [x] `bun test test/algorithm/isa/checkpoint.test.ts`: **46/46**

## Severity

**High** — silent secret-scan bypass + permanent commit data loss via sidecar dedup. Recommend high priority.

author: akarras
body:
## Summary

Batch of five small bug fixes surfaced by a refactor audit. Each is independent.

- **`get_multiple_listings_for_worlds_hq_sensitive` silently ignored `hq` and `limit`** — the function accepted both params but called `get_listings_for_world` which applies neither. `analyzer_service.rs:301` passes `hq: key.hq` expecting HQ filtering. Replaced the inner call with a direct query that filters on HQ, orders by price ASC, and applies the limit.
- **Local `analyze_sales` in `fc_crafting_analyzer.rs` ignored outlier filtering** — shadowed the canonical `analysis::analyze_sales` and silently used unfiltered averages. Deleted the duplicate, use the shared function with `filter_outliers=false` (this analyzer doesn't currently expose the toggle).
- **`character_search` could panic on an unknown Lodestone world name** — `unwrap_or_else(|| panic!(\"World {} not found\"))` inside a `flat_map` in a request handler. Returns `None` to skip unknown worlds instead.
- **`venture_analyzer` `venture_cost_gil = 0` placeholder** — misleading subtraction since ventures cost coins, not gil. Removed the no-op math and added a comment clarifying the result is gross revenue.
- **`recipe_analyzer` debug logs** — removed four `leptos::logging::log!` calls left in the sales-fetch resource.

Also includes a `cargo fmt` pass on `ultros-db/src/lists.rs` that was already failing on main (likely from a recent merge that bypassed the fmt gate). That's needed for `check_ci.sh` to pass on this branch.

## Test plan

- [x] `./check_ci.sh` passes (fmt + clippy on all targets)
- [ ] Manual: load the FC Crafting analyzer and verify daily-sales/avg-price numbers still render
- [ ] Manual: load the Venture analyzer and verify the "profit" column matches `market_price * quantity`
- [ ] Manual: trigger character search with a real Lodestone character to confirm results still come back

body:
Treasure Egg vouchers can be created and banked into `eggRewardInventory`, but there was no debug UI to inspect or open them. This adds a dev-only path to visually test voucher → canonical creature collection flow through the existing egg opening service.

- **Debug panel inventory**
  - Adds a dev-mode “Treasure Eggs” section to the Island Run debug panel.
  - Displays voucher id, egg tier, target island, rarity roll, status, and opened creature id.

- **Canonical opening action**
  - Adds an `Open Egg` button for unopened vouchers.
  - Routes opening through the existing `openEggRewardInventoryEntry(...)` service.
  - Refreshes the board’s canonical runtime state from the returned record.

```tsx
const result = await openEggRewardInventoryEntry({
  session,
  client,
  eggRewardId,
  triggerSource: 'dev_treasure_eggs_debug_panel_open',
});
```

- **Scope constraints**
  - Dev/debug only.
  - No production UI, travel wiring, `localStorage`, hatchery mutation, or legacy `LuckyRollBoard` changes.
